title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄序
嘉靖戊午秋湖廣復當鄉試
巡按監察御史吳百朋舉行
如
制秉公肅度務脩成法而加飭焉
先是巡按御史黃季瑞招致
四方文學至是咸集乃以學
===
詩與教授蔣三近司考試學
正余兆陽教諭黃驊顧仕吳
鑄朱塗陳夢雷鍾道譚文通
同考試提調屬左布政使傅
鎮右布政使谷嶠監試屬按
察使俞憲副使章士元一切
簾內外擇可者然後授事乃
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄序

嘉靖戊午秋，湖廣復當鄉試。巡按監察御史吳百朋舉行如制，秉公肅度，務脩成法而加飭焉。先是，巡按御史黃季瑞招致四方文學，至是咸集。乃以學詩與教授蔣三近司考試，學正余兆陽、教諭黃驊、顧仕、吳鑄、朱塗、陳夢雷、鍾道、譚文通同考試。提調屬左布政使傅鎮、右布政使谷嶠，監試屬按察使俞憲、副使章士元。一切簾內外，擇可者然後授事，乃
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the wuwu year of the Jiajing reign (1558), Huguang was again due to hold its Provincial Examination. Wu Baipeng, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector, conducted it according to the prescribed regulations. Maintaining impartiality and strict standards, he strove to uphold established procedures and further tighten their observance. Previously, Huang Jirui, the preceding Regional Inspector, had invited men of literary learning from all quarters; by this time they had all assembled. Xueshi 學詩 and Professor Jiang Sanjin were appointed Examiners. Instructor Yu Zhaoyang and Instructors Huang Hua, Gu Shi, Wu Zhu, Zhu Tu, Chen Menglei, Zhong Dao, and Tan Wentong served as Associate Examiners. The duties of Proctor were entrusted to Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Fu Zhen and Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Gu Jiao; supervision of the examination was entrusted to Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Yu Xian and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhang Shiyuan. For every duty, both inside and outside the examination curtain, suitable men were selected before responsibilities were assigned. Then …

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
合提學副使張天復與先劉
起宗所簡士三千三百人三
試之得九十人錄其名氏幷
文之式者以
獻學詩從諸執事後縱觀楚髦瑰
特振振濟濟有不可盡紀者
竊惟江漢之麗于王服也任
===
物作貢如元龜包茅之微猶
足以待邦之大事自古志之
矧斯人文涵濡
道化其所遘會尤不偶然者乎
昔
睿宗獻皇帝肇基于郢
知天守道
punctuated:
合提學副使張天復與先劉起宗所簡士三千三百人，三試之，得九十人，錄其名氏幷文之式者以獻。學詩從諸執事後，縱觀楚髦，瑰特振振，濟濟有不可盡紀者。
竊惟江漢之麗于王服也，任物作貢，如元龜、包茅之微，猶足以待邦之大事，自古志之。矧斯人文涵濡道化，其所遘會尤不偶然者乎？昔睿宗獻皇帝肇基于郢，知天守道，
translation_en:
…bringing together the 3,300 candidates selected by Zhang Tianfu, the Education Intendant and Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and his predecessor Liu Qizong, they examined them in three sessions and selected ninety. They recorded their names, together with those compositions that could serve as models, for presentation to the throne. I, Xueshi, following behind the officials conducting the examination, surveyed the outstanding scholars of Chu: extraordinary in talent, flourishing and numerous, they possessed qualities beyond exhaustive description.
I humbly reflect that, since the lands of the Jiang and Han rivers came under royal dominion, they have furnished tribute according to their produce. Even such modest offerings as great tortoises and bundled thatching grass sufficed to serve the great affairs of the state; this has been recorded since antiquity. How much more is this true of these cultivated men, steeped in the transforming influence of the Way! Surely the occasion they have encountered is especially far from accidental? Formerly, Emperor Ruizong Xian established his foundation at Ying, comprehending Heaven and holding fast to the Way…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
含靈篤慶誕毓
皇上
神聖繼天於昭
大統夫五百年而王者興其間有
命世者多士之生應
皇上之會此其效也棫樸之雅曰
倬彼雲漢爲章于天周王壽
===
考遐不作人思齊曰古之人
無斁譽髦斯士夫多士所以
寧文王也詩人不云士之賢
乃云文王壽考無斁之所致
然則楚材之盛不有所由致
哉我
皇上道久化成之效章章較著已
punctuated: 含靈篤慶，誕毓皇上，神聖繼天，於昭大統。夫五百年而王者興，其間有命世者。多士之生，應皇上之會，此其效也。《棫樸》之雅曰：「倬彼雲漢，爲章于天。周王壽考，遐不作人？」《思齊》曰：「古之人無斁，譽髦斯士。」夫多士所以寧文王也。詩人不云士之賢，乃云文王壽考、無斁之所致。然則楚材之盛，不有所由致哉？我皇上道久化成之效，章章較著已。
translation_en: …imbued with numinous potency and abundant blessings, he begot and nurtured His Majesty, whose divine sagacity carried on Heaven’s mandate and made the great imperial succession resplendent. Every five hundred years a true king arises, and in the interval there are men renowned in their age. The birth of these many scholars accords with the advent of His Majesty: this is evidence of that pattern. The court hymn “Luxuriant Oaks” (Yu pu) says: “Brilliant is that River of Heaven, forming a pattern in the sky. Long-lived is the king of Zhou: does he not nurture men of talent?” “Thinking of the Worthy” (Si qi) says: “The men of old were tireless in fostering these outstanding scholars.” These many scholars were the means by which King Wen was brought peace. Yet the poet does not speak of the scholars’ worthiness, but attributes it to King Wen’s longevity and tireless efforts. Does not the flourishing of talent in Chu likewise have a cause? The effects of His Majesty’s long practice of the Way and the fulfillment of his transforming influence are already abundantly manifest.

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
雖然士之自致與其所由□
於上其道未始不相須也士
以是應之而異其初之所成
上以是道之而違其終之所
望是鄉試之錄士辟之虛車
輪轅徒飾無所用之周之制
也三年賓興其鄉之賢者能
===
者而獻其書于王王拜受之
登之天府內史貳之此謂使
民興賢出使長也使民興能
入使治也賢與能皆書矣而
其用之德成而上藝成而下
其等異也當是時士之所以
致於上爭懋其德而不獨以
punctuated:
雖然，士之自致與其所由□於上，其道未始不相須也。士以是應之，而異其初之所成；上以是道之，而違其終之所望，是鄉試之錄士，辟之虛車，輪轅徒飾，無所用之。
周之制也，三年賓興其鄉之賢者能者，而獻其書于王。王拜受之，登之天府，內史貳之。此謂使民興賢，出使長也；使民興能，入使治也。賢與能皆書矣，而其用之，德成而上，藝成而下，其等異也。當是時，士之所以致於上，爭懋其德，而不獨以
translation_en:
Nevertheless, the means by which scholars attain distinction through their own efforts and those by which they receive □ from above [?] have always depended upon one another. If scholars respond to this yet depart from what initially formed them, and those above guide them in this way yet frustrate what was ultimately hoped for, then selecting scholars through the Provincial Examination is like an empty carriage: its wheels and shafts are mere ornaments, serving no purpose.
Under the Zhou system, every three years the worthy and capable men of each district were honored as guests and recommended, and a written record of them was presented to the king. The king bowed as he received it and deposited it in the Celestial Treasury; the Interior Scribe kept a duplicate. This is what was meant by having the people recommend the worthy, who were sent out to serve as leaders, and having the people recommend the capable, who were brought in to administer affairs. Both the worthy and the capable were recorded, but in their employment those accomplished in virtue were placed above, and those accomplished in skills below: their ranks differed. At that time, scholars seeking advancement under their superiors vied in cultivating their virtue, rather than relying solely on…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
藝自能故罝兎在野之人至
可爲公侯腹心功棐迪篤罔
不在時於稽内史之治信可
明徵後世抽天府之藏猶可
以指述勵翼篤棐之士而無
愧矣今鄉試之典其禮與成
周竝隆者也書多士之文辭
===
卒澤於道德仁義粹如也其
所以應上之求得猶未免於
藝乎如以成而下者自獻得
無與所望者背乎書曰皇極
之敷言是彝是訓惟帝其訓
皇之敬德錫厥庶民猶彝訓也矧
多士首沐
punctuated: 藝自能。故罝兎在野之人，至可爲公侯腹心；功棐迪篤，罔不在時。於稽内史之治，信可明徵。後世抽天府之藏，猶可以指述勵翼篤棐之士而無愧矣。今鄉試之典，其禮與成周竝隆者也。書多士之文辭，卒澤於道德仁義，粹如也。其所以應上之求，得猶未免於藝乎？如以成而下者自獻，得無與所望者背乎？《書》曰：「皇極之敷言，是彝是訓，惟帝其訓。」皇之敬德，錫厥庶民，猶彝訓也。矧多士首沐
translation_en:
…regard themselves as capable on the strength of their accomplishments alone. Thus even men setting rabbit nets in the countryside could become the trusted confidants of dukes and lords; those who rendered service and assistance, gave guidance, and practiced steadfastness were all to be found among them. Examining the administration of the Palace Secretary provides clear confirmation of this. Later generations, drawing upon the holdings of the Celestial Treasury, could still identify and recount, without embarrassment, the men who diligently assisted and steadfastly supported their rulers.
The present institution of the Provincial Examination rivals that of the fully established Zhou in the grandeur of its rites. The literary compositions of its many scholars are recorded; throughout, they are imbued with the Way, virtue, benevolence, and righteousness, and display purity. Can their response to what their superiors seek still remain confined to literary accomplishments? If they offer themselves on the basis of accomplishments that qualify them only for a lower rank, would they not run counter to what is expected of them?
The Book of Documents says: “The words setting forth the August Standard are constant principles and instructions; they are the sovereign’s instructions.” The emperor’s reverence for virtue, bestowed upon his common people, likewise constitutes constant principles and instructions. How much more, then, the many scholars, who are foremost in receiving…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
聖化久且益深自玆以往共能克
對大章而有指述於後世以
無失其終之望則文王以寧
之盛尚亦有稽於斯錄也夫
學詩不佞敬敘諸首簡維時
總督湖廣川貴軍務兵部侍
郎王崇先巡撫今總督湖廣
===
川貴採木都御史李憲卿巡
撫湖廣都御史趙炳然撫治
鄖陽都御史劉學易保釐輯
寧文武為憲江漢若流膠序
咸賴巡按直隸御史林騰蛟
考賦所至視學談經多士風
焉若雅志右文則總兵安遠
punctuated:
聖化久且益深，自玆以往，共能克對大章，而有指述於後世，以無失其終之望，則文王以寧之盛，尚亦有稽於斯錄也夫！學詩不佞，敬敘諸首簡。
維時，總督湖廣川貴軍務兵部侍郎王崇先，巡撫今總督湖廣川貴採木都御史李憲卿，巡撫湖廣都御史趙炳然，撫治鄖陽都御史劉學易，保釐輯寧，文武為憲，江漢若流，膠序咸賴。巡按直隸御史林騰蛟，考賦所至，視學談經，多士風焉。若雅志右文，則總兵安遠
translation_en:
…the sage ruler’s transforming influence for so long and ever more deeply. If, from this time forward, all can worthily respond to this great pattern [?] and leave something for later generations to point to and recount, without disappointing the hope that they will remain steadfast to the end, then the flourishing peace attained by King Wen may also find testimony in this record! I, Xueshi, though lacking in ability, respectfully place this preface at the beginning of the volume.
At this time, Wang Chongxian, Vice Minister of War and Supreme Commander of Military Affairs in Huguang, Sichuan, and Guizhou; Li Xianqing, Censor-in-chief, formerly Grand Coordinator and now Superintendent of Timber Procurement in Huguang, Sichuan, and Guizhou; Zhao Bingran, Censor-in-chief and Grand Coordinator of Huguang; and Liu Xueyi, Censor-in-chief and Pacification Commissioner of Yunyang, maintained good government and secured peace. They provided models in civil and military affairs; the Jiang and Han rivers flowed smoothly, and the schools all benefited from their support. Lin Tengjiao, Regional Inspector of Zhili, assessed levies [?] wherever he went, inspected schools, and discussed the Classics; the many scholars were inspired by his example. As for those whose enduring ambition was to promote literary learning, there was the Regional Commander, the Marquis of Anyuan…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
侯柳震守備太監張方而工
部郎中張國珍員外郎朱裳
主事方良曙先後有事茲土
胥勸得人者也左參政雷賀
右參政徐霈游震得張希舉
右參議成子學李燧宋廷表
郝成性副使龔秉德黃宗器
===
程秀民張正和周鎬王光祖
熊勉學僉事于錦周美柳宗
葵崔都朱天球署都指揮僉
事常勳與入
賀副使馮覲參議李萬實皆與
有勞焉至是計上而賢能適
與計偕斯亦全楚之修以待
punctuated: 侯柳震、守備太監張方，而工部郎中張國珍、員外郎朱裳、主事方良曙，先後有事茲土，胥勸得人者也。左參政雷賀，右參政徐霈、游震得、張希舉，右參議成子學、李燧、宋廷表、郝成性，副使龔秉德、黃宗器、程秀民、張正和、周鎬、王光祖、熊勉學，僉事于錦、周美、柳宗葵、崔都、朱天球，署都指揮僉事常勳，與入賀副使馮覲、參議李萬實，皆與有勞焉。至是，計上而賢能適與計偕，斯亦全楚之修以待
translation_en:
…Marquis Liu Zhen and the eunuch defender Zhang Fang; also Zhang Guozhen, Director in the Ministry of Works, Zhu Shang, Vice Director, and Fang Liangshu, Secretary, who successively undertook duties in this territory—all encouraged the recruitment of worthy men.
Lei He served as Left Administration Vice Commissioner. Xu Pei, You Zhende, and Zhang Xiju served as Right Administration Vice Commissioners. Cheng Zixue, Li Sui, Song Tingbiao, and Hao Chengxing served as Right Administration Assistant Commissioners. Gong Bingde, Huang Zongqi, Cheng Xiumin, Zhang Zhenghe, Zhou Hao, Wang Guangzu, and Xiong Mianxue served as Surveillance Vice Commissioners. Yu Jin, Zhou Mei, Liu Zongkui, Cui Du, and Zhu Tianqiu served as Surveillance Assistant Commissioners. Chang Xun served as Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner. Together with Surveillance Vice Commissioner Feng Jin and Administration Assistant Commissioner Li Wanshi, who went to court to offer congratulations, they all contributed their efforts to this undertaking.
Now the accounts have been submitted, and the worthy and able duly accompany their submission. This, too, represents the cultivation undertaken throughout Chu in preparation for…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
邦之大用者也於戲備矣
廣東廣州府儒學教授桂學
詩謹序
punctuated:
邦之大用者也。於戲，備矣！

廣東廣州府儒學教授桂學詩謹序。
translation_en:
…for great service to the state. Ah, all is complete!

Preface respectfully written by Gui Xueshi, Instructor at the Confucian School of Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong.

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試
監臨官
巡按湖廣監察御史吳百朋〔惟錫浙江義烏縣人丁未進士〕
提調官
湖廣等處承宣布政使司左布政使傅鎮〔國鼎福建中左千戶所籍福清縣人壬辰進士〕
湖廣等處承宣布政使司右布政使谷嶠〔惟升直隸興州前屯衞官籍河南息縣人戊戌進士〕
監試官
湖廣等處提刑按察司按察使俞憲〔汝成直隸無錫縣人戊戌進士〕
湖廣等處提刑按察司副使章士元〔伯允直隸吳縣人甲辰進士〕
===
考試官
廣東廣州府儒學教授桂學詩〔用言江西上饒縣人癸卯貢士〕
江西南昌府儒學教授蔣三近〔兼修四川涪州人丙午貢士〕
同考試官
直隸眞定府晉州儒學學正余兆陽〔少明廣西桂林中衞官籍直隸定遠縣人乙卯貢士〕
江西南昌府豐城縣儒學教諭黃驊〔德遠應天府六合縣人壬子貢士〕
河南河南府洛陽縣儒學教諭顧仕〔時可直隸興化縣人乙卯貢士〕
江西廣信府玉山縣儒學教諭吳鑄〔以範福建長樂縣人己酉貢士〕
浙江溫州府永嘉縣儒學教諭朱塗〔希禹江西樂平縣人丙午貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試。

監臨官。
巡按湖廣監察御史吳百朋〔惟錫，浙江義烏縣人，丁未進士〕。

提調官。
湖廣等處承宣布政使司左布政使傅鎮〔國鼎，福建中左千戶所籍，福清縣人，壬辰進士〕。
湖廣等處承宣布政使司右布政使谷嶠〔惟升，直隸興州前屯衞官籍，河南息縣人，戊戌進士〕。

監試官。
湖廣等處提刑按察司按察使俞憲〔汝成，直隸無錫縣人，戊戌進士〕。
湖廣等處提刑按察司副使章士元〔伯允，直隸吳縣人，甲辰進士〕。

考試官。
廣東廣州府儒學教授桂學詩〔用言，江西上饒縣人，癸卯貢士〕。
江西南昌府儒學教授蔣三近〔兼修，四川涪州人，丙午貢士〕。

同考試官。
直隸眞定府晉州儒學學正余兆陽〔少明，廣西桂林中衞官籍，直隸定遠縣人，乙卯貢士〕。
江西南昌府豐城縣儒學教諭黃驊〔德遠，應天府六合縣人，壬子貢士〕。
河南河南府洛陽縣儒學教諭顧仕〔時可，直隸興化縣人，乙卯貢士〕。
江西廣信府玉山縣儒學教諭吳鑄〔以範，福建長樂縣人，己酉貢士〕。
浙江溫州府永嘉縣儒學教諭朱塗〔希禹，江西樂平縣人，丙午貢士〕。
translation_en:
Huguang Provincial Examination, thirty-seventh year of Jiajing (1558).

Supervising Official
Wu Baipeng, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Huguang, had the courtesy name Weixi and was a native of Yiwu County, Zhejiang. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the dingwei year.

Proctors
Fu Zhen, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Huguang, had the courtesy name Guoding. He was registered in the Zhongzuo Battalion in Fujian, was a native of Fuqing County, and became a metropolitan graduate in the renchen year.
Gu Jiao, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Huguang, had the courtesy name Weisheng. He belonged to the military officer register of the Xingzhou Front Garrison Guard in Zhili, was a native of Xi County, Henan, and became a metropolitan graduate in the wuxu year.

Examination Overseers
Yu Xian, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Huguang, had the courtesy name Rucheng and was a native of Wuxi County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate in the wuxu year.

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
舜有臣五人而天下治
及其至也察乎天地
心之所同然者何也謂理也義也聖人先
得我心之所同然耳故理義之悅我心
猶芻豢之悅我口
易
元吉在上大有慶也
===
說之大民勸矣哉
制而用之謂之法利用出入民咸用之謂
之神
昔者聖人之作易也將以順性命之理是
以立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔
與剛立人之道曰仁與義兼三才而兩
之故易六畫而成卦分陰分陽迭用柔
剛故易六位而成章
書
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

舜有臣五人，而天下治。

及其至也，察乎天地。

心之所同然者何也？謂理也，義也。聖人先得我心之所同然耳，故理義之悅我心，猶芻豢之悅我口。

易

元吉在上，大有慶也。

說之大，民勸矣哉！

制而用之謂之法，利用出入，民咸用之謂之神。

昔者聖人之作易也，將以順性命之理，是以立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。兼三才而兩之，故易六畫而成卦；分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，故易六位而成章。

書
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Shun had five ministers, and all under Heaven was well governed.

…At its fullest extent, it is manifest throughout Heaven and Earth.

What is it that our hearts alike affirm? It is principle and righteousness. The sages simply apprehended before us what our hearts alike affirm. Thus principle and righteousness delight my heart just as the meat of grass-fed and grain-fed animals delights my palate.

Book of Changes (Yijing)

“Supreme good fortune” in the upper position means that there is great cause for rejoicing.

Great indeed is the power of joyousness: the people are thereby encouraged!

Fashioning something and putting it to use is called a method; making it beneficial in going out and coming in, so that all the people use it, is called the numinous.

When the sages of antiquity made the Changes, they intended to accord with the principles of human nature and destiny. Thus they established the Way of Heaven as yin and yang, the Way of Earth as yielding and firm, and the Way of humanity as benevolence and righteousness. They encompassed the Three Powers and doubled each; hence, in the Changes, six lines form a hexagram. They distinguished yin and yang and alternately employed yielding and firm; hence, in the Changes, the six positions form an ordered pattern.

Book of Documents (Shujing)

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
惟動丕應徯志以昭受上帝天其申命用
休
江漢朝宗于海九江孔殷沱潛既道雲土
夢作乂
一曰食二曰貨三曰祀四曰司空五曰司
徒六曰司寇七曰賓八曰師
公其惟時成周建無窮之基亦有無窮之
聞
詩
===
采采芣苢薄言袺之采采芣苢薄言襭之
如跂斯翼如矢斯棘如鳥斯革如翬斯飛
君子攸躋
虎拜稽首天子萬年
豐年多黍多稂亦有高廩萬億及秭為酒
為醴烝畀祖妣以洽百禮降福孔皆
春秋
秋九月齊侯宋公江人黃人盟于貫〔僖公〕
〔二年〕
punctuated:
惟動丕應，徯志，以昭受上帝，天其申命用休。
江漢朝宗于海，九江孔殷，沱潛既道，雲土夢作乂。
一曰食，二曰貨，三曰祀，四曰司空，五曰司徒，六曰司寇，七曰賓，八曰師。
公其惟時成周，建無窮之基，亦有無窮之聞。
詩
采采芣苢，薄言袺之。采采芣苢，薄言襭之。
如跂斯翼，如矢斯棘，如鳥斯革，如翬斯飛，君子攸躋。
虎拜稽首，天子萬年！
豐年多黍多稂，亦有高廩，萬億及秭。為酒為醴，烝畀祖妣，以洽百禮，降福孔皆。
春秋
秋九月，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人盟于貫。〔僖公〕〔二年〕
translation_en:
Whenever you acted, there was a mighty response; the people awaited your will. Thus you manifestly received the mandate of the Lord on High. Heaven will renew its mandate with favor.

The Jiang and Han rivers flow toward the sea as lords go to court. The nine rivers are well ordered; the Tuo and Qian have been channeled. The land at Yun and Meng was brought under cultivation.

The first is food; the second, goods; the third, sacrifices; the fourth, the Minister of Works; the fifth, the Minister of Education; the sixth, the Minister of Justice; the seventh, guests; and the eighth, the army.

May you, Duke, now bring Zhou to completion, establishing an everlasting foundation and likewise an everlasting renown.

Classic of Poetry

Gather, gather the plantain; hold up your skirts to carry it. Gather, gather the plantain; tuck your skirts into your belts to carry it.

Like someone standing on tiptoe, stately; like an arrow, straight; like a bird spreading its wings; like a pheasant in flight: here the noble lord ascends.

Hu bowed and knocked his head to the ground: “May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years!”

In a bountiful year there is much millet and much darnel [?], and there are lofty granaries, holding myriads upon myriads of grain. We make wine and sweet wine, presenting them to our ancestral fathers and mothers, fulfilling the hundred rites. They send down blessings in fullest measure.

Spring and Autumn Annals

In autumn, in the ninth month, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and representatives of Jiang and Huang made a covenant at Guan. 〔Duke Xi〕〔Second year〕

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
歸父還自晉至笙遂奔齊〔宣公十有八年〕
夏蔡朝吳出奔鄭〔昭公十有五年〕秋
晉士鞅宋樂祁犁衞北宮喜曹人邾人
滕人會于扈〔昭公二十有七年〕三月
公會劉子晉侯宋公蔡侯衞侯陳子鄭
伯許男曹伯莒子邾子頓子胡子滕子
薛伯杞伯小邾子齊國夏于召陵侵楚
〔定公四年〕
吳入州來〔成公七年〕
===
冬楚子蔡侯陳侯許男頓子沈子徐人越
人伐吳〔昭公五年〕夏曹公孫會自鄭
出奔宋〔昭公二十年〕
禮記
凡在天下九州之民者無不咸獻其力以
共皇天上帝社稷寢廟山林名川之祀
樂者心之動也聲者樂之象也文采節奏
聲之飾也君子動其本樂其象然後治
其飾
punctuated:
歸父還自晉，至笙，遂奔齊。〔宣公十有八年〕夏，蔡朝吳出奔鄭。〔昭公十有五年〕秋，晉士鞅、宋樂祁犁、衞北宮喜、曹人、邾人、滕人會于扈。〔昭公二十有七年〕三月，公會劉子、晉侯、宋公、蔡侯、衞侯、陳子、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、莒子、邾子、頓子、胡子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊國夏于召陵，侵楚。〔定公四年〕吳入州來。〔成公七年〕冬，楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、許男、頓子、沈子、徐人、越人伐吳。〔昭公五年〕夏，曹公孫會自鄭出奔宋。〔昭公二十年〕

禮記

凡在天下九州之民者，無不咸獻其力，以共皇天上帝、社稷、寢廟、山林、名川之祀。

樂者，心之動也；聲者，樂之象也；文采節奏，聲之飾也。君子動其本，樂其象，然後治其飾。
translation_en:
Guifu returned from Jin, reached Sheng, and then fled to Qi. 〔Eighteenth year of Duke Xuan.〕 In summer, Chao Wu of Cai fled to Zheng. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕 In autumn, Shi Yang of Jin, Yue Qili of Song, Beigong Xi of Wei, and representatives of Cao, Zhu, and Teng met at Hu. 〔Twenty-seventh year of Duke Zhao.〕 In the third month, the Duke of Lu met with the Viscount of Liu, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Wei, the Viscount of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi 杞, the Viscount of Lesser Zhu, and Guo Xia of Qi 齊 at Shaoling, and invaded Chu. 〔Fourth year of Duke Ding.〕 Wu entered Zhoulai. 〔Seventh year of Duke Cheng.〕 In winter, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Chen, the Baron of Xu, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Shen, and representatives of Xu 徐 and Yue attacked Wu. 〔Fifth year of Duke Zhao.〕 In summer, Gongsun Hui of Cao fled from Zheng to Song. 〔Twentieth year of Duke Zhao.〕

Record of Rites (Liji)

All the people dwelling in the Nine Provinces under Heaven contribute their labor to provide for sacrifices to August Heaven and the Sovereign on High, the gods of soil and grain, the ancestral chambers and temples, the mountains and forests, and the renowned rivers.

Music is the movement of the heart; sound is the manifestation of music; patterned embellishments and rhythm are the adornments of sound. The gentleman sets its root in motion, takes pleasure in its manifestation, and then regulates its adornments.

擬唐以姚元之同三品誥〔開元元年〕。
擬賜歷代名臣奏議羣臣謝表〔永樂十四年〕。
判語〔五條〕
官員赴任過限。
虛出通關硃鈔。
致祭祀典神祇。
軍民約會詞訟。
修理橋梁道路。
第叁場
translation_en:
Blessing means completeness; completeness is the name for conformity in every respect. To be in conformity in every respect is what is called completeness.
Benevolence is on the right; the Way is on the left.
Second Session
Discourse
“Great indeed was Yao as a ruler!”
Edicts, Letters of Appointment, and Memorials 〔One topic from among these [?].〕
Compose an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty ordering the commanderies and kingdoms to seek out worthy men who have been overlooked. 〔Eleventh year of Emperor Gao’s reign.〕
Compose a letter of appointment in the manner of the Tang dynasty appointing Yao Yuanzhi as Grand Councilor (tong sanpin). 〔First year of the Kaiyuan reign.〕
Compose a memorial of thanks on behalf of the assembled officials upon receiving the imperially bestowed Memorials of Famous Ministers of Successive Dynasties. 〔Fourteenth year of the Yongle reign.〕
Legal Judgments 〔Five items.〕
Officials exceeding the time limit for taking up their posts.
Fraudulent issuance of vermilion clearance receipts.
Offering sacrifices to deities listed in the official register of sacrifices.
Military personnel and civilians arranging to meet for litigation [?].
Repairing bridges and roads.
Third Session

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第五道
問養士莫重於明倫化民莫先於善俗斯
二者人治之大者也聖帝明王其教思
無窮矣而施由近始恒於湯沐惓惓焉
書紀平章詩頌譽髦皆是道也兩漢繼
周而興稍爲近古詔郡國以孝廉舉士
詔有司以孝弟教民流風善政猶有存
者然而歌風餘烈徒詫乎帝鄉臨雍上
儀無裨於主德方諸古昔遠矣其得失
===
可詳言之歟由漢而下亦有足稱者歟
我
太祖高皇帝繼天立極用夏變夷治教畢張人
士永賴過淮
諭父老示之以化俗之大端
卽位諭中書示之以興學之上務篤近舉遠
德教沛然洋洋
聖謨萬世爲楷亦可得而誦說之歟至我
皇上建
punctuated:
第五道

問：養士莫重於明倫，化民莫先於善俗，斯二者人治之大者也。聖帝明王，其教思無窮矣，而施由近始，恒於湯沐惓惓焉。《書》紀平章，《詩》頌譽髦，皆是道也。兩漢繼周而興，稍爲近古，詔郡國以孝廉舉士，詔有司以孝弟教民，流風善政猶有存者。然而歌風餘烈徒詫乎帝鄉，臨雍上儀無裨於主德，方諸古昔遠矣。其得失可詳言之歟？由漢而下，亦有足稱者歟？我太祖高皇帝繼天立極，用夏變夷，治教畢張，人士永賴。過淮，諭父老，示之以化俗之大端；卽位，諭中書，示之以興學之上務。篤近舉遠，德教沛然洋洋，聖謨萬世爲楷，亦可得而誦說之歟？至我皇上建
translation_en:
Fifth Question

Question: In nurturing scholars, nothing is more important than clarifying human relationships; in transforming the people, nothing takes precedence over improving customs. These two are great concerns of human governance. The sage emperors and enlightened kings gave inexhaustible thought to instruction, yet began its implementation close at hand, showing constant solicitude for their home domains. The Documents records the harmonizing of the people, and the Odes celebrates men of outstanding reputation: both embody this principle. The two Han dynasties arose after the Zhou and came somewhat close to ancient practice. They commanded the commanderies and kingdoms to recommend men for their filial piety and integrity, and instructed the responsible officials to teach the people filial piety and respect for elder brothers. Something of the inherited influence and good government of antiquity thus remained. Nevertheless, the lingering glory of the Song of the Wind merely occasioned boasts in the emperor’s hometown, while the grand ceremony of visiting the imperial school did nothing to advance the ruler’s virtue. Compared with antiquity, these fell far short. Can you explain their successes and failures in detail? From the Han onward, were there also examples worthy of praise?

Our Emperor Taizu Gao succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard, transforming the non-Chinese through the civilization of Xia. Government and instruction were fully instituted, and scholars and people have benefited ever since. When passing through Huai, he addressed the elders, showing them the fundamental principles for transforming customs. Upon ascending the throne, he instructed the Secretariat, showing it the foremost duties in promoting learning. He devoted care to those nearby and extended it to those afar; his moral instruction flowed abundantly and expansively. His sagely plans are a model for ten thousand generations. Can you also recite and explain them? Coming to our present emperor, who establishes …

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
君師之極操政教之本
聲教所訖莫不彬彬而
首善之建始于南國其
幸舊邦也頒
詔閭里立烝民之彝訓其顯
先德也勒文郡學覲
皇考之耿光所以丕承
祖禰廣勵士民亦必有典要乎視我
皇祖之舊章帝王之遐軌同一揆乎否邪夫識
===
其大者惟賢者能之其對揚
天子之
顯命
問大倫有五而君親爲重臣之事君子之
事親惟忠與孝爾此至德要道萬世不
可易也昔之論大孝純忠至虞舜周公
止矣載攷傳記有分忠孝爲二者有合
忠孝爲一者有專問孝而不及於忠者
豈其道固當兼盡而亦未始相悖歟孝
punctuated:
君師之極，操政教之本，聲教所訖，莫不彬彬。而首善之建，始于南國。其幸舊邦也，頒詔閭里，立烝民之彝訓；其顯先德也，勒文郡學，覲皇考之耿光。所以丕承祖禰，廣勵士民，亦必有典要乎？視我皇祖之舊章、帝王之遐軌，同一揆乎？否邪？夫識其大者，惟賢者能之，其對揚天子之顯命。

問：大倫有五，而君親爲重。臣之事君，子之事親，惟忠與孝爾。此至德要道，萬世不可易也。昔之論大孝純忠，至虞舜、周公止矣。載攷傳記，有分忠孝爲二者，有合忠孝爲一者，有專問孝而不及於忠者。豈其道固當兼盡，而亦未始相悖歟？孝
translation_en:
…the highest standard of ruler and teacher, grasping the foundations of government and moral instruction. Wherever his civilizing influence reaches, all are refined and well ordered. The establishment of a model of goodness began in the southern lands. When he visited his former homeland, he promulgated an edict throughout its neighborhoods and villages, establishing enduring precepts for the people. To make manifest his forebears’ virtue, he had a text engraved at the prefectural school, displaying [?] the radiant glory of his deceased imperial father. Surely there must be authoritative principles by which he thus grandly carries forward the legacy of his ancestors and father and broadly encourages scholars and commoners? Compared with the established institutions of our imperial ancestor and the precedents of emperors and kings of distant antiquity, do these follow the same guiding principle, or not? Only the worthy can discern what is greatest in these matters. Respond to and extol the Son of Heaven’s illustrious command.

Question: There are five great human relationships, of which those with one’s ruler and parents are the most important. A minister’s service to his ruler and a son’s service to his parents consist simply in loyalty and filial piety. These are the highest virtues and the essential Way, unalterable for ten thousand generations. In discussions of great filial piety and pure loyalty in antiquity, none surpassed Shun of Yu and the Duke of Zhou. Yet, on examining transmitted writings and records, we find some that distinguish loyalty and filial piety as two things, some that unite them as one, and some that inquire solely into filial piety without addressing loyalty. Is it that this Way requires both to be fulfilled, and that they have never been mutually contradictory? The Classic of Filial…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
經一書成於曾子門人之手其言自天
子至於庶人孝無終始後世乃有擬作
忠經而其中所列則以聖君冢臣百工
守宰兆人為序然則忠之為道又不專
為人臣者訓其可與孝經相為表裏否
歟抑别有可議者歟我
國家以綱常為治甞莊誦
孝順事實
歷代臣鑒與夫
===
五倫書所載所以教天下之為人臣子者至
矣其宏綱要旨可數而敬陳之歟諸士
子行且服官移孝為忠矣試以平日所
講明者著于篇以觀敦本重倫之學毋
徒曰藝焉已哉
問天道運而陰陽相巡故百物化聖德運
而文武並用故百志成三代之英非獨
文事能也而亦有用武之績若大禹伊
尹周公是已聖帝明王咸用之而致盛
punctuated:
經一書成於曾子門人之手，其言自天子至於庶人，孝無終始。後世乃有擬作《忠經》，而其中所列，則以聖君、冢臣、百工、守宰、兆人為序。然則忠之為道，又不專為人臣者訓，其可與《孝經》相為表裏否歟？抑别有可議者歟？我國家以綱常為治，甞莊誦《孝順事實》、《歷代臣鑒》與夫《五倫書》所載，所以教天下之為人臣子者至矣。其宏綱要旨，可數而敬陳之歟？諸士子行且服官，移孝為忠矣。試以平日所講明者著于篇，以觀敦本重倫之學，毋徒曰藝焉已哉！

問：天道運而陰陽相巡，故百物化；聖德運而文武並用，故百志成。三代之英，非獨文事能也，而亦有用武之績，若大禹、伊尹、周公是已。聖帝明王咸用之而致盛
translation_en:
…the Classic of Filial Piety was composed by disciples of Zengzi. It speaks of everyone from the Son of Heaven down to the common people, saying that filial piety has neither end nor beginning [?]. In later ages, someone composed a Classic of Loyalty in imitation of it. Its contents proceed in the order of the sage ruler, chief ministers, the various officials, prefects and magistrates, and the multitude of the people. Thus, the Way of loyalty likewise offers instruction beyond those who serve as subjects. Can this work and the Classic of Filial Piety complement one another as outer and inner aspects of the same teaching? Or are there other points open to question? Our dynasty governs through the cardinal bonds and constant virtues. Having reverently read the contents of True Accounts of Filial Obedience, Mirror for Ministers of Successive Dynasties, and the Book of the Five Human Relationships, we find that their instruction for all under Heaven who are subjects and children is most complete. Can you enumerate and respectfully explain their broad principles and essential meanings? You candidates will soon hold office and turn your filial devotion into loyalty. Set down in an essay what you have studied and clarified in your daily learning, so that we may assess your learning in strengthening the foundations and honoring human relationships. Do not regard this merely as an exercise in literary skill!

Question: The Way of Heaven moves, and yin and yang alternate; thus the myriad things are transformed. Sagely virtue operates, and civil and military means are employed together; thus the many purposes are accomplished. The outstanding men of the Three Dynasties were capable not only in civil affairs but also achieved success through the use of arms. Yu the Great, Yi Yin, and the Duke of Zhou are examples. Sage emperors and enlightened kings employed both and thereby brought about flourishing…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
治其經緯之章戡定之烈果相須乎否
邪後世若左袒之師澶淵之役武功競
矣或木彊少文或不學無術終不以其
故貶功獨何歟他若才儗管葛而前部
生心言事慷慨而車戰失利之二子非
不文也何爲乎勝負無益邪我
皇上文武聖神法天爲治思得全才而任使之
今搢紳之士莫不知兵封疆之臣莫不
講業文武之材具矣南平日本北走匈
===
奴率用此也然而當事諸臣猶或不能
稱
上意何哉頃者
詔求備邊之材羣臣得舉所知矣其間才各有
長短而華實亦異誇大者或慕請纓之
名雍容者或襲緩帶之譽執秩者將何
以科察之夫文武爲憲其人楚産也諸
士尚友古人必有足述者願聞其槩當
爲籍
punctuated: 治，其經緯之章、戡定之烈，果相須乎？否邪？後世若左袒之師、澶淵之役，武功競矣，或木彊少文，或不學無術，終不以其故貶功，獨何歟？他若才儗管葛而前部生心、言事慷慨而車戰失利之二子，非不文也，何爲乎勝負無益邪？我皇上文武聖神，法天爲治，思得全才而任使之。今搢紳之士莫不知兵，封疆之臣莫不講業，文武之材具矣。南平日本，北走匈奴，率用此也。然而當事諸臣猶或不能稱上意，何哉？頃者詔求備邊之材，羣臣得舉所知矣。其間才各有長短，而華實亦異。誇大者或慕請纓之名，雍容者或襲緩帶之譽，執秩者將何以科察之？夫文武爲憲，其人楚産也。諸士尚友古人，必有足述者，願聞其槩，當爲籍
translation_en:
…order. Were their achievements in organizing government and their exploits in suppressing disorder indeed mutually dependent, or were they not? In later ages, military achievements were outstanding in such instances as the army that bared its left arms and the campaign at Chanyuan. Yet one leader was blunt and unpolished, another unlearned and lacking in method; ultimately, their accomplishments were not belittled on that account. Why was this? Consider, too, those two men: one whose abilities were compared to those of Guan Zhong and Zhuge Liang, yet whose vanguard became disaffected; the other who spoke impassionedly on affairs, yet suffered defeat in chariot warfare. Neither lacked civil accomplishments. Why, then, did these avail them nothing in determining victory or defeat?
Our Emperor, accomplished in civil and military affairs, sagely and divine, models his government on Heaven and wishes to find men of comprehensive ability to employ. Today, among the officials there are none who do not understand warfare, and among the ministers responsible for the frontiers there are none who do not study their duties. Talent in both civil and military affairs is thus available. Pacifying the Japanese in the south and putting the Xiongnu to flight in the north have largely depended upon this. Yet some ministers charged with these affairs still fail to satisfy the imperial will. Why is this?
Recently, an edict sought men capable of defending the frontiers, permitting the ministers to recommend those they knew. Among such men, each has strengths and weaknesses, and outward brilliance likewise differs from actual substance. The boastful may covet the fame of volunteering for military service; the composed may lay claim to the reputation of a commander who wears his sash loosely. How should officials holding rank scrutinize and assess them? As for the man who was ‘a model in civil and military affairs,’ he was a native of Chu. You candidates take the ancients as your friends and must have something worth recounting. I would hear its broad outlines, and shall make a record of it…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
奏之
問六籍而下楚士以論著鳴者吾得二人
焉昔稱或爲詞賦之祖或得孔孟之傳
固皆不朽之言矣槩諸六經何所祖述
乎世謂易微而易在楚詩亡而詩在楚
信斯議也宜莫如二家之言乃今挾策
而讀之則無當二者詩與易安在哉宋
玉景差為騷羽翼其後移官長沙者賦
而悼之則皆受繩墨於騷矣可與三閭
絜廣狹乎二程伯仲受圖歸洛其後講
業嶽麓者猶多發明則皆受符節於圖
矣可與春陵相後先乎夫引三后之純
粹揭聖人之立極其言弘廓深遠矣使
得志當世果能有所建述庶幾疇昔者
乎藉令絳灌之言不入黨錮之禁輒罷
二三君子所就業孰多邪諸士居其國
誦讀其詩書宜論其世矣豈曰方人為
賢
punctuated:
奏之。

問：六籍而下，楚士以論著鳴者，吾得二人焉。昔稱或爲詞賦之祖，或得孔孟之傳，固皆不朽之言矣。槩諸六經，何所祖述乎？世謂易微而易在楚，詩亡而詩在楚。信斯議也，宜莫如二家之言。乃今挾策而讀之，則無當二者，詩與易安在哉？宋玉、景差為騷羽翼，其後移官長沙者賦而悼之，則皆受繩墨於騷矣，可與三閭絜廣狹乎？二程伯仲受圖歸洛，其後講業嶽麓者猶多發明，則皆受符節於圖矣，可與春陵相後先乎？夫引三后之純粹，揭聖人之立極，其言弘廓深遠矣。使得志當世，果能有所建述，庶幾疇昔者乎？藉令絳灌之言不入，黨錮之禁輒罷，二三君子所就業孰多邪？諸士居其國，誦讀其詩書，宜論其世矣。豈曰方人為賢？
translation_en:
…submit it to the throne.

Question: Among the scholars of Chu since the Six Classics, I find two renowned for their writings. One has been called the progenitor of lyric poetry and rhapsodies; the other, an inheritor of the teachings of Confucius and Mencius. Their writings are assuredly imperishable. Yet, measured against the Six Classics, what did they take as their models and transmit? People say that when the Changes became obscure, the Changes remained in Chu, and when the Poetry was lost, the Poetry remained in Chu. If this judgment is sound, nothing should surpass the writings of these two masters. Yet when we take up their books and read them today, they correspond to neither of these two classics. Where, then, are the Poetry and the Changes?

Song Yu and Jing Cha lent wings to the Encountering Sorrow (Li sao). Later, the man transferred to office in Changsha [Jia Yi] composed a rhapsody lamenting its author. All thus took their standards from the Encountering Sorrow. Can their breadth of vision be measured against that of the Grand Master of the Three Clans [Qu Yuan]? The two Cheng brothers received the Diagram and returned to Luo; those who later taught at Yuelu further elucidated much of its meaning. All thus received their credentials from the Diagram. Can they rank alongside the master of Chunling [Zhou Dunyi]?

One invoked the unsullied virtue of the three sovereigns; the other expounded the sage’s establishment of the Supreme Ultimate. Their words were expansive, profound, and far-reaching. Had they been able to realize their aspirations in their own times, could they indeed have established institutions and transmitted teachings approaching those of antiquity? Suppose that the words of Jiang and Guan had gone unheeded and the prohibitions against the proscribed faction had promptly been lifted: which of these gentlemen would have accomplished more?

You scholars dwell in their country and recite their poetry and writings; you ought therefore to consider the times in which they lived. Could one say that merely comparing others makes one worthy?

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
問楚地踔遠三江七澤在焉大都利病水
利與江防是已夫稻人之職周以足民
樓船之官漢以弭盜其籍固在可舉而
行之與後若芍陂開利漳水興謠引涇
而名鄭渠灌蜀而號陸海此皆興民利
者也渤海易俗交趾作歌到部而冀州
遂安懸鼓而兗州無警此皆捍民患者
也所至輒效其果遵何術哉
國家之制以營水利則郡縣分職監司董之
===
矣然潜沔之隄防猶或潰溢公滋之利
患互爲乘除沙洋之績不終穴口之議
復沮是興利而利未滋也以飭江防則
吏士分部監司督之矣然沿江而下不
廢干掫舟楫所過猶多警備或乘徵調
而牟利或爲嚮導而召姦是捍患而患
未弭也察斯二者果無治人乎抑亦無
治法乎玆欲導地利以布民詰方慝以
屏惡將何施而可願爲有司決策焉
punctuated:
問：楚地踔遠，三江七澤在焉，大都利病，水利與江防是已。夫稻人之職，周以足民；樓船之官，漢以弭盜。其籍固在，可舉而行之與？後若芍陂開利，漳水興謠，引涇而名鄭渠，灌蜀而號陸海，此皆興民利者也。渤海易俗，交趾作歌，到部而冀州遂安，懸鼓而兗州無警，此皆捍民患者也。所至輒效，其果遵何術哉？
國家之制，以營水利，則郡縣分職，監司董之矣。然潜沔之隄防猶或潰溢，公滋之利患互爲乘除，沙洋之績不終，穴口之議復沮，是興利而利未滋也。以飭江防，則吏士分部，監司督之矣。然沿江而下，不廢干掫；舟楫所過，猶多警備。或乘徵調而牟利，或爲嚮導而召姦，是捍患而患未弭也。察斯二者，果無治人乎？抑亦無治法乎？玆欲導地利以布民，詰方慝以屏惡，將何施而可？願爲有司決策焉。
translation_en:
Question: The territory of Chu extends far and wide, encompassing the Three Rivers and Seven Marshes. Its principal benefits and troubles concern water management and river defense. Through the office of the Rice Officer, the Zhou ensured the people’s sufficiency; through officials commanding towered warships, the Han suppressed banditry. The records of these institutions still exist. Can they be taken up and put into practice?
In later times, the Shaopi reservoir brought benefits, and works on the Zhang River inspired popular songs. Water diverted from the Jing gave the Zheng Canal its name, while irrigation in Shu earned that region the designation “a sea on land.” These all promoted the people’s welfare. Customs were transformed in Bohai, and songs were composed in Jiaozhi; an official’s arrival in his jurisdiction brought peace to Jizhou, and the hanging of a drum left Yanzhou free of alarms. These all protected the people against harm. Wherever such officials went, their measures proved effective. What methods did they actually follow?
Under the institutions of our dynasty, prefectures and counties have their respective responsibilities for water management, while the surveillance authorities oversee them. Yet the embankments of Qian and Mian still sometimes breach and overflow; in Gong and Zi [?], benefits and harms alternately increase and diminish; the works at Shayang remain unfinished, and the proposal concerning Xuekou has again been obstructed. Thus, benefits are promoted, yet have not increased.
For maintaining river defense, civil officials and soldiers are assigned separate sectors, and the surveillance authorities supervise them. Yet patrols cannot be discontinued along the river downstream, and wherever boats pass, extensive precautions remain necessary. Some exploit requisitions and mobilizations for profit; others act as guides, bringing in malefactors. Thus, harm is resisted, yet has not been quelled.
Considering these two matters, is there truly a lack of people capable of governing? Or is there also a lack of effective methods of government? We now wish to develop the land’s resources so that the people may be settled, and to investigate local wrongdoing so that evil may be expelled. What measures would accomplish this? Please determine a course of action for the responsible authorities.

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
舜有臣五人而天下治
陳述齡
同考試官敎諭陳批揄揚而有典則卽有
能言斯亦擅塲矣
同考試官敎諭吳批形容虞廷明良相遇
之盛讀之令人躍然
考試官敎授蔣批爾雅深厚一字不苟
===
考試官敎授桂批精緻
聖君得人之盛而天下化成焉蓋君得臣而萬
化行也大舜得人之盛如此其治化之隆也有
以哉記者之意若謂天之生才不偶而君臣之
相遇爲難惟夫舜也以重華之德陟元后之位
紹堯致治太和丕著於人文應運而興羣賢咸
服於有位禹爲司空棄爲后稷凡其所翕受以
熙帝之載者皆名世之良弼焉契作司徒臯陶
作士而伯益作虞凡其所時舉以亮天之工者
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

舜有臣五人而天下治

陳述齡

同考試官敎諭陳批：揄揚而有典則，卽有能言，斯亦擅塲矣。

同考試官敎諭吳批：形容虞廷明良相遇之盛，讀之令人躍然。

考試官敎授蔣批：爾雅深厚，一字不苟。

考試官敎授桂批：精緻。

聖君得人之盛，而天下化成焉。蓋君得臣而萬化行也。大舜得人之盛如此，其治化之隆也有以哉！記者之意若謂：天之生才不偶，而君臣之相遇爲難。惟夫舜也，以重華之德，陟元后之位，紹堯致治，太和丕著於人文；應運而興，羣賢咸服於有位。禹爲司空，棄爲后稷，凡其所翕受以熙帝之載者，皆名世之良弼焉。契作司徒，臯陶作士，而伯益作虞，凡其所時舉以亮天之工者，
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Shun had five ministers, and all under Heaven was well governed.”

Chen Shuling

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Its praise accords with classical standards. Even among accomplished writers, this author would excel.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “It depicts the flourishing court of Yu, where an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers met. Reading it makes one leap with delight.”

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: “Elegant and substantial; not a single word is carelessly chosen.”

Comment by Examiner Gui, Professor: “Exquisite.”

So abundantly did the sage ruler obtain worthy men that all under Heaven was transformed and perfected. For when a ruler obtains ministers, every transforming influence takes effect. Such was the abundance of worthy men obtained by the great Shun: surely the flourishing of his government and transforming influence had its cause!

The recorder’s meaning seems to be this: Heaven does not produce talented men by chance, yet a ruler and his ministers seldom find one another. Shun, possessing the virtue of ‘redoubled splendor,’ ascended to the sovereign’s throne. Succeeding Yao in bringing about good government, he made supreme harmony manifest in human culture. Arising in response to his destined time, he had all the assembled worthies serving in official positions. Yu served as Minister of Works, and Qi as Minister of Agriculture. Those whom he gathered and welcomed to advance the sovereign’s undertakings were all excellent supporting ministers renowned in their age. Xie served as Minister of Education, Gao Yao as Judge, and Bo Yi as Forester. All those whom he raised up at the proper time to assist in Heaven’s work …

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
皆盛時之黎獻焉以舜爲君使五人者爲臣是
不惟有君也而又有臣也不惟有臣也而又衆
多也天下欲無治焉得乎蓋舜統治於上則聖
人作而萬物覩五人者分治於下則賢才輔而
庶績凝股肱耳目各能其職而水土以平也民
人以育也野無遺賢茲萬邦之所以咸寧乎左
右贊襄各宣其力而百姓以親也五刑以明也
鳥獸草木以若也俊乂在官茲四方之所以風
動乎天爲舜而生才舜爲天下而得人知人以
===
安民此惟大舜之能事而有虞人才之盛可想
見矣抑聞之天不言而萬物亨歲功成者五行
之運宣其化矣舜猶天也五人者猶五行之順
布於四時也承君之德而宣之民者也舜與天
合德則其從欲以治者豈惟得人焉爾乎嗚呼
雖甚盛德蔑以加矣
及其至也察乎天地
張楚翹
同考試官教諭顧 批察天地處括盡章旨
punctuated:
皆盛時之黎獻焉。以舜爲君，使五人者爲臣，是不惟有君也，而又有臣也；不惟有臣也，而又衆多也。天下欲無治，焉得乎？蓋舜統治於上，則聖人作而萬物覩；五人者分治於下，則賢才輔而庶績凝。股肱耳目各能其職，而水土以平也，民人以育也。野無遺賢，茲萬邦之所以咸寧乎！左右贊襄，各宣其力，而百姓以親也，五刑以明也，鳥獸草木以若也。俊乂在官，茲四方之所以風動乎！天爲舜而生才，舜爲天下而得人，知人以安民，此惟大舜之能事，而有虞人才之盛可想見矣。抑聞之，天不言而萬物亨、歲功成者，五行之運宣其化矣。舜猶天也，五人者猶五行之順布於四時也，承君之德而宣之民者也。舜與天合德，則其從欲以治者，豈惟得人焉爾乎？嗚呼！雖甚盛德，蔑以加矣。
及其至也，察乎天地。
張楚翹
同考試官教諭顧批：察天地處，括盡章旨。
translation_en:
…were all worthies of that flourishing age. With Shun as ruler and these five men serving as his ministers, there was not only a ruler but also ministers; and not only ministers, but a wealth of them. How could the realm fail to be well governed? For when Shun presided over government above, the sage arose and all things beheld him; when the five men shared the work of government below, worthy and talented men assisted him, and every undertaking was firmly established. Serving as his limbs, ears, and eyes, each fulfilled his office: the waters and lands were brought into order, and the people were nurtured. No worthy remained overlooked in the countryside—was this not why the myriad states all enjoyed peace? Those assisting him on either side each exerted their strength: the people were brought into affectionate harmony, the five punishments were made clear, and birds, beasts, plants, and trees flourished in due order. Outstanding men held office—was this not why the four quarters responded as if stirred by the wind? Heaven produced talented men for Shun, and Shun secured men for the sake of the realm. To recognize men’s abilities and thereby bring peace to the people was the particular accomplishment of the great Shun; from this we can imagine the abundance of talent under the house of Youyu.
I have also heard that Heaven does not speak, yet all things prosper and the year’s work is accomplished because the movements of the Five Phases give effect to its transforming power. Shun was like Heaven; these five men were like the Five Phases, duly distributed through the four seasons. They received their ruler’s virtue and extended it to the people. Since Shun’s virtue accorded with Heaven, could his governing as he wished have depended merely on securing the right men? Ah! Even virtue of the greatest magnificence could add nothing to this.
“When it reaches its utmost extent, it is manifest throughout Heaven and Earth.”
Zhang Chuqiao
Comment by Associate Examiner Gu, Instructor: The passage on “manifest throughout Heaven and Earth” encompasses the entire purport of the chapter.…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
類以浮詞失之此作良是
同考試官學正余批體認旣明詞復純正
可以爲文矣
考試官敎授蔣批馴雅可誦
考試官敎授桂批有理致
中庸舉斯道之全體而通極於天地焉夫法象
莫大於天地也而斯道之全體有以通極之不
其費矣乎中庸論費隱而結之以此若曰道之
在天下也始於近不禦於遠君子之於道也析
===
其精必合其全故語道而始於夫婦者特就其
造端言之耳而非其全體也若推類以究其極
則徵之聖人而聖人無全能質之天地而天地
有遺憾小大莫不無該而上下相爲昭格是不
亦察於天地乎故仰觀於天凡高明所覆而在
天成象者皆斯道之峻極也俯察於地凡博厚
所載而在地成形者皆斯道之蟠委也以兩而
化則乾以大生坤以廣生其並行而不悖者孰
非太極之各足邪以一而神則天道下濟地道
punctuated:
類以浮詞失之，此作良是。
同考試官學正余批：體認旣明，詞復純正，可以爲文矣。
考試官敎授蔣批：馴雅可誦。
考試官敎授桂批：有理致。
中庸舉斯道之全體而通極於天地焉。夫法象莫大於天地也，而斯道之全體有以通極之，不其費矣乎？中庸論費隱而結之以此，若曰：道之在天下也，始於近，不禦於遠；君子之於道也，析其精，必合其全。故語道而始於夫婦者，特就其造端言之耳，而非其全體也。若推類以究其極，則徵之聖人，而聖人無全能；質之天地，而天地有遺憾。小大莫不無該，而上下相爲昭格，是不亦察於天地乎？故仰觀於天，凡高明所覆而在天成象者，皆斯道之峻極也；俯察於地，凡博厚所載而在地成形者，皆斯道之蟠委也。以兩而化，則乾以大生，坤以廣生，其並行而不悖者，孰非太極之各足邪？以一而神，則天道下濟，地道
translation_en:
…Generally, they go astray through empty phrasing; this composition is very sound.
Associate Examiner Yu, an Instructor, comments: “His grasp is clear, and his language is also pure and correct. This qualifies as accomplished writing.”
Examiner Jiang, a Professor, comments: “Refined and elegant, worthy of recitation.”
Examiner Gui, a Professor, comments: “It has reasoned depth.”
The Doctrine of the Mean presents this Way in its entirety, extending its reach to the utmost throughout Heaven and Earth. Now, among models and manifestations, none are greater than Heaven and Earth. Yet the entirety of this Way can extend throughout them to their furthest limits: is its scope not vast? The Doctrine of the Mean discusses the Way’s vastness and hidden subtlety and concludes with this statement, as though saying: The Way in the world begins with what is near, yet is not held back from what is distant. In approaching the Way, the gentleman analyzes its subtleties but must also bring together its entirety. Thus, when discussion of the Way begins with husband and wife, it speaks only of its starting point, not of its entirety. If we extend the analogy to investigate its ultimate reach, then, when tested against the sages, even the sages cannot master it completely; when measured against Heaven and Earth, even Heaven and Earth have imperfections. Nothing, small or great, lies outside its embrace [?], and above and below illuminate and reach one another. Is this not its manifest presence throughout Heaven and Earth?
Thus, looking upward to Heaven, everything covered by its height and brightness and taking form there as a celestial manifestation is this Way in its towering sublimity. Looking downward to Earth, everything borne by its breadth and thickness and taking shape there is this Way in its winding extension. In transforming through duality, Qian brings forth through greatness, and Kun brings forth through breadth. As they proceed together without conflict, how could either fail to possess the Supreme Ultimate in full? In working wondrously through unity, Heaven’s Way descends to aid below, and Earth’s Way…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
上行其相得而有合者孰非帝則之必察邪是
知道始於夫婦而不止於夫婦也察於天地而
不盡於天地也其用甚廣而其體則微大哉道
乎斯其至矣君子察於此於是乎有體道之
焉蓋道也者通於天地而實本於吾心者也夫
婦吾心之彝倫也鳶魚吾心之物理也天地聖
人吾心之統會也知道具於一心而動靜交相
為力則中和致而天地以位萬物以育裁成輔
相舉得之矣是故君子不求諸天地而求諸吾
===
心
心之所同然者何也謂理也義也聖人先
得我心之所同然耳故理義之悅我心
猶芻豢之悅我口
李鳴
同考試官教諭譚 批詞不繁而意已盡深得性善之
旨者
同考試官教諭鍾 批構思精密且無一贅詞宜錄以
式
punctuated:
上行，其相得而有合者，孰非帝則之必察邪？是知道始於夫婦，而不止於夫婦也；察於天地，而不盡於天地也。其用甚廣，而其體則微。大哉，道乎！斯其至矣。君子察於此，於是乎有體道之焉。蓋道也者，通於天地，而實本於吾心者也。夫婦，吾心之彝倫也；鳶魚，吾心之物理也；天地聖人，吾心之統會也。知道具於一心，而動靜交相為力，則中和致，而天地以位，萬物以育，裁成輔相，舉得之矣。是故君子不求諸天地，而求諸吾心。
心之所同然者何也？謂理也，義也。聖人先得我心之所同然耳。故理義之悅我心，猶芻豢之悅我口。
李鳴。
同考試官教諭譚批：詞不繁而意已盡，深得性善之旨者。
同考試官教諭鍾批：構思精密，且無一贅詞，宜錄以式。
translation_en:
…ascends. In their mutual accord and union, what does not make manifest the Supreme Lord’s norm? Thus we know that the Way begins with husband and wife but does not stop with husband and wife; it is manifest in Heaven and Earth but is not exhausted by Heaven and Earth. Its operation is exceedingly extensive, yet its substance is subtle. Great indeed is the Way! Here it reaches its utmost. The gentleman perceives this and thereby comes to embody the Way [?]. For the Way pervades Heaven and Earth, yet is truly rooted in my own heart. Husband and wife represent the constant human relationships within my heart; kites and fish, the principles of things within my heart; Heaven, Earth, and the sages, the comprehensive unity within my heart. Knowing that the Way is fully present in the single heart, and letting activity and stillness lend strength to one another, one brings equilibrium and harmony to their utmost: Heaven and Earth take their proper places, and the myriad things are nourished. Shaping and completing their transformations, assisting and supporting their workings—all are thereby accomplished. Thus the gentleman seeks it not in Heaven and Earth, but in his own heart.
“What is it that hearts alike approve? It is principle and rightness. The sages have simply apprehended before us what our hearts alike approve. Thus principle and rightness delight my heart just as the meat of grass-fed and grain-fed animals delights my palate.”
Li Ming.
Comment by Associate Examiner Tan, Instructor: “The wording is concise, yet the meaning is fully expressed. This deeply grasps the purport of the goodness of human nature.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhong, Instructor: “The conception is meticulous, and there is not a single superfluous phrase. It should be recorded as a model.”

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授蔣批切當
考試官敎授桂批簡而文
大賢深著人心好德之同以見性之善也蓋理
義之心人皆有之也卽其好德之同情而可以
識心矣且夫道原於性性統於心心也者妙衆
體而爲言者也惟口耳目尚有同者何獨至於
心而疑之心之所同然者何也理義之謂也夫
理寓於物者也而吾心之體具焉所以立天下
之有也夫義裁夫事者也而吾心之用行焉所
===
以效天下之動也斯二者皆降衷之恒性雖聖
人與人同也其知覺超乎庶類若非夫人之可
幾及而理義出於一原亦不過先得我心之所
同然者耳聖人何以異於人哉唯其取諸心而
至足故自悅諸心而無間心不與理義期而理
義自不能不契於吾心蓋有天機存焉不知理
義之美者無良心者也猶之口不與芻豢期而
芻豢自不能不嗜於吾口蓋有至味存焉不知
芻豢之美者不知味者也人同則心同心同則
punctuated:
考試官敎授蔣批：切當。
考試官敎授桂批：簡而文。

大賢深著人心好德之同，以見性之善也。蓋理義之心，人皆有之也。卽其好德之同情，而可以識心矣。且夫道原於性，性統於心。心也者，妙衆體而爲言者也。惟口耳目尚有同者，何獨至於心而疑之？心之所同然者何也？理義之謂也。夫理，寓於物者也，而吾心之體具焉，所以立天下之有也。夫義，裁夫事者也，而吾心之用行焉，所以效天下之動也。斯二者，皆降衷之恒性，雖聖人與人同也。其知覺超乎庶類，若非夫人之可幾及，而理義出於一原，亦不過先得我心之所同然者耳。聖人何以異於人哉？唯其取諸心而至足，故自悅諸心而無間。心不與理義期，而理義自不能不契於吾心，蓋有天機存焉。不知理義之美者，無良心者也。猶之口不與芻豢期，而芻豢自不能不嗜於吾口，蓋有至味存焉。不知芻豢之美者，不知味者也。人同則心同，心同則
translation_en:
Examiner Jiang, an Instructor, comments: “Precisely apt.”
Examiner Gui, an Instructor, comments: “Concise and elegant.”

The great worthy clearly reveals that human hearts share a love of virtue, thereby showing the goodness of human nature. All people possess a heart endowed with principle and righteousness. Through their shared disposition to love virtue, we can understand the heart. The Way originates in human nature, and human nature is governed by the heart. The term “heart” refers to that which wondrously unifies the various bodily faculties. Even mouths, ears, and eyes have something in common; why should we doubt this only when it comes to the heart? What is it that all hearts alike affirm? It is principle and righteousness. Principle inheres in things, yet it is fully present in the substance of my heart: it is that by which all existence under Heaven is established. Righteousness determines what is fitting in affairs, yet it operates through the functioning of my heart: it is that by which all activity under Heaven is brought into effect. These two are the constant nature bestowed by Heaven within us; even sages share them with other people. Sages’ understanding surpasses that of ordinary people, seemingly beyond anyone’s reach. Yet principle and righteousness issue from a single source, and sages have merely apprehended before us what our hearts alike affirm. How, then, are sages different from other people? Because what they draw from their hearts is utterly sufficient, their hearts naturally delight in it without interruption. The heart makes no appointment with principle and righteousness, yet principle and righteousness cannot but accord with my heart, for Heaven’s spontaneous workings reside within it. Those who do not recognize the beauty of principle and righteousness are without their good heart. Similarly, the mouth makes no appointment with the meat of grass-fed and grain-fed animals, yet such meat cannot but please my palate, for it possesses the finest flavor. Those who do not recognize the excellence of such meat do not understand flavor. Since people are alike, their hearts are alike; since their hearts are alike, then…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
悅同觀其所悅而心之所同然者明矣不然則
是心也何以能達之天下哉吁彼有陷溺其心
而顧於降才之殊是尤焉亦弗思耳矣雖然芻
豢者物也外也理義者管於心者也內也非外
也人有芻豢則知求之有理義而不知求此陷
溺之所由來也反而求之則窮理盡性精義入
神所以作聖者胥此矣人莫不飲食也鮮能知
味也知性者當自得之
易
===
元吉在上大有慶也
李畿嗣
同考試官教諭顧批履至上九乃履道之成
天人感應之妙也是作闡揚其義無餘蘊矣錄之
同考試官學正余批不襲陳言而詞理俱
足自中矩矱佳士佳士
考試官教授蔣批講大有慶處得旨
考試官教授桂批明暢
象傳舉履爻大善之極而深著其得天之佑也
punctuated:
悅同。觀其所悅，而心之所同然者明矣。不然，則是心也，何以能達之天下哉？吁！彼有陷溺其心，而顧於降才之殊是尤焉，亦弗思耳矣。雖然，芻豢者，物也，外也；理義者，管於心者也，內也，非外也。人有芻豢則知求之，有理義而不知求，此陷溺之所由來也。反而求之，則窮理盡性，精義入神，所以作聖者胥此矣。人莫不飲食也，鮮能知味也。知性者當自得之。

易

元吉在上，大有慶也。

李畿嗣

同考試官教諭顧批：「履至上九，乃履道之成，天人感應之妙也。是作闡揚其義無餘蘊矣，錄之。」

同考試官學正余批：「不襲陳言，而詞理俱足，自中矩矱。佳士！佳士！」

考試官教授蔣批：「講大有慶處得旨。」

考試官教授桂批：「明暢。」

象傳舉履爻大善之極，而深著其得天之佑也。
translation_en:
…their delight is the same. Observe what delights them, and what their hearts alike affirm becomes clear. Otherwise, how could this heart be common to everyone under Heaven? Alas! Some allow their hearts to become submerged and corrupted, yet blame differences in the capacities bestowed upon them. They simply fail to reflect. Nevertheless, grass-fed and grain-fed meats are material things, external to us; moral principle and righteousness belong to the heart: they are internal, not external. People know to seek these meats, yet do not know to seek the moral principle and righteousness they possess. This is the source of their hearts’ corruption. If they turn back and seek within themselves, they can investigate principle fully and fulfill their nature, refine their understanding of righteousness and enter the realm of the numinous. Everything by which one becomes a sage lies here. Everyone eats and drinks, but few can discern flavor. Those who understand human nature should realize this for themselves.

Book of Changes

“Supreme good fortune at the top: there is great cause for celebration.”

Li Jisi

Comment by Associate Examiner Gu, Instructor: “When Treading reaches the top nine, the Way of treading is complete: here is the wonder of the mutual response between Heaven and humanity. This composition expounds that meaning, leaving nothing unexplored. Include it.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, School Instructor: “Without borrowing hackneyed expressions, it is fully accomplished in both language and reasoning, and naturally meets the standards. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!”

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: “The discussion of ‘great cause for celebration’ captures the purport.”

Comment by Examiner Gui, Professor: “Clear and fluent.”

The Commentary on the Images cites the culmination of supreme goodness in the line of Treading and brings out profoundly how it receives Heaven’s aid.

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
蓋履道之成天人感應之機係之也上九旣會
大善之極矣則天之佑也豈其微哉象傳之意
蓋謂履之爲道也本諸已以大善爲極功徵諸
天以大順爲極致此視履之所期以自遂而不
可必得者玆惟爻至上九履已成矣履至其旋
善已極矣合衆善以成其行而德崇業廣之下
自足以上格乎天心聚百順以成其身而體信
達順之餘自可以永綏乎天命故始而曰吉可
以顯惠迪之應矣而尤益之元吉以申其命繼
===
而曰元吉可以彰大善之徵矣而尤要之在上
以昭其極則其慶之大爲何如哉蓋惟天顯道
而吾考道以爲無失則天命之寵綏者自獲乎
多福之懷惟天眷德而吾聚德以爲不回則上
帝之賚予者將出於自外之益保佑命之可以
言慶矣而又自天申之則嘉樂之休所以凝其
命於無疆者何其久而大也福履綏之可以言
慶矣而又勿替引之則申錫之祚所以貽其福
於無窮者何其遠而大也履而至是則吾之昭
punctuated: 蓋履道之成，天人感應之機係之也。上九旣會大善之極矣，則天之佑也，豈其微哉？象傳之意，蓋謂履之爲道也，本諸已，以大善爲極功；徵諸天，以大順爲極致。此視履之所期以自遂，而不可必得者。玆惟爻至上九，履已成矣；履至其旋，善已極矣。合衆善以成其行，而德崇業廣之下，自足以上格乎天心；聚百順以成其身，而體信達順之餘，自可以永綏乎天命。故始而曰「吉」，可以顯惠迪之應矣，而尤益之「元吉」，以申其命；繼而曰「元吉」，可以彰大善之徵矣，而尤要之「在上」，以昭其極。則其慶之大爲何如哉？蓋惟天顯道，而吾考道以爲無失，則天命之寵綏者，自獲乎多福之懷；惟天眷德，而吾聚德以爲不回，則上帝之賚予者，將出於自外之益。「保佑命之」，可以言慶矣，而又「自天申之」，則嘉樂之休，所以凝其命於無疆者，何其久而大也！「福履綏之」，可以言慶矣，而又「勿替引之」，則申錫之祚，所以貽其福於無窮者，何其遠而大也！履而至是，則吾之昭
translation_en: …For the completion of the way of conduct is where the workings of the mutual response between Heaven and humanity reside. Since the top nine has already brought together goodness in its highest perfection, could Heaven’s aid possibly be slight? The meaning of the Commentary on the Images is, in essence, that the way of conduct takes its foundation in oneself, with supreme goodness as its highest achievement, and finds its confirmation in Heaven, with supreme accord as its ultimate fulfillment. This is what one who examines one’s conduct hopes to attain for oneself, yet cannot be certain of obtaining. Now, when the lines reach the top nine, conduct is complete; when conduct comes full circle, goodness has reached its utmost. By bringing together every goodness to perfect one’s actions, one elevates virtue and broadens one’s accomplishments, thereby becoming fully able to reach Heaven’s heart above. By gathering every form of accord to perfect oneself, one embodies trustworthiness and attains harmony, thereby becoming able to rest forever secure in Heaven’s mandate. Thus, the initial statement, “auspicious,” suffices to reveal the response to following the Way; yet “supremely auspicious” is further added to reaffirm its pronouncement. The subsequent statement, “supremely auspicious,” suffices to manifest the evidence of supreme goodness; yet it is further qualified by “at the top,” to make clear its culmination. How great, then, must its blessings be! For Heaven makes the Way manifest, and if I examine the Way so as to remain without error, the favor and security bestowed by Heaven’s mandate will of themselves bring the embrace of abundant blessings. Heaven cherishes virtue, and if I accumulate virtue without deviation, the gifts of the Lord on High will bring an increase from beyond myself. “He protects, assists, and commands him” is already sufficient to speak of blessing; yet there is also “from Heaven he repeats it.” How enduring and great, then, is the favor celebrated in ‘Admirable Joy’ (Jia le), by which his mandate is secured without limit! “Blessings and good fortune bring him peace” is already sufficient to speak of blessing; yet there is also “without ceasing, he prolongs them.” How far-reaching and great, then, are these repeatedly bestowed blessings, by which good fortune is transmitted without end! When conduct reaches this point, then my radiant…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
格於天者已深而天之降祥於我者益隆履道
之成何以加此視履者盍求端於天哉抑嘗因
是而得天人之道矣爻之視履非求知於天也
爲履善之不可以已也天之垂慶非有私於人
也爲福善之不可以已也一善積而慶自集焉
乃知盡人足以合天而天之未始不爲人也是
故知天人之道者其知履之所爲乎
昔者聖人之作易也將以順性命之理是
以立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔
===
與剛立人之道曰仁與義兼三才而兩
之故易六畫而成卦分陰分陽迭用柔
剛故易六位而成章
董良遂
同考試官敎諭顧批此題作者類牽强成
文殊戾本旨潔淨精微此作得之
同考試官學正余批說出畫前有易意甚
分明其得先天之學者
考試官敎授蔣批發明性命之理殆盡
punctuated:
格於天者已深，而天之降祥於我者益隆。履道之成，何以加此？視履者盍求端於天哉？抑嘗因是而得天人之道矣。爻之視履，非求知於天也，爲履善之不可以已也；天之垂慶，非有私於人也，爲福善之不可以已也。一善積而慶自集焉，乃知盡人足以合天，而天之未始不爲人也。是故知天人之道者，其知履之所爲乎！
昔者聖人之作易也，將以順性命之理，是以立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。兼三才而兩之，故易六畫而成卦；分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，故易六位而成章。
董良遂
同考試官敎諭顧批：此題作者類牽强成文，殊戾本旨。潔淨精微，此作得之。
同考試官學正余批：說出畫前有易意甚分明，其得先天之學者。
考試官敎授蔣批：發明性命之理殆盡。
translation_en:
…has reached Heaven profoundly, and Heaven’s bestowal of auspicious blessings upon us grows ever more abundant. How could the fulfillment of the Way of Treading surpass this? Should those who examine their conduct not seek its source in Heaven? Indeed, through this I have come to understand the Way of Heaven and humanity. The line statement’s injunction to examine one’s conduct is not a matter of seeking recognition from Heaven: it is because one must never cease treading the path of goodness. Heaven’s bestowal of blessings is not a matter of partiality toward human beings: it is because Heaven never ceases to bless goodness. Once goodness accumulates, blessings gather of themselves. Thus we know that fully discharging human responsibilities suffices to accord with Heaven, and that Heaven has never failed to act on humanity’s behalf. Therefore, those who understand the Way of Heaven and humanity surely understand the purpose of Treading!
“In ancient times, when the sages made the Changes, they intended thereby to accord with the principles of human nature and destiny. Thus they established the Way of Heaven as yin and yang, the Way of Earth as yielding and firm, and the Way of humanity as benevolence and righteousness. They combined the Three Powers and doubled them; hence, in the Changes, six lines form a hexagram. They distinguished yin and yang and employed yielding and firm alternately; hence, in the Changes, the six positions form an ordered pattern.”
Dong Liangsui 董良遂
Comment by Associate Examiner Gu, Instructor: “Those who write on this topic generally force their arguments into an essay, greatly departing from its fundamental purport. Purity, refinement, subtlety, and precision—this essay achieves them.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, School Instructor: “The idea that the Changes existed before the lines were drawn is expressed very clearly. This is someone who has grasped the learning of Prior Heaven.”
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: “The principles of human nature and destiny are elucidated almost exhaustively.”

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授桂批精確
大傳原易有以闡乎性命因詳言以明之也夫
性命之理三才備矣卦爻即三才之道也謂易
非性命之奧乎夫子翼易之意蓋以易雖陳乎
法象之粗而義實該夫至理之奧昔者聖人之
作易非曰意為之也亦惟融性命於擬議之精
而發幽微於形器之顯立象盡意本順乎斯理
焉而已何者自天道之所以成象曰陰與陽而
靜專動直焉地道之所以成質曰柔與剛而靜
===
翕動闢焉人道之所以成德曰仁與義而慈愛
斷制焉斯固性命之分見於三才者也而何以
順之蓋聖人以三才皆以兩而成體而三畫不
足以備其體也於是兼三才而兩之貞悔全而
大小合故易六畫而成卦矣吾見五上以兩而
陰陽分也三四以兩而仁義明也初二以兩而
剛柔配也不亦統之而得性命之全乎又以三
才每相錯以為用而定畫不足以盡其用也於
是分陰分陽迭用柔剛爻有等而物相雜故易
punctuated:
考試官教授桂批：精確。
大傳原易有以闡乎性命，因詳言以明之也。夫性命之理，三才備矣；卦爻即三才之道也，謂易非性命之奧乎？夫子翼易之意，蓋以易雖陳乎法象之粗，而義實該夫至理之奧。昔者聖人之作易，非曰意為之也，亦惟融性命於擬議之精，而發幽微於形器之顯。立象盡意，本順乎斯理焉而已。何者？自天道之所以成象，曰陰與陽，而靜專動直焉；地道之所以成質，曰柔與剛，而靜翕動闢焉；人道之所以成德，曰仁與義，而慈愛斷制焉。斯固性命之分見於三才者也，而何以順之？蓋聖人以三才皆以兩而成體，而三畫不足以備其體也，於是兼三才而兩之，貞悔全而大小合，故易六畫而成卦矣。吾見五上以兩而陰陽分也，三四以兩而仁義明也，初二以兩而剛柔配也，不亦統之而得性命之全乎？又以三才每相錯以為用，而定畫不足以盡其用也，於是分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，爻有等而物相雜，故易
translation_en:
Examiner Gui, Professor, comments: “Precise and accurate.”

The Great Commentary traces the origins of the Changes to show how it elucidates human nature and destiny, and therefore explains this in detail. The principles of human nature and destiny are fully present in the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity. The hexagrams and their lines embody the Way of these Three Powers. Could one say that the Changes does not contain the profundities of human nature and destiny? The Master's purpose in supplementing the Changes was surely this: although the Changes sets forth the relatively coarse forms of patterns and images, its meaning encompasses the profundities of ultimate principle. When the sages of antiquity made the Changes, they did not devise it arbitrarily. Rather, they integrated human nature and destiny into the subtle work of comparison and deliberation, and disclosed what was hidden and subtle through manifest forms and concrete things. In establishing images to express their meaning fully, they were simply following this underlying principle.

Why is this so? That by which the Way of Heaven produces images is called yin and yang: in stillness it is concentrated, and in movement it proceeds directly. That by which the Way of Earth produces substance is called the yielding and the firm: in stillness it closes, and in movement it opens. That by which the Way of humanity produces virtue is called benevolence and righteousness: these manifest themselves in compassionate love and decisive judgment. These are indeed the distinct manifestations of human nature and destiny in the Three Powers. But how are they to be followed?

The sages considered that each of the Three Powers takes its complete form through a pair, and that three lines were insufficient to represent those forms fully. They therefore brought together the Three Powers and doubled them. The inner and outer trigrams were complete, and the small and great were united; thus, in the Changes, six lines make a hexagram. I see that the fifth and top lines form a pair through which yin and yang are distinguished; the third and fourth form a pair through which benevolence and righteousness are made clear; and the first and second form a pair through which the firm and yielding are matched. Is this not to bring them together and thereby grasp human nature and destiny in their entirety?

Moreover, the Three Powers constantly interweave in their operation, and fixed lines are insufficient to express that operation exhaustively. Thus yin and yang are distinguished, and the yielding and firm are employed alternately. The lines have their ranks, and things intermingle; therefore, in the Changes…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
六位而成章矣吾見五陽上陰而動靜交也三
仁四義而慈斷行也初剛二柔而翕闢時也不
亦扐之而盡性命之變乎是則非性命無以立
三才非易書無以順性命易其至矣乎夫是義
也得之河圖焉五位之合卽三才之兩也而其
相得卽剛柔之迭用也一而已矣然圖從中起
而三才之所以各一太極太極之所以流行於
三才不外是焉噫性命之原淵乎微矣
書
===
惟動丕應徯志以昭受上帝天其申命用
休
李鳴
同考試官教諭譚批講得天得民處詞莊
意切眞得古人告君之體
同考試官教諭鍾批詞意渾融于蓋善發
天人之蘊者
考試官教授蔣批思致精密
考試官教授桂批雋永可玩
punctuated:
六位而成章矣。吾見五陽上陰而動靜交也，三仁四義而慈斷行也，初剛二柔而翕闢時也。不亦扐之而盡性命之變乎？是則非性命無以立三才，非易書無以順性命，易其至矣乎！夫是義也，得之河圖焉。五位之合，卽三才之兩也；而其相得，卽剛柔之迭用也。一而已矣。然圖從中起，而三才之所以各一太極，太極之所以流行於三才，不外是焉。噫！性命之原，淵乎微矣！
書
「惟動丕應，徯志，以昭受上帝，天其申命用休。」
李鳴
同考試官教諭譚批：講得天得民處，詞莊意切，眞得古人告君之體。
同考試官教諭鍾批：詞意渾融，于蓋善發天人之蘊者。
考試官教授蔣批：思致精密。
考試官教授桂批：雋永可玩。
translation_en:
…the six positions thus form an ordered pattern. I see that the fifth position is yang and the topmost yin, so movement and stillness interact; the third is benevolence and the fourth righteousness, so compassion and decisiveness operate; the first is firm and the second yielding, so closing and opening occur at their proper times. Does this not also, by arranging them [?], exhaust the transformations of nature and destiny? Thus, without nature and destiny, there would be no means of establishing the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity; without the Book of Changes, there would be no means of following nature and destiny. How consummate the Changes is! This principle is found in the River Chart. The conjunction of the five positions is precisely the pairing within each of the Three Powers; their mutual accord is precisely the alternating operation of firmness and yielding. These are one and the same. Yet the Chart begins from its center: the reason each of the Three Powers embodies a Supreme Ultimate, and the reason the Supreme Ultimate circulates through the Three Powers, lie nowhere beyond this. Ah! How profound and subtle is the source of nature and destiny!
Book of Documents
“Whenever you act, [the people] respond fully, awaiting your intent; thereby you gloriously receive [the favor of] the Lord on High. Heaven will renew its mandate to you with blessings.”
Li Ming
Comment by Associate Examiner Tan, Instructor: In discussing how to win Heaven and win the people, the language is dignified and the meaning earnest. It truly captures the manner in which the ancients addressed their rulers.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhong, Instructor: The language and meaning are seamlessly integrated. [An unclear character follows: 于.] This is indeed a fine exposition of the profound workings of Heaven and humanity.
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: The thought is refined and precise.
Comment by Examiner Gui, Professor: Rich in lasting meaning and worthy of contemplation.

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
大臣告聖君欲其得民而得天也蓋君德與天
人相為感通者也夫旣慎厥位矣而得民得天
豈非理之所必至哉大禹陳謨于舜而推言至
此意蓋曰人君成位乎中上承天命而下係民
情者也夫苟內外交脩之至則其所感召者為
何如邪彼民罔常懷而丕從厥志者其情也今
惟出其慎脩者而著于動作之間則導之者為
盡善應之者為盡神動之而言也民莫不承聽
焉先意以迎之有不令而從者矣動之而行也
===
民莫不承順焉傾心以嚮之有不戒而孚者矣
是何也人之所助者信也君能信以發志而民
之順以從君也有不出于必然者乎天無常親
而惟德是與者其道也今惟本其慎脩者以凝
乎至顯之命則受之者非妄圖佑之者非私與
荷天之寵固陟此元后矣而保定之休自是垂
之於勿替焉享天之祜固奄有四海矣而純嘏
之錫自是申之於無疆焉是何也天之所助者
順也君能順以承天而天之眷命用懋也有不
punctuated: 大臣告聖君，欲其得民而得天也。蓋君德與天人相為感通者也。夫旣慎厥位矣，而得民得天，豈非理之所必至哉？大禹陳謨于舜，而推言至此，意蓋曰：人君成位乎中，上承天命而下係民情者也。夫苟內外交脩之至，則其所感召者為何如邪？彼民罔常懷而丕從厥志者，其情也。今惟出其慎脩者而著于動作之間，則導之者為盡善，應之者為盡神。動之而言也，民莫不承聽焉，先意以迎之，有不令而從者矣；動之而行也，民莫不承順焉，傾心以嚮之，有不戒而孚者矣。是何也？人之所助者信也。君能信以發志，而民之順以從君也，有不出于必然者乎？天無常親而惟德是與者，其道也。今惟本其慎脩者以凝乎至顯之命，則受之者非妄圖，佑之者非私與。荷天之寵，固陟此元后矣，而保定之休，自是垂之於勿替焉；享天之祜，固奄有四海矣，而純嘏之錫，自是申之於無疆焉。是何也？天之所助者順也。君能順以承天，而天之眷命用懋也，有不
translation_en:
The great minister, in admonishing the sage ruler, wished him to win the people and thereby win Heaven. For the ruler’s virtue moves Heaven and the people, and responds to them in turn. Once he has exercised care in his position, is winning the people and Heaven not the inevitable outcome of principle? When the Great Yu presented his counsels to Shun and extended his argument to this point, his meaning was this: the ruler occupies his position in the midst of Heaven and earth, receiving Heaven’s mandate above and holding the people’s affections below. If his inward cultivation and outward conduct are both perfected, what responses will he call forth?

The people cherish no one constantly, but follow wholeheartedly what accords with their own aspirations: such is their disposition. Now, if the ruler manifests his careful self-cultivation in his actions, the guidance he gives will be entirely good, and their response entirely wondrous. When he expresses himself in speech, all the people listen respectfully; anticipating his intentions, they comply even without an order. When he expresses himself in action, all the people follow obediently; turning toward him with all their hearts, they trust him even without an admonition. Why is this? Those whom people assist are the trustworthy. If the ruler expresses his intentions with sincerity, could the people’s obedient following of him be anything but inevitable?

Heaven has no constant favorite, but supports virtue alone: such is its way. Now, if the ruler grounds himself in careful self-cultivation to secure Heaven’s most manifest mandate, he receives it without presumptuous designs, and Heaven aids him without partial favor. Bearing Heaven’s favor, he has indeed ascended to the position of sovereign; henceforth, the blessing of its protection and stabilization will descend upon him without ceasing. Enjoying Heaven’s blessing, he has indeed come to possess all within the Four Seas; henceforth, the bestowal of its abundant blessings will be renewed without limit. Why is this? Those whom Heaven assists are those who accord with it. If the ruler accords with Heaven in serving it, and Heaven’s gracious mandate is thereby strengthened, could this fail to…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
出于必然者乎吁下而得民則君位以民心之
歸而益安上而得天則君位以天命之隆而益
固向非交修之力其何以致是哉抑聞之位在
德元則慎位者君之道當然耳乃禹猶推及于
天與人歸之盛豈亦取必于未然者乎蓋觀天
者觀之民觀民者觀我生者也天也人也己也
一理也感應一機也舜以玄德升聞而天下謳
歌朝覲訟獄者無不歸焉其得天民蓋固有之
也而禹實要其至焉耳豈徒托諸空言已邪以
===
是知天人相與之際古聖人所爲兢業而弗懈
者蓋深有見于是理矣
一曰食二曰貨三曰祀四曰司空五曰司
徒六曰司寇七曰賓八曰師
陳文燭
同考試官教諭譚 批敘次有法詞氣渾成
非徒經生組繪之談而已錄之
同考試官教諭鍾 批因天厚民之意發揮
殆盡誠非苟作者
punctuated:
出于必然者乎？吁！下而得民，則君位以民心之歸而益安；上而得天，則君位以天命之隆而益固。向非交修之力，其何以致是哉？抑聞之，位在德元，則慎位者，君之道當然耳。乃禹猶推及于天與人歸之盛，豈亦取必于未然者乎？蓋觀天者觀之民，觀民者觀我生者也。天也，人也，己也，一理也；感應，一機也。舜以玄德升聞，而天下謳歌、朝覲、訟獄者無不歸焉。其得天民，蓋固有之也，而禹實要其至焉耳，豈徒托諸空言已邪？以是知天人相與之際，古聖人所爲兢業而弗懈者，蓋深有見于是理矣。
一曰食，二曰貨，三曰祀，四曰司空，五曰司徒，六曰司寇，七曰賓，八曰師。
陳文燭
同考試官教諭譚批：敘次有法，詞氣渾成，非徒經生組繪之談而已，錄之。
同考試官教諭鍾批：因天厚民之意，發揮殆盡，誠非苟作者。
translation_en:
…could this fail to follow inevitably? Ah! Below, when the ruler wins the people, his position grows more secure as their hearts turn to him; above, when he wins Heaven, his position grows firmer through the fullness of Heaven’s mandate. Without the effort of cultivating both aspects, how could this have been achieved? Moreover, I have heard that the throne belongs to the foremost in virtue. Thus, taking care over his position is simply what the ruler’s Way requires. Yet Yu went further, speaking of the abundant support of Heaven and allegiance of the people. Was he seeking certainty about what had not yet happened? Those who would observe Heaven observe the people; those who would observe the people examine their own conduct. Heaven, the people, and oneself share a single principle; stimulus and response operate through a single mechanism. Shun’s profound virtue became known on high, and throughout the realm those who sang praises, attended court, or brought lawsuits all turned to him. He already possessed the support of Heaven and the people; Yu was merely urging him to bring this to its fullest realization. Could these have been mere empty words? From this we know that, in the mutual dealings of Heaven and humanity, the ancient sages remained vigilant and unremitting because they understood this principle deeply.
“First, food; second, goods; third, sacrifices; fourth, the Minister of Works; fifth, the Minister of Education; sixth, the Minister of Justice; seventh, guests; eighth, the army.”
Chen Wenzhu 陳文燭
Comment by Associate Examiner Tan, Instructor: “The exposition is methodically ordered, and its language and spirit form a harmonious whole. This is more than the ornamental discourse of a mere student of the Classics. Include it.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhong, Instructor: “The idea of following Heaven to enrich the people’s livelihood is developed almost exhaustively. This is certainly no carelessly composed work.”

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授蔣批詞理俱優
考試官敎授桂批語有典要
君子列八政之目以緩急而爲敘焉夫八政皆
所以厚民而其敘有緩急也知所先後斯可以
言治乎箕子陳洪範之疇而衍及于此意謂邦
本係乎民民生貴乎厚所謂農用八政者其目
維何食所以養生饑斯困矣則播時百穀以遂
其樂利之天者無不足也貨所以利用壅斯匱
矣則阜通五材以裕其貿遷之化者罔弗周也
===
是故食居一而貨卽次焉祀典不備何以敎敬
于是乎制三禮而禋五祀焉示天下萃渙之義
也司空不建何以奠居于是乎居四民而時地
利焉貽天下幹止之寧也是故祀居三而司空
又次焉由是而性有未復則利用敎乃立司徒
以掌敎焉敷典和則式訓于旣富之餘矣由是
而敎有或違則利用刑乃立司寇以掌刑焉明
罰敕法允防其姦暴之過矣玆二政者不居于
五與六乎禮不可廢而有交焉則立之賓晉接
punctuated:
考試官敎授蔣批：詞理俱優。
考試官敎授桂批：語有典要。
君子列八政之目，以緩急而爲敘焉。夫八政皆所以厚民，而其敘有緩急也。知所先後，斯可以言治乎！箕子陳洪範之疇，而衍及于此，意謂邦本係乎民，民生貴乎厚。所謂農用八政者，其目維何？食所以養生，饑斯困矣，則播時百穀，以遂其樂利之天者，無不足也。貨所以利用，壅斯匱矣，則阜通五材，以裕其貿遷之化者，罔弗周也。是故食居一，而貨卽次焉。祀典不備，何以敎敬？于是乎制三禮而禋五祀焉，示天下萃渙之義也。司空不建，何以奠居？于是乎居四民而時地利焉，貽天下幹止之寧也。是故祀居三，而司空又次焉。由是而性有未復，則利用敎，乃立司徒以掌敎焉，敷典和則，式訓于旣富之餘矣。由是而敎有或違，則利用刑，乃立司寇以掌刑焉，明罰敕法，允防其姦暴之過矣。玆二政者，不居于五與六乎？禮不可廢而有交焉，則立之賓，晉接
translation_en:
Examiner Jiang, an Instructor, comments: “Both the diction and the reasoning are excellent.”
Examiner Gui, an Instructor, comments: “The language has classical authority and captures the essentials.”
The gentleman enumerates the eight affairs of government, arranging them according to their relative urgency. All eight serve to enrich the people’s livelihood, but their order reflects differing degrees of urgency. Only when one knows what must come first and what should follow can one speak of governing! When Jizi set forth the categories of the Great Plan and elaborated on this point, his meaning was that the foundation of the state rests upon the people, and that what matters for their livelihood is abundance. What, then, are the items meant by “diligently employing the eight affairs of government”?
Food sustains life; hunger brings distress. Thus, sowing the various grains in their proper seasons fully provides for the people to fulfill their Heaven-given capacity for happiness and well-being. Goods supply practical needs; obstructed circulation brings scarcity. Thus, increasing the supply and circulation of the five materials fully provides for the beneficial transformations brought about by trade and exchange. Food therefore stands first, and goods immediately follow.
If the sacrificial ordinances are incomplete, how can reverence be taught? Hence the three rites are instituted and the five sacrifices reverently performed, showing all under Heaven the principles expressed in Gathering and Dispersion. If the office of Minister of Works is not established, how can people be securely settled? Hence the four classes of people are settled, and the resources of the land are used in their proper seasons, bequeathing to all under Heaven the peace of firm and settled dwellings. Sacrifices therefore stand third, and the Minister of Works comes next.
If, after this, people’s moral nature has not yet been restored, instruction is needed. The Minister of Education is therefore appointed to oversee instruction, promulgating the constant norms and harmonizing the standards, thereby teaching the people once they have become prosperous. If, after this, some still transgress those teachings, punishments are needed. The Minister of Justice is therefore appointed to oversee punishments, making penalties clear and putting the laws in order, truly guarding against offenses of wickedness and violence. Do these two affairs not occupy the fifth and sixth places?
Ritual propriety cannot be abandoned when there are relations with other states; thus the reception of guests is established, and their reception in audience…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之有儀懷柔之有道所以親邦國也勢不得已
而有伐焉則立之師不軌者必懲弗庭者有討
所以平邦國也玆二政者不居於七與八乎夫
八政之用緩急有敘如此人君次第舉之則民
生厚矣何皇極弗建而彝倫不敘哉大抵王政
之要在厚生食貨與居有生道焉教所以全其
生也祀賓以交神人濟其生也刑師以除不恪
衞其生也因天以成民而治道備矣然皇極者
八政之本也人君修德建極於其上而又命官
===
率屬以分理之治斯至矣故曰固邦本者尚平
政厚八政者本於極
詩
如跂斯翼如矢斯棘如鳥斯革如翬斯飛
君子攸躋
歐希稷
同考試官教諭陳 批創造規模形容親切
當時中興氣象宛然在目
同考試官教諭吳 批王制之壯麗未易以言
punctuated:
之有儀，懷柔之有道，所以親邦國也。勢不得已而有伐焉，則立之師，不軌者必懲，弗庭者有討，所以平邦國也。玆二政者不居於七與八乎？夫八政之用，緩急有敘如此，人君次第舉之，則民生厚矣，何皇極弗建而彝倫不敘哉？大抵王政之要在厚生，食貨與居有生道焉；教所以全其生也；祀賓以交神人，濟其生也；刑師以除不恪，衞其生也。因天以成民，而治道備矣。然皇極者，八政之本也。人君修德建極於其上，而又命官率屬以分理之，治斯至矣。故曰：「固邦本者尚平政，厚八政者本於極。」

詩
如跂斯翼，如矢斯棘，如鳥斯革，如翬斯飛，君子攸躋。
歐希稷
同考試官教諭陳批：創造規模，形容親切，當時中興氣象，宛然在目。
同考試官教諭吳批：王制之壯麗，未易以言

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
詩人取譬曲盡其美此作足以稱之
考試官教授蔣批閎廓莊嚴
考試官教授桂批正而葩
詩人形容其堂之美而王者之聽治在是矣蓋
王者之堂所以聽天下之治者也是宜其盡美
而詩人形容之也歟若曰吾王之作室固以繼
述爲孝尤以嚮明爲治堂者出治之所其在今
日則已成之矣而其美何如哉是故言乎其大
勢而中正之制得於辨方之餘者如人之跂而
===
翼焉何嚴正也言乎其廉隅而畫一之規成於
繩直之后者如矢之棘而直焉何整飭也以棟
宇尚其隆則其崇高而峻起者巍乎其不可踰
已不有如鳥之警而革邪以簷阿尚其文則其
華采而軒翔者煥乎其不容掩已不有如翬之
飛而矯其翼邪夫堂之盡美如此寧非君子之
攸躋者乎吾見其正位以凝命也一人出天下
之政其宅中而圖大也朝廷立四方之極以臨
百官而百官於是乎承式焉上下於庭所以揚
punctuated:
詩人取譬，曲盡其美，此作足以稱之。
考試官教授蔣批：閎廓莊嚴。
考試官教授桂批：正而葩。
詩人形容其堂之美，而王者之聽治在是矣。蓋王者之堂，所以聽天下之治者也，是宜其盡美而詩人形容之也歟！若曰：吾王之作室，固以繼述爲孝，尤以嚮明爲治。堂者，出治之所，其在今日則已成之矣，而其美何如哉？是故言乎其大勢，而中正之制得於辨方之餘者，如人之跂而翼焉，何嚴正也！言乎其廉隅，而畫一之規成於繩直之后者，如矢之棘而直焉，何整飭也！以棟宇尚其隆，則其崇高而峻起者，巍乎其不可踰已，不有如鳥之警而革邪？以簷阿尚其文，則其華采而軒翔者，煥乎其不容掩已，不有如翬之飛而矯其翼邪？夫堂之盡美如此，寧非君子之攸躋者乎？吾見其正位以凝命也，一人出天下之政；其宅中而圖大也，朝廷立四方之極。以臨百官，而百官於是乎承式焉；上下於庭，所以揚
translation_en:
…The poet employs comparisons that fully convey its beauty; this composition does justice to them.
Examiner Jiang, Professor, comments: Expansive and solemn.
Examiner Gui, Professor, comments: Correct yet richly ornamented.
The poet describes the beauty of the hall, and it is here that the king attends to government. The king’s hall is the place where he attends to the governance of all under Heaven. Surely it is fitting that it should be perfectly beautiful and that the poet should describe it!
It is as though he were saying: In building his palace, our king certainly expresses filial devotion by carrying forward his predecessors’ undertakings; above all, he governs by facing the light. The hall is the place from which government issues. Now that it has been completed, what is its beauty like? Speaking of its overall form, its balanced and upright design, achieved after the cardinal directions were determined, resembles a man rising on tiptoe with arms outspread. How imposing and correct! Speaking of its edges and corners, its uniform proportions, established by the straight measuring cord, resemble the straight shaft of an arrow. How orderly! If we prize the height of its ridgepole and roof, they soar steeply upward, so lofty that nothing can surpass them. Is this not like a bird alert and spreading its wings? If we prize the ornament of its eaves and roof curves, their brilliant colors and soaring forms shine with a splendor that cannot be concealed. Is this not like a pheasant in flight, lifting its wings?
With the hall so perfect in its beauty, is it not indeed the place to which the lord ascends? I see him take his proper position and make Heaven’s mandate secure: the One Man issues policies for all under Heaven. He occupies the center and plans great undertakings: the court establishes the standard for the four quarters. Here he presides over the hundred officials, and here they receive their model. Moving up and down within the court, thereby to proclaim…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
底法之訓而成端拱之休者咸與維新矣以統
萬民而萬民於是乎具瞻焉南面而治所以修
肯構之道而致垂衣之化者此爲之所矣是其
堂之美也而豈徒哉吁君子是以知宣王之能
率祖攸行也昔者洛邑之成也而召公之告成
王必曰我受天命丕若有夏歷年式勿替有殷
歷年欲王以小民受天永命夫有周作大邑者
非棘其欲也固將以圖治而受命也然則宣王
之肯堂由繼先言之則子道盡矣由勤民言之
===
則君道盡矣其王業中興而祈天永命也宜哉
噫王可謂丕承先烈者矣
虎拜稽首天子萬年
胡鶴來
同考試官教諭陳 批語和而莊召公報稱
之意溢於言外是深於詩者
同考試官教諭吳 批詞意懇至體制謹嚴
足稱善頌矣
考試官教授蔣 批忠愛之意藹然
punctuated:
底法之訓，而成端拱之休者，咸與維新矣。以統萬民，而萬民於是乎具瞻焉；南面而治，所以修肯構之道而致垂衣之化者，此爲之所矣。是其堂之美也，而豈徒哉！吁！君子是以知宣王之能率祖攸行也。昔者洛邑之成也，而召公之告成王必曰：「我受天命，丕若有夏歷年，式勿替有殷歷年。」欲王以小民受天永命。夫有周作大邑者，非棘其欲也，固將以圖治而受命也。然則宣王之肯堂，由繼先言之，則子道盡矣；由勤民言之，則君道盡矣。其王業中興而祈天永命也，宜哉！噫！王可謂丕承先烈者矣。

虎拜稽首，天子萬年。
胡鶴來

同考試官教諭陳批：語和而莊，召公報稱之意溢於言外，是深於詩者。
同考試官教諭吳批：詞意懇至，體制謹嚴，足稱善頌矣。
考試官教授蔣批：忠愛之意藹然。
translation_en:
…the instructions for upholding the statutes and bring about the blessings of a ruler who sits with hands folded—all participate in the renewal. He presides over the myriad people, and here they all look up to him. Facing south, he governs: this is the place where he carries forward the work of building begun by his forebears and brings about the transforming influence of a ruler who merely lets his robes hang down. Such is the excellence of his hall: could it be merely ornamental? Ah! From this the gentleman knows that King Xuan could follow the path of his ancestors. Formerly, when Luoyi was completed, the Duke of Shao admonished King Cheng in these terms: “Having received Heaven’s Mandate, let us fully match the years of Xia, and certainly not fall short of the years of Yin.” He wished the king, through care for the common people, to receive Heaven’s enduring Mandate. When Zhou built its great city, it was not to hasten the gratification of its desires [?], but assuredly to pursue good government and receive the Mandate. Thus, in King Xuan’s willingness to build the hall, considered as continuing his forebears’ work, he fully discharged the duties of a son; considered as diligent care for the people, he fully discharged the duties of a ruler. How fitting that he revived the royal enterprise and sought Heaven’s enduring Mandate! Ah! The king may indeed be said to have splendidly carried forward his forebears’ achievements.

“Hu bowed and knocked his head to the ground: ‘May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years!’”
Hu Helai

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The language is harmonious yet solemn. The Duke of Shao’s wish to repay the sovereign’s favor finds expression beyond the words themselves. This is someone with a profound understanding of the Book of Odes.”
