Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “The language and sentiments are deeply sincere, and the form is disciplined and rigorous. It well deserves to be called an excellent eulogy.”

Examiner Jiang, Professor, comments: “A spirit of loyalty and affection is abundantly evident.”

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授桂批〔疏鬯舂容〕
大臣拜命而欲壽其君以所感者深也夫壽君
之心固不待於有感大臣承寵命而祝之以萬
年也充其情之不能自已者乎昔者召虎經營
平僭亂於江漢天王錫祉隆寵命於岐周夫是
舉也圭瓚秬鬯之釐祀可崇其先祖而山川土
田之錫傳遂及之後人虎也覩王命之在前將
侈之爲不世之遇榮無以尚矣而敢不拜嘉乎
儼天顏於咫尺蓋持之以如臨之心禮不敢越
===
也於是而稽首焉人臣受恩無可以報謝者但
曰天子萬年而已矣蓋王者端拱於上惟以高
朗令終爲福而人臣願獻於君亦以永錫難老
爲忠其必天佑良而王躬是保所以出禮樂征
伐於天下者萬年歷有道之長而後帝嘏始純
也舎是若諸福之物則君之餘爾而又何加焉
天篤周而歷數爾常所以修田獵會同於諸侯
者四國仰無疆之慶而後臣心始愜也外此如
可致之祥皆足以供之而又何尚邪君念勳而
punctuated:
考試官敎授桂批〔疏鬯舂容〕。

大臣拜命而欲壽其君，以所感者深也。夫壽君之心，固不待於有感。大臣承寵命而祝之以萬年也，充其情之不能自已者乎？昔者召虎經營，平僭亂於江漢；天王錫祉，隆寵命於岐周。夫是舉也，圭瓚秬鬯之釐，祀可崇其先祖；而山川土田之錫，傳遂及之後人。虎也覩王命之在前，將侈之爲不世之遇，榮無以尚矣，而敢不拜嘉乎？儼天顏於咫尺，蓋持之以如臨之心，禮不敢越也。於是而稽首焉。人臣受恩，無可以報謝者，但曰「天子萬年」而已矣。蓋王者端拱於上，惟以高朗令終爲福；而人臣願獻於君，亦以永錫難老爲忠。其必天佑良而王躬是保，所以出禮樂征伐於天下者，萬年歷有道之長，而後帝嘏始純也。舎是，若諸福之物，則君之餘爾，而又何加焉？天篤周而歷數爾常，所以修田獵會同於諸侯者，四國仰無疆之慶，而後臣心始愜也。外此，如可致之祥，皆足以供之，而又何尚邪？君念勳而
translation_en:
Examiner Gui, an Instructor, comments: 〔Lucid and flowing, measured and ample.〕

That a great minister bows upon receiving his appointment and wishes his lord long life arises from the depth of his feelings. Indeed, the wish that his lord live long does not depend upon any particular occasion stirring him. Yet when a great minister receives a gracious command and wishes his lord ten thousand years, is he not giving full expression to feelings he cannot restrain?

Formerly, Shao Hu conducted his campaigns and quelled usurpation and disorder in the Jiang and Han region; the Heavenly King bestowed blessings and honored him with a gracious command at Qizhou. On this occasion, the gifts of a jade libation ladle and black-millet sacrificial wine enabled him to honor his ancestors more highly in sacrifice, while the grant of mountains, rivers, and lands would pass down to his descendants. Seeing the royal command before him, Hu would surely regard it as an encounter with royal favor such as comes but once in many generations. No honor could surpass it: how could he dare fail to bow in gratitude? Reverently envisioning the royal countenance close at hand, he maintained the attitude of one standing in the king’s presence and dared not overstep ritual propriety. Thus he bowed his head to the ground. A subject who has received such favor has nothing with which to repay it or express his thanks; he can only say, “May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years!”

For a king, seated upright above with hands folded, blessing consists solely in a lofty, enlightened life and a good end. Likewise, a subject wishing to make an offering to his lord expresses his loyalty by wishing him enduring freedom from the infirmities of age. Only when Heaven aids the good and protects the king’s person, so that he who issues commands concerning rites, music, and punitive expeditions throughout the realm enjoys ten thousand years of enduring, principled rule, are the blessings of the Lord on High complete. Apart from this, the various objects accounted blessings are merely things the ruler has in abundance: what could they add?

When Heaven deals generously with Zhou and makes its allotted succession enduring [?], so that the ruler who conducts the hunts and assemblies among the feudal lords brings boundless felicity for the states of all four quarters to look up to, only then is the minister’s heart satisfied. Beyond this, whatever auspicious things may be procured can all readily be supplied to him: what further value would they have? The ruler remembers meritorious service and…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
寵其臣臣受賜而祝其君上下交相愛也如此
周之治所以不可及歟抑因是而知穆公忠愛
之心無有已也夫萬年之壽惟一人之德可以
當之而萬年之治亦惟一人之德可以成之也
公之勸君也欲其令聞不已而洽四國以文德
焉其明保治之基乎夫其身本以武功獲懋賞
而保治永圖乃欲於文德取之豈謀身不及謀
國哉君子於是知古人愛君之心之無已也
春秋
===
秋九月齊侯宋公江人黃人盟于貫〔僖公二年〕
陳謨
同考試官教諭朱 批經意專在服楚與國見桓公伯業慮周義著不分對是
考試官教授蔣 批得春秋予齊桓意
考試官教授桂 批雅健
伯主服遠以孤外勢春秋特詞以予之也此貫
澤之盟齊桓服江黃以制楚也其慮周而義著
punctuated:
寵其臣，臣受賜而祝其君，上下交相愛也如此，周之治所以不可及歟！抑因是而知穆公忠愛之心無有已也。夫萬年之壽，惟一人之德可以當之；而萬年之治，亦惟一人之德可以成之也。公之勸君也，欲其令聞不已，而洽四國以文德焉，其明保治之基乎！夫其身本以武功獲懋賞，而保治永圖，乃欲於文德取之，豈謀身不及謀國哉！君子於是知古人愛君之心之無已也。

春秋

秋九月，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人盟于貫。〔僖公二年〕
陳謨

同考試官教諭朱批：經意專在服楚與國，見桓公伯業慮周義著，不分對是。
考試官教授蔣批：得春秋予齊桓意。
考試官教授桂批：雅健。

伯主服遠以孤外勢，春秋特詞以予之也。此貫澤之盟，齊桓服江黃以制楚也，其慮周而義著
translation_en:
…bestows favor upon his ministers, and the ministers, receiving his gifts, invoke blessings upon their ruler. Such was the mutual affection between those above and those below: was this not why Zhou’s governance could not be equaled? From this, moreover, we recognize that Duke Mu’s loyal affection knew no end. Only the virtue of the One Man can merit a lifespan of ten thousand years; likewise, only the virtue of the One Man can bring about ten thousand years of good government. In exhorting his ruler, the duke wished his good reputation never to cease and his civil virtue to reach throughout the four quarters. Was this not the foundation for wisely preserving good government? He himself had originally received lavish rewards for military achievements, yet for the enduring preservation of good government he sought a basis in civil virtue. Could his planning for himself have fallen short of his planning for the state? Here the gentleman recognizes that the ancients’ love for their ruler knew no end.

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In autumn, in the ninth month, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and men of Jiang and Huang made a covenant at Guan.” 〔Second year of Duke Xi〕
By Chen Mo.

Associate Examiner Zhu, an Instructor, comments: “The classic’s meaning lies specifically in bringing Chu’s allied states into submission, revealing the thoroughness of Duke Huan’s planning and the manifest righteousness of his hegemonic enterprise. It is right not to divide the treatment into paired sections [?].”
Examiner Jiang, a Professor, comments: “Captures the Spring and Autumn Annals’ intent in commending Duke Huan of Qi.”
Examiner Gui, a Professor, comments: “Elegant and vigorous.”

The hegemon brought distant states into submission in order to isolate an external power, and the Spring and Autumn Annals employs special wording to commend him. This covenant at Guanze was how Duke Huan of Qi brought Jiang and Huang into submission in order to check Chu. His planning was thorough and his righteousness manifest…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
矣君子是以許之且江黃者何荆楚之與國也
齊胡為而盟之邪桓自北杏創伯以來日以安
攘為事使楚之黨與未離即齊之計謀弗審也
楚何由制幸而桓也有見於此以為伐彊以遠
交為事馭敵以制勝為先於是約誓以申其詞
用合諸侯之眾招徠以携其黨預為撓楚之權
而江黃服焉君子曰是役也二國之從楚已失
其右臂矣友邦之附齊固得其先聲也則是今
日服遠之謀謂非他日勝楚之績歟自是盟好
===
既定或用之為掎正之分或資之為掎角之圖
而計出于萬全矣桓之所以帖遠謀大者其慮
不亦周乎厥後威惠竝著楚人輸納款之忠斯
民免左衽之患而功成於一匡矣桓之所以安
夏攘夷者其義不已著乎故聖人謂齊桓之成
伯也荆楚之屈服也先定于及江黃之一舉獨
言遠國者許是盟也其諸武王誓師牧野遠及
庸蜀彭濮八國之勢歟此可見功莫大於攘夷
謀當先於服遠桓之伯業斯為盛矣抑有憾焉
punctuated: 矣。君子是以許之。且江黃者何？荆楚之與國也。齊胡為而盟之邪？桓自北杏創伯以來，日以安攘為事。使楚之黨與未離，即齊之計謀弗審也，楚何由制？幸而桓也有見於此，以為伐彊以遠交為事，馭敵以制勝為先。於是約誓以申其詞，用合諸侯之眾；招徠以携其黨，預為撓楚之權，而江黃服焉。君子曰：是役也，二國之從，楚已失其右臂矣；友邦之附，齊固得其先聲也。則是今日服遠之謀，謂非他日勝楚之績歟？自是盟好既定，或用之為掎正之分，或資之為掎角之圖，而計出于萬全矣。桓之所以帖遠謀大者，其慮不亦周乎？厥後威惠竝著，楚人輸納款之忠，斯民免左衽之患，而功成於一匡矣。桓之所以安夏攘夷者，其義不已著乎？故聖人謂齊桓之成伯也，荆楚之屈服也，先定于及江黃之一舉。獨言遠國者，許是盟也。其諸武王誓師牧野，遠及庸蜀彭濮八國之勢歟？此可見功莫大於攘夷，謀當先於服遠。桓之伯業斯為盛矣。抑有憾焉。
translation_en:
…Thus the gentleman approves of him. Now, what were Jiang and Huang? They were allied states of Jing-Chu. Why, then, did Qi enter into a covenant with them? Ever since Duke Huan established his hegemony at Beixing, he had devoted himself daily to securing the central states and repelling outsiders. If Chu’s allies had remained attached to it, Qi’s planning would have lacked careful consideration: how could Chu have been brought under control? Fortunately, Duke Huan understood this. He held that attacking a powerful state required cultivating distant allies, and that managing an enemy required first securing the means of victory. Accordingly, he solemnized his declarations through covenants and oaths, thereby bringing together the forces of the feudal lords. He enticed Chu’s allies away, preparing in advance a means of weakening Chu, and Jiang and Huang submitted.

The gentleman says: In this undertaking, once the two states followed Qi, Chu had already lost its right arm. With friendly states attaching themselves to it, Qi had certainly gained a reputation that would precede its advance. Could this plan for winning over distant states today be said not to constitute an achievement contributing to the later victory over Chu? Once these friendly covenants were established, the allies could be assigned roles in pinning down the enemy and attacking directly [?], or employed in a plan for coordinated attacks from different directions. The planning thus provided for every contingency. In pacifying distant states and planning great undertakings, was Duke Huan’s foresight not comprehensive?

Afterward, his might and beneficence were both made manifest. The people of Chu offered sincere submission, the people of the central states escaped the calamity of wearing their robes fastened on the left, and his achievement of setting the realm to rights was complete. In securing the Xia states and repelling the non-Chinese peoples, was Duke Huan’s righteousness not already manifest? Thus the Sage held that Duke Huan of Qi’s attainment of hegemony and Jing-Chu’s submission had been determined in advance by this single act of extending the covenant to Jiang and Huang. His express mention of the distant states signifies approval of this covenant. Was this perhaps comparable to the strength assembled when King Wu swore an oath before his troops at Muye, reaching as far as the eight states that included Yong, Shu, Peng, and Pu? From this we can see that no achievement is greater than repelling outsiders, and that planning should begin by winning over distant states. In this, Duke Huan’s hegemonic enterprise reached its height. Yet there was cause for regret.

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
江黃從齊其志可嘉矣奈之何爲義不終楚人
伐之而齊弗救君子固深閔之也管敬仲曰江
黃遠齊而近楚楚爲利之國也伐不能救則無
以宗諸侯仲固逆知之矣然則爲二國之謀者
其亦不幸也夫
冬楚子蔡侯陳侯許男頓子沈子徐人越
人伐吳昭公五年夏曹公孫會自鄭
出奔宋昭公二十年
劉方
===
同考試官教諭朱批措詞莊重能融會傳
中重世類意春秋義當如此
考試官教授蔣批能發明聖人善善長之旨
考試官教授桂批峻潔
春秋論世進人也有因從兵以義者有因去國
以禮者此見越與曹會皆聖賢之後也春秋因
事各致意於書法之間有以夫吳處慶封楚人
執而殺之入棘櫟麻以報朱方狄道也兆龜告
吉楚於是有羅汭之師則比吳爲善而師亦有
punctuated:
江黃從齊，其志可嘉矣。奈之何爲義不終，楚人伐之而齊弗救？君子固深閔之也。管敬仲曰：「江黃遠齊而近楚，楚爲利之國也，伐不能救，則無以宗諸侯。」仲固逆知之矣。然則爲二國之謀者，其亦不幸也夫！
「冬，楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、許男、頓子、沈子、徐人、越人伐吳。」昭公五年。「夏，曹公孫會自鄭出奔宋。」昭公二十年。
劉方
同考試官教諭朱批：措詞莊重，能融會傳中重世類意，春秋義當如此。
考試官教授蔣批：能發明聖人善善長之旨。
考試官教授桂批：峻潔。
春秋論世進人也，有因從兵以義者，有因去國以禮者。此見越與曹會皆聖賢之後也。春秋因事各致意於書法之間，有以夫！吳處慶封，楚人執而殺之；入棘櫟麻以報朱方，狄道也。兆龜告吉，楚於是有羅汭之師，則比吳爲善，而師亦有
translation_en:
…Jiang and Huang followed Qi, and their intentions were praiseworthy. Why, then, did Qi fail to carry its righteous undertaking through to the end, leaving them unaided when Chu attacked? The gentleman indeed deeply deplores this. Guan Jingzhong said: “Jiang and Huang are distant from Qi but close to Chu. Chu is a state that pursues advantage. If they are attacked and we cannot rescue them, we shall have no means of acting as leader of the feudal lords.” Jingzhong had indeed foreseen this. Those who devised the policy for the two states were thus unfortunate indeed!
“In winter, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Chen, the Baron of Xu 許, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Shen, and men of Xu 徐 and Yue attacked Wu.” Fifth year of Duke Zhao. “In summer, Gongsun Hui of Cao fled from Zheng to Song.” Twentieth year of Duke Zhao.
Liu Fang 劉方
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “The phrasing is dignified and successfully integrates the Commentary’s concern for ancestral lineage. Interpretations of the Spring and Autumn Annals should be like this.”
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: “It successfully elucidates the Sage’s intention to praise goodness and extend that praise to descendants.”
Comment by Examiner Gui, Professor: “Forceful and concise.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals considers ancestry when according people higher standing: some receive this recognition because they join a military expedition in accordance with righteousness, others because they leave their state in accordance with ritual propriety. Here we see that Yue and Hui of Cao were both descended from sages and worthies. In each case, the Spring and Autumn Annals conveys its meaning through its manner of recording the event, and with good reason! Wu had given Qing Feng a place to settle, and the men of Chu seized and killed him. To invade Ji, Li, and Ma [?] in retaliation for Zhufang was the way of the barbarians. The tortoise-shell divination gave an auspicious omen, and Chu thereupon undertook the campaign at Luorui. Compared with Wu, it was acting well, and its campaign also had…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
名矣玆越也修我戈矛與子同仇其從兵也是
爲得宜噫越何人哉大禹之後也元德顯功通
于周室君子安可以後世之夷而累上世之夏
故與徐皆得稱人者蓋進越而思禹也美哉禹
功明德遠矣會爲公孫曹伯惡而逐之待罪於
境以承君命臣道也賜玦則去會於是有自鄭
之行則放而後出視君有體貌矣玆奔也善則
稱君過則歸己其去國也是爲得禮噫會何人
哉子臧之後也能以國讓不取乎爲諸侯君子
===
何幸有後人之賢而益光前人之美其曰公孫
自鄭蓋善臧以及會也卓哉子臧達節著矣此
見聖人取善之公延賞之厚其義大矣哉抑無
瑕者可以戮人楚之虔猶齊之封也其何以徇
於諸侯子臧之賢公孫會逐焉爲善者懼矣曹
伯之手足腹心安在哉是故正己以率人褒賢
以風後君子御世之善物也噫可不慎歟
禮記
樂者心之動也聲者樂之象也文采節奏
punctuated:
名矣。玆越也，修我戈矛，與子同仇，其從兵也，是爲得宜。噫！越何人哉？大禹之後也。元德顯功，通于周室，君子安可以後世之夷而累上世之夏？故與徐皆得稱人者，蓋進越而思禹也。美哉！禹功明德遠矣！會爲公孫，曹伯惡而逐之，待罪於境，以承君命，臣道也。賜玦則去，會於是有自鄭之行，則放而後出，視君有體貌矣。玆奔也，善則稱君，過則歸己，其去國也，是爲得禮。噫！會何人哉？子臧之後也。能以國讓，不取乎爲諸侯，君子何幸有後人之賢，而益光前人之美！其曰「公孫」「自鄭」，蓋善臧以及會也。卓哉！子臧達節著矣！此見聖人取善之公，延賞之厚，其義大矣哉！抑無瑕者可以戮人，楚之虔猶齊之封也，其何以徇於諸侯？子臧之賢，公孫會逐焉，爲善者懼矣。曹伯之手足腹心安在哉？是故正己以率人，褒賢以風後，君子御世之善物也。噫！可不慎歟？

禮記

樂者，心之動也；聲者，樂之象也；文采節奏
translation_en:
…had legitimate grounds. Here Yue “made ready our dagger-axes and spears, sharing your enmity”: its participation in the campaign was fitting. Ah! Who were the people of Yue? Descendants of Yu the Great. His supreme virtue and illustrious achievements reached down to the house of Zhou. How could the gentleman allow the barbarian status of later generations to tarnish the civilized status of their ancestors? Thus, when Yue and Xu are both accorded the designation “men,” this elevates Yue out of remembrance of Yu. How splendid! Far-reaching indeed are Yu’s achievements and luminous virtue!

Hui was a ducal grandson. The Earl of Cao disliked him and drove him out, but he awaited punishment at the border, ready to receive his lord’s command: this was the proper way of a minister. Only when presented with a jade ring signifying severance would he depart. Hui’s journey “from Zheng” thus followed his banishment; he left only after being expelled, treating his lord with due respect. In this flight, he attributed good to his lord and took blame upon himself. His departure from the state therefore conformed to ritual propriety. Ah! Who was Hui? A descendant of Zizang, who could yield possession of a state and decline to become a feudal lord. How fortunate the gentleman is when a worthy descendant adds further lustre to an ancestor’s excellence! The wording “ducal grandson” and “from Zheng” extends approval of Zizang to Hui. How outstanding! Zizang’s discerning observance of moral principle is manifest!

Here we see the Sage’s impartiality in recognizing goodness and his generosity in extending commendation to descendants. How great is the significance of this! Yet only one without blemish may punish others. Qian of Chu was like Feng of Qi: on what grounds could he make a punitive example of him before the feudal lords? Despite Zizang’s worthiness, his descendant, the ducal grandson Hui, was expelled; those who do good have cause for fear. Where were the Earl of Cao’s trusted servants, his hands and feet, his heart and belly? Thus, rectifying oneself to lead others, and commending the worthy to influence later generations, are excellent means by which the gentleman governs the world. Ah! Can one fail to exercise care?

Book of Rites

“Music is the movement of the heart; sound is the manifestation of music; embellishment and rhythm…”

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
聲之飾也君子動其本樂其象然後治
其飾
范宗鎮
同考試官教諭黃批言樂則人人能之若順
理成章不失和平之體此其先鳴者
考試官教授蔣批不費詞而意自足
考試官教授桂批典雅
記者備舉樂之所由成因著君子立樂之方也
夫有本有文樂之成也本立而文從之樂之能
===
事畢矣記者之意若曰樂不可以偽為君子為
能知樂何以言之比諸器之謂樂樂非滯於器
也流通於心者也蓋人心涵聲氣之元因感而
動者因樂而宣矣播諸言之謂聲聲非止於言
也具體乎樂者也蓋人聲極高下之變發言為
聲者成象為樂矣及夫著而為文采合而為節
奏凡以盡飾也夫豈徒飾者哉蓋動容以盡其
變從律以和其聲所謂比物飾節者在是矣夫
樂生於心而聲和於樂君子脩此三者故全也
punctuated:
聲之飾也，君子動其本，樂其象，然後治其飾。
范宗鎮
同考試官教諭黃批：言樂則人人能之，若順理成章，不失和平之體，此其先鳴者。
考試官教授蔣批：不費詞而意自足。
考試官教授桂批：典雅。
記者備舉樂之所由成，因著君子立樂之方也。夫有本有文，樂之成也；本立而文從之，樂之能事畢矣。記者之意若曰：樂不可以偽為，君子為能知樂。何以言之？比諸器之謂樂，樂非滯於器也，流通於心者也。蓋人心涵聲氣之元，因感而動者，因樂而宣矣。播諸言之謂聲，聲非止於言也，具體乎樂者也。蓋人聲極高下之變，發言為聲者，成象為樂矣。及夫著而為文采，合而為節奏，凡以盡飾也。夫豈徒飾者哉？蓋動容以盡其變，從律以和其聲，所謂比物飾節者在是矣。夫樂生於心，而聲和於樂，君子脩此三者，故全也。
translation_en:
…are the embellishments of sound. The gentleman stirs music’s root, delights in its manifestation, and only then attends to its embellishments.

Fan Zongzhen

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: Anyone can discuss music. But when it comes to following principle and producing a coherent composition without losing the character of harmony and balance, this is a leading example.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: Without wasting words, it fully conveys its meaning.

Comment by Examiner Gui, Professor: Refined and elegant.

The compiler of the Record comprehensively sets out what brings music into being, thereby revealing the gentleman’s method of establishing music. Music is complete when it has both a root and ornamentation. Once the root is established and ornamentation follows, music’s full capabilities are realized. The compiler’s meaning seems to be this: music cannot be produced through pretence; it is the gentleman who can understand music. How can this be explained? Bringing instruments into accord is called music, yet music is not confined to instruments: it flows through the heart. The human heart contains the source of sound and vital breath; what stirs in response to external influences finds expression through music. Giving expression in words is called sound, yet sound does not stop at words: it takes concrete form in music. The human voice encompasses the full range of variations in pitch; what becomes sound through utterance takes shape as music. When this is displayed as patterned embellishment and coordinated as rhythm, all serves to perfect its adornment. Yet is it merely adornment? Movements and gestures fully express its variations, while conformity to the pitch standards harmonizes its sounds. Herein lies what is meant by coordinating things and embellishing their measures. Music arises in the heart, and sound accords with music. The gentleman cultivates these three aspects, and thus achieves completeness.

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
然其序惡可亂乎彼知心爲樂之本也則慎其
所感而性術於是乎形焉其心和矣知聲爲樂
之象也則慎其所發而辭氣於是順焉其聲和
矣由是省其文采廣其節奏器數爲之具陳而
心聲爲之盡美此和樂之所由興也要之兼體
而後樂備知序而后樂成唯君子能之則其廣
樂以成教者胥此矣信斯言也宜莫如舜歌南
風者其象也舞韶箾者其飾也而文明温恭之
德本之乃若冑子之教詩歌聲律有倫矣而和
===
德先焉此有由本也後世房中之歌廟中之舞
本之則無如樂何
福者備也備者百順之名也無所不順者
之謂備
嚴璞
同考試官教諭黃批題意曲折作者多蔓
說平正通達無踰此篇
考試官教授蔣批精切有味
考試官教授桂批得㫖
punctuated:
然其序惡可亂乎？彼知心爲樂之本也，則慎其所感，而性術於是乎形焉，其心和矣；知聲爲樂之象也，則慎其所發，而辭氣於是順焉，其聲和矣。由是省其文采，廣其節奏，器數爲之具陳，而心聲爲之盡美，此和樂之所由興也。要之，兼體而後樂備，知序而后樂成，唯君子能之，則其廣樂以成教者胥此矣。信斯言也，宜莫如舜：歌南風者，其象也；舞韶箾者，其飾也；而文明温恭之德本之。乃若冑子之教，詩歌聲律有倫矣，而和德先焉，此有由本也。後世房中之歌、廟中之舞，本之則無，如樂何？

「福者，備也；備者，百順之名也。無所不順者之謂備。」

嚴璞

同考試官教諭黃批：「題意曲折，作者多蔓說，平正通達，無踰此篇。」

考試官教授蔣批：「精切有味。」

考試官教授桂批：「得㫖。」
translation_en:
Yet how could their proper order be confused? Knowing that the heart is the foundation of music, one attends carefully to what moves it; one’s nature and practices [?] thereby take shape, and the heart becomes harmonious. Knowing that sound is the manifestation of music, one attends carefully to what one expresses; one’s words and tone thereby become fitting, and the sounds become harmonious. From this, one examines music’s embellishments and expands its rhythms. Its instruments and prescribed measures are fully set forth, and both heart and sound attain their full beauty. This is how harmonious music arises. In sum, music becomes complete only when its aspects are embodied together, and achieves fulfillment only when their proper sequence is understood. Only the gentleman can accomplish this; his expansion of music to bring instruction to fruition rests entirely upon it.

If these words are true, surely no one exemplifies them better than Shun. Singing the Southern Wind was music’s manifestation; dancing the Shaoxiao was its embellishment. Yet his virtues of refinement, enlightenment, warmth, and reverence formed their foundation. As for the education of the sons of the nobility, poetry, song, sounds, and pitch standards had their proper order, but harmonious virtue came first. This proceeded from a foundation. In later ages there were songs within the palace chambers and dances within the ancestral temples, but their foundation was absent [?]. What, then, could be done with music?

“Blessing means completeness. Completeness is the name for conformity in a hundred respects. To conform in every respect is what is called completeness.”

Yan Pu.

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “The meaning of the topic has many turns, and writers often become prolix. For balance, correctness, clarity, and thorough understanding, no essay surpasses this one.”

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: “Precise, pertinent, and rich in meaning.”

Comment by Examiner Gui, Professor: “Grasps the essential meaning.”

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
記者推福之義存乎備而因明其所由備焉夫
福之爲言順以備者也賢者之福其諸異乎世
之福與且夫福之時義大矣弗明其義惡可言
福弗能其事惡可致福故唯賢者能之而衆不
與焉彼其所謂福者非有祈而得之也備焉耳
矣夫事之所當爲者本咸正而無缺而吾之所
自致者乃兼舉而無遺外此以言福則誣矣其
所謂備者又非無故而獲之也百順焉耳矣夫
反諸一身其理未始有違而貞於百度其迹不
===
容有間外此以言備則惑矣旣曰百順則是順
之至也措則正而施則行有攸往而皆利也體
之信而達之順無所動而不宜也否則矯强者
未免於拂經而襲取者不足以成務將有所順
有所未順矣惡在其爲備也哉吁由備有福之
名則凡可以求備者何不用也由順有備之名
則凡可以致順者何不爲也祭之義其盡於此
而已乎抑聞易之介福書之錫福皆自天佑之
正世之所謂福也賢者盡祭之義則其所佑者
punctuated: 記者推福之義存乎備，而因明其所由備焉。夫福之爲言，順以備者也。賢者之福，其諸異乎世之福與？且夫福之時義大矣！弗明其義，惡可言福？弗能其事，惡可致福？故唯賢者能之，而衆不與焉。彼其所謂福者，非有祈而得之也，備焉耳矣。夫事之所當爲者，本咸正而無缺，而吾之所自致者，乃兼舉而無遺。外此以言福，則誣矣。其所謂備者，又非無故而獲之也，百順焉耳矣。夫反諸一身，其理未始有違，而貞於百度，其迹不容有間。外此以言備，則惑矣。旣曰百順，則是順之至也。措則正，而施則行，有攸往而皆利也；體之信，而達之順，無所動而不宜也。否則矯强者未免於拂經，而襲取者不足以成務，將有所順、有所未順矣，惡在其爲備也哉？吁！由備有福之名，則凡可以求備者，何不用也？由順有備之名，則凡可以致順者，何不爲也？祭之義，其盡於此而已乎？抑聞《易》之介福、《書》之錫福，皆自天佑之，正世之所謂福也。賢者盡祭之義，則其所佑者
translation_en: The compiler of the Record traces the meaning of blessing to completeness and thereby explains how that completeness comes about. Blessing means being complete through accord with what is right. Surely the blessings of the worthy differ from what the world calls blessings? Great indeed is the significance of blessing in its proper circumstances! Without understanding its meaning, how can one speak of blessing? Without being capable of the deeds it requires, how can one bring blessing about? Thus only the worthy can accomplish this; the multitude has no share in it. What they call blessing is not something obtained through prayer: it is simply completeness. Everything that ought to be done is inherently right and without deficiency, and what one personally accomplishes must encompass it all, leaving nothing out. To speak of blessing apart from this is false. Nor is what they call completeness obtained without a cause: it is simply accord in every respect. When one examines oneself, one has never departed from principle; when one holds steadfastly to the hundred standards of conduct, one's actions admit of no lapse. To speak of completeness apart from this is delusion. Since we speak of accord in every respect, this is accord carried to its utmost. Whatever one undertakes is right, and whatever one puts into practice succeeds: wherever one goes, all is beneficial. One embodies it sincerely and carries it through harmoniously: no action is unfitting. Otherwise, those who force themselves into conformity cannot avoid running counter to enduring principles, while those who merely borrow outward forms cannot accomplish their duties. There will then be accord in some respects but not in others. Where, then, is their completeness? Ah! If completeness gives rise to the name of blessing, why not employ every means of seeking completeness? If accord gives rise to the name of completeness, why not do everything that can bring about accord? Is the meaning of sacrifice exhausted by this alone? Yet I have heard that the ‘great blessing’ in the Book of Changes and the ‘bestowal of blessings’ in the Book of Documents both mean receiving Heaven's aid—precisely what the world calls blessing. When the worthy fulfill the meaning of sacrifice, then the aid they receive …

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
大矣而獨不及此何也夫聚百順以事君親則
不與福期而福自至但賢者非有心於求之耳
詩人紀祀享而恒舉純嘏壽考爲言盖亦有以
識此矣
第貳塲
論
大哉堯之爲君
陳述齡
同考試官教諭陳批德不可名堯之所以
===
爲大也此篇獨得肯綮庶幾乎知德之言
同考試官教諭吳批題意廣大作者無所措
手子獨根極體要如探淵海而得玄珠佳士佳士
考試官教授蔣批說堯合德於天意親切
考試官教授桂批平順
論曰聖人以德化天下而天下不有其德斯其
化也神矣天下之化將聖人是賴而聖人固以
其身先之此非有意於天下之必吾從而遂至
相忘於其德然後知聖人之化不可及也吾有
punctuated:
大矣，而獨不及此，何也？夫聚百順以事君親，則不與福期而福自至，但賢者非有心於求之耳。詩人紀祀享，而恒舉純嘏壽考爲言，盖亦有以識此矣。

第貳塲
論
大哉堯之爲君
陳述齡

同考試官教諭陳批：德不可名，堯之所以爲大也。此篇獨得肯綮，庶幾乎知德之言。

同考試官教諭吳批：題意廣大，作者無所措手。子獨根極體要，如探淵海而得玄珠。佳士！佳士！

考試官教授蔣批：說堯合德於天，意親切。

考試官教授桂批：平順。

論曰：聖人以德化天下，而天下不有其德，斯其化也神矣。天下之化，將聖人是賴，而聖人固以其身先之。此非有意於天下之必吾從，而遂至相忘於其德，然後知聖人之化不可及也。吾有
translation_en:
…is great indeed; why, then, is this alone left unmentioned? When one brings together every form of dutiful compliance in serving one’s ruler and parents, blessings arrive of themselves, without one expecting them. It is simply that the worthy have no deliberate intention of seeking them. When the poets recorded sacrificial offerings, they constantly spoke of great blessings and longevity; surely they, too, had some understanding of this.

Second Session
Discourse
“Great Indeed Was Yao as a Ruler!”
By Chen Shuling

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “His virtue could not be named: this is what made Yao great. This essay alone grasps the essential point; its words come close to showing an understanding of virtue.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “The topic’s meaning is so vast that a writer scarcely knows where to begin. You alone have probed its foundations and reached its essentials, like someone who searches the ocean depths and obtains the dark pearl. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!”

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: “The explanation of how Yao’s virtue accorded with Heaven is apt and incisive.”

Comment by Examiner Gui, Professor: “Even and fluent.”

The discourse says: The sage transforms all under Heaven through virtue, yet those under Heaven are unaware of his virtue: such transformation is truly wondrous. The transformation of all under Heaven depends upon the sage, and the sage assuredly leads through his own example. He has no deliberate intention that all under Heaven must follow him; ultimately, he and the people become oblivious to his virtue. Only then do we understand that the sage’s transforming influence cannot be equaled. I possess…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
道𨓏迪之機而使天下皆知其善吾有作為之跡
而使天下遂知其勞此其道非不足以治天下
而天下鰓鰓然得以窺其心之所存而吾方自
信以為天下之吾治焉斯亦小矣非所以與論
於神化也夫子論治而獨賛堯之大其深知堯
者歟易有之曰大哉乾元萬物資始乃統天夫
乾元天之道也而獨以大哉繫之何也謂其能
始物也能統天也於其始物也見聖人育民之
象焉於其統天也見聖人制治之象焉夫子釋
===
之曰乾始能以美利利天下不言所利大矣哉
蓋乾元有利天下之德而天下不知其所以利
是以不可得而言也今夫天之運于上也其命
則於穆其載則無聲無臭初若無所見於天下
者而流行之妙固變化而不可窮夫人見其沛
然潤者曰此雨露也虢然震者曰此雷霆也燦
然麗者曰此日月星辰也秩然順布者曰此寒
暑也夫其雨露之足為澤也雷霆之足為威也
日月星辰之足為明也寒暑之足以成歲功也
punctuated: 道𨓏迪之機，而使天下皆知其善；吾有作為之跡，而使天下遂知其勞。此其道非不足以治天下，而天下鰓鰓然得以窺其心之所存，而吾方自信以為天下之吾治焉，斯亦小矣，非所以與論於神化也。夫子論治，而獨賛堯之大，其深知堯者歟？《易》有之，曰：「大哉乾元，萬物資始，乃統天。」夫乾元，天之道也，而獨以「大哉」繫之，何也？謂其能始物也，能統天也。於其始物也，見聖人育民之象焉；於其統天也，見聖人制治之象焉。夫子釋之曰：「乾始能以美利利天下，不言所利，大矣哉！」蓋乾元有利天下之德，而天下不知其所以利，是以不可得而言也。今夫天之運于上也，其命則於穆，其載則無聲無臭，初若無所見於天下者，而流行之妙，固變化而不可窮。夫人見其沛然潤者，曰：「此雨露也。」虢然震者，曰：「此雷霆也。」燦然麗者，曰：「此日月星辰也。」秩然順布者，曰：「此寒暑也。」夫其雨露之足為澤也，雷霆之足為威也，日月星辰之足為明也，寒暑之足以成歲功也，
translation_en: …a means of guiding people onward [?], causing all under Heaven to recognize its goodness; I leave traces of my actions, causing all under Heaven to recognize my labors. Such a way is not insufficient to govern the world. Yet the people, anxiously watchful, can discern what lies in the ruler’s heart, while I confidently suppose that the world is governed by me. This is petty indeed, and affords no basis for discussing transformation of divine subtlety. When the Master discussed government, he singled out Yao’s greatness for praise. Surely he understood Yao profoundly! The Book of Changes says: “Great indeed is the primal power of Qian! The myriad things draw upon it for their beginnings, and it encompasses Heaven.” The primal power of Qian is the Way of Heaven. Why, then, is it specifically described as “great indeed”? Because it can give things their beginnings and encompass Heaven. In its giving things their beginnings, we see an image of the sage nurturing the people; in its encompassing Heaven, we see an image of the sage establishing orderly government. The Master explained it thus: “Qian, through its initiating power, can benefit all under Heaven with beautiful benefits, without saying what it benefits. Great indeed!” For the primal power of Qian possesses the virtue of benefiting all under Heaven, yet the world does not know how it confers those benefits; hence this cannot be expressed in words. Now, as Heaven moves above, its mandate is profound and mysterious, and its workings have neither sound nor scent. At first it seems to manifest nothing to the world, yet the subtlety of its circulation consists in transformations that cannot be exhausted. People see what moistens abundantly and say, “This is rain and dew.” They see what shakes with a roar [?] and say, “This is thunder.” They see what shines brilliantly and say, “These are the sun, moon, and stars.” They see what unfolds in orderly succession and say, “These are cold and heat.” As for rain and dew being sufficient to bestow bounty, thunder sufficient to manifest awe, the sun, moon, and stars sufficient to provide illumination, and cold and heat sufficient to complete the work of the year…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
天下莫不知其然而其所以爲雨露雷霆日月
之類者舉莫得其所以然此乾元所以爲大也
觀乾元之道則知堯矣今夫言聖之大者莫如
堯治之大者亦莫如堯此宜將以非常之事功
自異於天下而凡其所以存心加志焉者無從
而知也方其時洚水警予懷襄之害未除也而
庶土則交正矣蠻夷猾夏疆圉之棘未舒也而
四夷則來王矣黎民阻饑稼穡之利未奏也而
烝民則乃粒矣兜鯀並進姦宄之萌未憯也而
===
四罪則咸服矣五品不遜慎徽之典未備也而
萬邦則協和矣此數者天下之大患也堯皆爲
天下除而去之而天下且安之若其未有昔之
患也堯之德如此其偉也治如此其弘也而天
下且忘之若其未有今日之功也故曰殺之而
不怨利之而不庸民日遷善而不知爲之者此
聖人之神化與天地同流者也是故以功業求
之則其功業巍然爾以文章求之則其文章煥
然爾如其盡於功業文章而已巳非後世所能
punctuated: 天下莫不知其然，而其所以爲雨露、雷霆、日月之類者，舉莫得其所以然。此乾元所以爲大也。觀乾元之道，則知堯矣。今夫言聖之大者，莫如堯；治之大者，亦莫如堯。此宜將以非常之事功自異於天下，而凡其所以存心加志焉者，無從而知也。方其時，洚水警予，懷襄之害未除也，而庶土則交正矣；蠻夷猾夏，疆圉之棘未舒也，而四夷則來王矣；黎民阻饑，稼穡之利未奏也，而烝民則乃粒矣；兜鯀並進，姦宄之萌未憯也，而四罪則咸服矣；五品不遜，慎徽之典未備也，而萬邦則協和矣。此數者，天下之大患也。堯皆爲天下除而去之，而天下且安之，若其未有昔之患也。堯之德如此其偉也，治如此其弘也，而天下且忘之，若其未有今日之功也。故曰：「殺之而不怨，利之而不庸，民日遷善而不知爲之者。」此聖人之神化與天地同流者也。是故以功業求之，則其功業巍然爾；以文章求之，則其文章煥然爾。如其盡於功業文章而已，巳非後世所能
translation_en:
…Everyone under Heaven knows that these things are so, yet none can grasp what makes them rain and dew, thunder, sun and moon, and the like. This is what makes the primal power of Qian great. By contemplating its Way, one can understand Yao.

Among those called great in sagehood, none compares with Yao; among those great in governing, likewise none compares with Yao. One would expect him to distinguish himself before the world through extraordinary achievements. Yet there is no way to know all that occupied his heart and engaged his purpose. At that time, “the floodwaters alarm me”: the devastation of the overwhelming inundation had not been eliminated, yet the various lands were all set in order. The Man and Yi peoples disrupted the Xia realm: the troubles at the borders had not been relieved, yet the peoples of the four quarters came to acknowledge his kingship. The common people suffered hunger: the benefits of sowing and reaping had not yet been realized, yet the multitude obtained grain to eat. Dou and Gun advanced together: the budding of wickedness and disorder had not yet become grievous [?], yet the four offenders all submitted to punishment. The five human relationships lacked harmony: the institutions for carefully promoting these teachings were not yet complete, yet the myriad states were brought into concord.

These were great afflictions of the world. Yao removed and dispelled them all for the world, yet the people rested content, as though those former afflictions had never existed. Yao’s virtue was so magnificent, his governance so far-reaching, yet the people forgot them, as though the achievements of the present had never occurred. Thus it is said: “He puts them to death, yet they bear no resentment; he benefits them, yet they do not credit him with it. The people daily advance toward goodness without knowing who brings this about.” Such is the sage’s wondrous transforming influence, flowing together with Heaven and Earth.

Thus, if one seeks him in his achievements, those achievements are towering; if one seeks him in his cultural manifestations, those manifestations are resplendent. If his greatness were exhausted by achievements and cultural manifestations alone, even these would already be beyond what later ages could…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
及如其不盡於功業文章而已則其所爲大者
吾不知也彼其股肱之臣如舜禹臯陶皆親見
其成而交賛之則以爲帝德廣運而史氏從而
筆之則曰此陶唐之治云爾而康衢之歌且曰
不識不知順帝之則嗟夫堯何施而得此於民
哉今讀其書追想其治功恍然如在千載之上
神遊伊耆之庭仰觀嶽牧夔龍諸賢相與推讓
都俞而俯聽擊壤帝力何有之謠至於問之朝
野而不知則其所謂大者諒何如也是故雖欲
===
以言擬之不可得也雖欲以意象之亦不可得
也言與意之所不能盡可以觀大矣求堯於言
與意之所不能盡可以觀神矣甚哉堯之德非
後世所能知也豈惟後世雖其時天下之人亦
不能知也雖堯亦不自知也此堯所以同於天
也夫子之序卦也曰黃帝堯舜垂衣裳而治夫
固以其端拱而化成也然並舉三聖而獨取堯
之大何也自黃帝而上則顓蒙之俗猶在也自
舜而降則淳樸之德下衰也故前乎此者其人
punctuated: 及。如其不盡於功業文章而已，則其所爲大者，吾不知也。彼其股肱之臣，如舜、禹、臯陶，皆親見其成而交賛之，則以爲帝德廣運；而史氏從而筆之，則曰此陶唐之治云爾。而康衢之歌且曰：「不識不知，順帝之則。」嗟夫！堯何施而得此於民哉？今讀其書，追想其治功，恍然如在千載之上，神遊伊耆之庭，仰觀嶽牧、夔、龍諸賢相與推讓都俞，而俯聽擊壤「帝力何有」之謠。至於問之朝野而不知，則其所謂大者，諒何如也？是故雖欲以言擬之，不可得也；雖欲以意象之，亦不可得也。言與意之所不能盡，可以觀大矣；求堯於言與意之所不能盡，可以觀神矣。甚哉！堯之德非後世所能知也。豈惟後世？雖其時天下之人亦不能知也，雖堯亦不自知也。此堯所以同於天也。夫子之序卦也曰：「黃帝、堯、舜垂衣裳而治。」夫固以其端拱而化成也。然並舉三聖而獨取堯之大，何也？自黃帝而上，則顓蒙之俗猶在也；自舜而降，則淳樸之德下衰也。故前乎此者，其人
translation_en:
…match it. If, however, his greatness was not exhausted by his achievements and cultural brilliance, then wherein that greatness lay I do not know. His ministers, who served as his arms and legs—Shun, Yu, and Gao Yao—personally witnessed his accomplishments and joined in praising him, declaring that the emperor’s virtue was all-encompassing and far-reaching. The historians then committed this to writing, calling it simply the government of Taotang [Yao]. Yet the song of the broad thoroughfare also said: “Without recognition or knowledge, we follow the emperor’s pattern.” Ah! What did Yao do to elicit this from the people?

Reading these writings now and recalling the achievements of his government, I seem transported thousands of years into the past, roaming in spirit through the court of Yiqi [Yao]. Looking up, I see the worthy ministers—the regional chiefs and governors, Kui, and Long—yielding precedence to one another and exchanging words of counsel and assent. Looking down, I hear the clod-beating song: “What has the emperor’s power to do with me?” If even those questioned at court and among the common people did not know, what indeed must his so-called greatness have been? Thus, though one wished to describe it in words, one could not; though one wished to envision it in thought, one could not. In what words and thought cannot exhaust, one may perceive greatness. Seeking Yao in what words and thought cannot exhaust, one may perceive his spiritual efficacy.

How profound it was! Yao’s virtue could not be understood by later generations. And why only later generations? Even the people of the world in his own time could not understand it; even Yao himself was unaware of it. This is how Yao was like Heaven. When the Master set forth the hexagrams, he said: “The Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun let their robes hang down, and the world was governed.” This was surely because, seated upright with hands folded, they brought transformation to completion. Yet why, when mentioning the three sages together, did he single out Yao’s greatness? In the time of the Yellow Emperor and earlier, the customs of simple ignorance still persisted; from Shun onward, the virtue of unadorned simplicity declined. Thus, as for those who preceded this time, the men themselves…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
有所未至後乎此者其大有所不及堯之德益
有徵矣且夫子嘗以君哉稱舜以無間然稱禹
以至德稱文王而湯之慙德錄之于書武之未
盡善論之於樂皆不得與堯竝軌也彼舜禹承
堯之緒固堯之所嘗委任者也文王之大統未
集其化猶未洽也至于湯武之舉雖曰應天順
人有不得已之心焉雖欲爲堯之大皆弗可得
也或者謂堯禀德而生則天地之中和也應時
而興則元會之中數也舉賢而敷治則古今之
===
泰運也非德則無其基非時則無其運非賢則
無其助堯之治天下其亦有由矣然而未盡其
要也典謨夫子之所定也首敘欽明文思之德
而精一執中之訓又屢致意焉則天下化成之
本無乃出於此歟夫子嘗祖述其道而病天下
之莫能容乃取而明之以垂憲萬世是以兩觀
之游有志大道之行而傷其未逮焉宜其重感
於堯也
表
punctuated:
有所未至，後乎此者，其大有所不及，堯之德益有徵矣。且夫子嘗以「君哉」稱舜，以「無間然」稱禹，以「至德」稱文王，而湯之慙德錄之于《書》，武之未盡善論之於樂，皆不得與堯竝軌也。彼舜禹承堯之緒，固堯之所嘗委任者也。文王之大統未集，其化猶未洽也。至于湯武之舉，雖曰應天順人，有不得已之心焉，雖欲爲堯之大，皆弗可得也。或者謂堯禀德而生，則天地之中和也；應時而興，則元會之中數也；舉賢而敷治，則古今之泰運也。非德則無其基，非時則無其運，非賢則無其助，堯之治天下，其亦有由矣。然而未盡其要也。典謨，夫子之所定也，首敘欽明文思之德，而精一執中之訓，又屢致意焉，則天下化成之本，無乃出於此歟？夫子嘗祖述其道，而病天下之莫能容，乃取而明之，以垂憲萬世。是以兩觀之游，有志大道之行，而傷其未逮焉，宜其重感於堯也。

表
translation_en:
…had points they had not yet attained, while those who came afterward fell short in greatness: thus Yao’s virtue is all the more clearly attested. Moreover, the Master once praised Shun with “What a ruler!”, Yu with “I can find no fault,” and King Wen with “the highest virtue.” Yet Tang’s sense of shame concerning his virtue is recorded in the Documents, and King Wu’s failure to attain perfect goodness is discussed in connection with music. None could stand on an equal footing with Yao. Shun and Yu carried on Yao’s legacy and were men to whom Yao himself had entrusted responsibilities. King Wen had not yet brought the great succession to completion, and his transforming influence had not yet reached everywhere. As for the undertakings of Tang and Wu, although they responded to Heaven and accorded with the people, they acted from a sense that they had no alternative. Even had they wished to attain Yao’s greatness, they could not have done so.

Some say that Yao was born endowed with virtue through the balance and harmony of Heaven and Earth; that he arose in response to his time at the central juncture of the cosmic cycles of yuan and hui; and that his elevation of worthy men and extension of good government marked an auspicious turn in the fortunes of all history. Without virtue, he would have lacked a foundation; without the proper time, he would have lacked favorable fortune; without worthy men, he would have lacked assistance. Yao’s success in governing all under Heaven thus had its causes. Yet this does not fully explain its essentials. The Canons and Counsels, which the Master edited, begin by recounting the virtues of reverence, enlightenment, refinement, and thoughtfulness. They also repeatedly emphasize the teaching to remain discerning and single-minded and to hold fast to the mean. Might not the foundation for the transformation and perfection of all under Heaven lie here?

The Master once transmitted and followed Yao’s Way, but lamented that no one under Heaven could accommodate it. He therefore took it up and elucidated it, leaving a model for ten thousand generations. Thus, during his visit to the two gate towers, he aspired to the practice of the Great Way and grieved that he had not lived to see it. It is fitting that he should have felt so deeply about Yao.

Memorials

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
擬
賜歷代名臣奏議羣臣謝表永樂十四年
張楚翹
同考試官敎諭顧批我
成祖廣忠益於千載之上彙成
大典謝疏能敷陳其槩辭氣渾融他日可備論思之選矣
同考試官學正余批對
君之辭貴忠懇深厚不徒駢儷爲工而已唯吾子能之
考試官敎授蔣批不事補綴而爛然有
===
章黼黻之才也
考試官敎授桂批清和潤澤
永樂十四年某月某日具官臣某等伏蒙
聖恩頒
賜歷代名臣奏議臣等誠惶誠恐稽首頓首稱
謝者伏以
聖學懋昭求多聞而建事
皇極用訓集眾思以作忠諒文獻之足徵羡
君臣之相遇遂沐渙頒之
punctuated:
擬賜歷代名臣奏議羣臣謝表，永樂十四年。
張楚翹。
同考試官敎諭顧批：我成祖廣忠益於千載之上，彙成大典。謝疏能敷陳其槩，辭氣渾融，他日可備論思之選矣。
同考試官學正余批：對君之辭，貴忠懇深厚，不徒駢儷爲工而已，唯吾子能之。
考試官敎授蔣批：不事補綴而爛然有章，黼黻之才也。
考試官敎授桂批：清和潤澤。
永樂十四年某月某日，具官臣某等伏蒙聖恩頒賜歷代名臣奏議。臣等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首稱謝者。伏以聖學懋昭，求多聞而建事；皇極用訓，集眾思以作忠。諒文獻之足徵，羡君臣之相遇，遂沐渙頒之
translation_en:
Draft memorial of thanks from the assembled officials upon being granted Memorials and Deliberations of Eminent Ministers through the Dynasties, set in the fourteenth year of Yongle [1416].
By Zhang Chuqiao.
Comment by Associate Examiner Gu, Instructor: Our Emperor Chengzu sought far and wide for loyal counsel and beneficial advice from more than a thousand years of the past, gathering it into a great compendium. This memorial of thanks sets forth its essential purport; its language and spirit form a harmonious whole. In days to come, its author could be chosen to deliberate upon affairs and offer counsel.
Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, School Director: In words addressed to the sovereign, what matters is loyalty, sincerity, depth, and substance, rather than merely accomplished parallel phrasing. You, sir, have achieved this.
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: Without resorting to piecing together borrowed phrases, this writing displays a brilliant pattern: here is a talent capable of adorning imperial governance.
Comment by Examiner Gui, Professor: Clear and harmonious, rich and polished.
On a certain day of a certain month in the fourteenth year of Yongle, your servants, so-and-so and others, holding their respective offices, humbly received your sagely favor in the bestowal of Memorials and Deliberations of Eminent Ministers through the Dynasties. With profound awe and trepidation, we bow our heads to the ground and kowtow, offering our thanks.
We humbly reflect that Your Majesty’s sagely learning shines ever more brightly: you seek extensive knowledge to accomplish affairs. The sovereign’s supreme standard serves as instruction: you gather the thoughts of many to elicit loyal service. Truly, these writings and worthy men provide ample testimony; we admire the happy encounters between sovereigns and ministers. Thus we have been bathed in your munificent bestowal of …

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
寵式占晉接之
光竊惟外廷旌善熈帝載於敷言內史獻書茂
王猷於納誨若金作礪惟木從繩下達上
宣交每通於天地予違汝弼誼尤重乎古
今粤稽歷世之名賢恒負匡君之宏略雖
就事而論事各因其時然啓心以沃心必
求諸道舉爵作戒納牖示占決策鼓音爰
重鄙乎肉食聽謀輿誦遂狎主于耳盟都
俞之日彌遐謇諤之風斯下炎精啓祚收
===
勝筭於轉圜文德受符納直言於止輦英
明間作忠讜竝陳代不乏人數可更僕懷
謀猷而入告善必稱君策便宜以上聞志
惟許國式存蓍鑑用比韋弦凡其昭德塞
違事或專於報主與夫獻可替否計有切
於利民惟多識夫前言庶少裨乎至治顧
汝愚之采輯成編僅止於宋臣暨蘇軾之
奏陳屬簡惟專於陸相舊章有待曠典尚
虛雖逆耳之談在往世未售其志而格心
punctuated: 寵，式占晉接之光。竊惟外廷旌善，熈帝載於敷言；內史獻書，茂王猷於納誨。若金作礪，惟木從繩，下達上宣，交每通於天地；予違汝弼，誼尤重乎古今。粤稽歷世之名賢，恒負匡君之宏略。雖就事而論事，各因其時；然啓心以沃心，必求諸道。舉爵作戒，納牖示占，決策鼓音，爰重鄙乎肉食；聽謀輿誦，遂狎主于耳盟。都俞之日彌遐，謇諤之風斯下。炎精啓祚，收勝筭於轉圜；文德受符，納直言於止輦。英明間作，忠讜竝陳，代不乏人，數可更僕。懷謀猷而入告，善必稱君；策便宜以上聞，志惟許國。式存蓍鑑，用比韋弦。凡其昭德塞違，事或專於報主；與夫獻可替否，計有切於利民。惟多識夫前言，庶少裨乎至治。顧汝愚之采輯成編，僅止於宋臣；暨蘇軾之奏陳屬簡，惟專於陸相。舊章有待，曠典尚虛。雖逆耳之談，在往世未售其志，而格心
translation_en:
…favor, and thus enjoy the glory of being received in audience. We humbly reflect that, when the outer court honors good counsel, imperial undertakings flourish through the presentation of advice; when the palace scribe presents writings, royal plans prosper through the acceptance of admonition. As metal requires a whetstone and wood follows the marking line, so words from below reach above and commands from above are proclaimed below: their interchange ever joins Heaven and Earth. “When I err, you must correct me”: this duty has been especially weighty throughout past and present. Examining the renowned worthies of successive ages, we find that they always possessed broad strategies for setting their sovereigns right. Although their discussions addressed particular affairs according to the circumstances of their times, in awakening and nourishing their rulers’ minds they invariably sought guidance in the Way. Raising the cup, they offered admonition; gaining access as through a window, they revealed the import of divination. In deciding policy amid the sound of drums, they laid particular stress on the shortsightedness of those who ate meat—that is, those holding office; in heeding counsel and the songs of common people, they brought the ruler into familiar contact with “ear covenants” [?]. As the days of harmonious consultation receded ever further into the past, the practice of forthright remonstrance declined.

When the dynasty of the fiery essence inaugurated its rule, it gained victorious strategies by responding as readily as something round turns; when the ruler of civil virtue received the mandate, he halted his carriage to accept frank speech [?]. Wise and discerning sovereigns arose from time to time, and loyal, upright counsel was presented alongside them. No age lacked such men; to enumerate them would require successive attendants. They brought plans into the royal presence, always attributing the good to their sovereign; they submitted proposals suited to circumstances, their sole resolve being to devote themselves to the state. Their words were preserved as guides like divining stalks and mirrors, serving as reminders like leather thongs and bowstrings. In illuminating virtue and checking error, their efforts might be directed especially toward repaying their lord; in advancing what was sound and rejecting what was unsound, their plans closely concerned the people's welfare. Only by acquiring broad knowledge of earlier sayings could one hope to contribute even a little to consummate government.

Yet the compilation assembled by [Zhao] Ruyu extended only to ministers of the Song; and the writings Su Shi proposed for presentation to the throne concerned Chancellor Lu alone. The writings of earlier times still awaited attention, and this exceptional undertaking remained unfulfilled. Although words unwelcome to the ear had failed to accomplish their purpose in former ages, the art of rectifying the ruler’s heart…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之術非
明主孰諒其忠倘尺牘之具存宜寸長之備錄
恭惟
皇帝陛下
功符乾始
德象帝先
誕撫瑤圖格兩階而弘化
懋膺寶籙秉九伐以靖旹
弘謨烈於重光
===
廓乾坤於再造爰屬
萬幾之暇旁求一德之資思保大以肇基期執
中而布度謂天下之理未盡而日中之治
惟幾主善為師與治同道旁搜歷代藎言
偶契于
淵衷博覽殘編羣策畢收於汗簡
令傳左省來宣載筆之臣
詔下西崑式啓藏書之府類分彙集綱舉目張
自周武迄于宋元由君德至於夷狄前後
punctuated:
之術，非明主孰諒其忠？倘尺牘之具存，宜寸長之備錄。
恭惟皇帝陛下，功符乾始，德象帝先。誕撫瑤圖，格兩階而弘化；懋膺寶籙，秉九伐以靖旹。弘謨烈於重光，廓乾坤於再造。爰屬萬幾之暇，旁求一德之資，思保大以肇基，期執中而布度。謂天下之理未盡，而日中之治惟幾，主善為師，與治同道。旁搜歷代藎言，偶契于淵衷；博覽殘編，羣策畢收於汗簡。令傳左省，來宣載筆之臣；詔下西崑，式啓藏書之府。類分彙集，綱舉目張。自周武迄于宋元，由君德至於夷狄，前後
translation_en:
…as for their methods of rectifying the ruler’s heart, who but an enlightened sovereign could appreciate their loyalty? If their letters survive intact, every measure of merit in them should be fully recorded.
We reverently consider that Your Majesty the Emperor’s achievements accord with Heaven’s creative beginnings, and your virtue resembles that which preceded the Lord on High. You have magnificently assumed the precious mandate, extending your transforming influence through the submission achieved between the two stairways of the court; you have worthily received the treasured register of sovereignty, wielding the nine forms of punitive expedition to bring peace to the age. You have magnified great designs and achievements in renewed brilliance, and opened wide Heaven and Earth through their re-creation. Thus, in the intervals between your myriad affairs of state, you have sought far and wide for resources to sustain unified virtue, intent on preserving greatness and laying its foundations, and aspiring to hold to the mean and promulgate standards. You consider that the principles governing the world have not yet been exhaustively explored, and that government, even at its noonday height, depends on the subtlest beginnings of change. You take goodness as your teacher and follow the path of good government. Searching widely for the loyal counsels of successive ages, you find them consonant with your profound intentions; surveying surviving writings broadly, you gather every counsel into written records. Your command was transmitted to the Left Office [?], summoning the officials who wield the brush; your edict descended upon the Western Kunlun, the imperial library, opening its repositories of books. The material was classified and collected, its main divisions established and its particulars arranged. Extending from King Wu of Zhou down to the Song and Yuan, and ranging from the ruler’s virtue to the peoples beyond the realm, altogether…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
餘三百卷六籍之旨益明上下幾四千年
百氏之書咸備或紆籌於遇主有裨後事
之師或抗疏於從王無忝先資之信詎云
借才於異代廼亦取善於同人玆特擅場
餘皆合轍固四聰之可達靡一得之遂遺
對
君奚取於面從論世何傷於骨鯁開卷而陳敬
怠無庸座右之箴記篋而括古今殆勝席
前之問旣
===
麗正以懸離照猶
虛中而著謙光匪徒觀乎人文寔皆關於
聖德石渠底績
奏功著作之廷
天府效珍垂象昭回之域職以太史
訓示無疆屬之梓人
恩覃有位芸香槀紙羣捧紫泥之封
鳳軸鸞章旁耀青藜之影臣等學窺佔畢才乏
經綸立志未奇敢抵掌而談世務逢時非
punctuated: 餘三百卷，六籍之旨益明；上下幾四千年，百氏之書咸備。或紆籌於遇主，有裨後事之師；或抗疏於從王，無忝先資之信。詎云借才於異代，廼亦取善於同人。玆特擅場，餘皆合轍。固四聰之可達，靡一得之遂遺。對君奚取於面從？論世何傷於骨鯁？開卷而陳敬怠，無庸座右之箴；記篋而括古今，殆勝席前之問。旣麗正以懸離照，猶虛中而著謙光。匪徒觀乎人文，寔皆關於聖德。石渠底績，奏功著作之廷；天府效珍，垂象昭回之域。職以太史，訓示無疆；屬之梓人，恩覃有位。芸香槀紙，羣捧紫泥之封；鳳軸鸞章，旁耀青藜之影。臣等學窺佔畢，才乏經綸。立志未奇，敢抵掌而談世務？逢時非
translation_en:
…more than three hundred juan, making the purport of the Six Classics still clearer; spanning nearly four thousand years, it comprehensively includes the writings of the many schools. Some devised plans upon finding a receptive ruler, offering useful lessons for later undertakings; others submitted outspoken memorials while serving their sovereign, faithfully upholding the guidance inherited from their predecessors [?]. How could this be merely borrowing talent from other ages? It is also taking what is good from fellow men. These examples are especially outstanding; the remainder all follow the same course. Surely all can reach Your Majesty’s hearing, open to the four quarters, and no single valuable insight is left out. In addressing one’s ruler, what use is compliance to his face? In discussing the affairs of an age, what harm is there in forthrightness? Open the volumes, and examples of reverence and negligence are set forth: there is no need for an admonition beside one’s seat. Stored in the book chest, they encompass antiquity and the present, surpassing, perhaps, inquiries made of advisers before the imperial seat.

Already cleaving to rectitude and displaying the illumination of Li, the trigram of brightness, Your Majesty nevertheless remains receptive and manifests the radiance of humility. This is not merely a contemplation of human culture: all of it bears upon Your sagely virtue. The work of the Stone Canal library has reached completion, and its accomplishment is reported at the court of literary composition. The Celestial Treasury presents its treasures, displaying exemplary patterns within the realm of imperial radiance. The Grand Historian is charged with the task, that instruction may extend without limit; the work is entrusted to block carvers, that imperial favor may reach all who hold office. Amid rue-scented books and manuscript paper, all reverently receive the packages sealed with purple clay; phoenix scroll rollers and splendid writings shine beside the light of the green goosefoot staff.

We, Your servants, have acquired only a glimpse of learning through poring over texts, and lack the talent to order the realm. Our aspirations are as yet unremarkable: how could we presume to discourse on affairs of state with expansive gestures? That we have encountered such an age is no…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
偶幸屈首而受成規若或啟衷何宜釋手
牙籤侈事無論萬卷之藏金鑑微忠未數
千秋之獻
蕃錫已逾於什襲博綜寧靳於三餘敢不益
殫論思共圖職業聞道而能識其大期悟
意于忘筌取法而僅得其中欲追踪于補
袞伏願
凝神宥密侔虞舜之巍巍
恢度含弘進周王之諤諤保玆
===
丕緒愼乃永圖
武緯文經秉全能於參兩
道高德厚饗
純嘏於億千臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
punctuated:
偶，幸屈首而受成規。若或啟衷，何宜釋手？牙籤侈事，無論萬卷之藏；金鑑微忠，未數千秋之獻。蕃錫已逾於什襲，博綜寧靳於三餘？敢不益殫論思，共圖職業？聞道而能識其大，期悟意于忘筌；取法而僅得其中，欲追踪于補袞。
伏願凝神宥密，侔虞舜之巍巍；恢度含弘，進周王之諤諤。保玆丕緒，愼乃永圖。武緯文經，秉全能於參兩；道高德厚，饗純嘏於億千。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
translation_en:
…chance; we are fortunate to bow our heads and receive established rules. If these writings should open our hearts, how could we put them down? As for the lavish spectacle of books with ivory labels, we need not speak of a collection of ten thousand volumes; as for the modest loyalty embodied in a Golden Mirror of admonition, even the offering for the Thousand Autumns festival scarcely bears comparison. Your abundant gifts already exceed what we could wrap in ten protective layers; how could we begrudge the study of their breadth during the “three spare times”? Dare we fail to devote ourselves still more fully to deliberation and reflection, and together attend to our official duties? In hearing the Way and recognizing its greater principles, we hope to grasp the meaning and forget the fish trap; though in taking the highest as our standard we attain only the middle rank, we wish to follow those who mended the imperial robes by correcting their sovereign’s faults.
We humbly pray that, concentrating your spirit in profound stillness, you may equal the towering majesty of Shun of Yu; that, enlarging your capacity for tolerance and generosity, you may encourage the outspoken remonstrance welcomed by the king of Zhou. Preserve this great inheritance and give careful thought to your enduring plans. With military achievement as the weft and civil accomplishment as the warp, exercise your complete powers in accordance with Heaven’s three and Earth’s two. Lofty in the Way and abundant in virtue, may you enjoy unalloyed blessings for countless ages. Your servants, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, cannot contain our intense emotion and trembling awe. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our thanks and make them known to Your Majesty.

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第叁場
策
第一問
張楚翹
同考試官教諭顧批我
皇上加志郢都明倫化俗之訓同符
聖祖媲美典謨子獨能颺言之所謂識其大者非邪
同考試官學正余批我
皇上以彝倫為訓而天下化成然文德所洽始於南國子能誦
===
說其盛蓋涵咏之深者取之
考試官教授蔣批我
皇上之訏謨根極於敬一之學非徒以言教而已韋布之流顧
能仰窺其際宜裒然首舉之
考試官教授桂批敷對詳明宜錄以式
聖王以道治天下也有人紀肇脩之要焉
聖王以道教天下也有人文化成之美焉
凡其本諸身而見於彝倫之大者均之人
紀也道之所由立也凡其存諸心而宣於
punctuated:
第叁場
策
第一問
張楚翹

同考試官教諭顧批：我皇上加志郢都，明倫化俗之訓，同符聖祖，媲美典謨。子獨能颺言之，所謂識其大者非邪？

同考試官學正余批：我皇上以彝倫為訓，而天下化成。然文德所洽，始於南國。子能誦說其盛，蓋涵咏之深者，取之。

考試官教授蔣批：我皇上之訏謨，根極於敬一之學，非徒以言教而已。韋布之流，顧能仰窺其際，宜裒然首舉之。

考試官教授桂批：敷對詳明，宜錄以式。

聖王以道治天下也，有人紀肇脩之要焉；聖王以道教天下也，有人文化成之美焉。凡其本諸身而見於彝倫之大者，均之人紀也，道之所由立也。凡其存諸心而宣於
translation_en:
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Zhang Chuqiao

Comment by Associate Examiner Gu, Instructor: Our Emperor has devoted his attention to Yingdu. His instructions for clarifying human relationships and transforming customs accord with those of the Sagely Founder and rival the beauty of the Canons and Counsels in the Book of Documents. You alone have been able to proclaim this eloquently. Are you not what is meant by one who understands the greater matters?

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor: Our Emperor takes the constant human relationships as the subject of his instruction, and the realm is thereby transformed. Yet the influence of his civil virtue first spread through the southern lands. You can recount and expound its flourishing achievements, surely because you have pondered them deeply. Accept this essay.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: Our Emperor’s grand counsels are rooted ultimately in the learning of reverent single-mindedness. He does not teach through words alone. That someone from among the common scholars should nevertheless be able to glimpse these heights merits his being singled out and placed first.

Comment by Examiner Gui, Professor: The response is detailed and clear. It should be recorded as a model.

When the sage king governs the realm through the Way, there is an essential principle by which the ordering of human relationships is first cultivated. When the sage king teaches the realm through the Way, there is the beauty of transformation accomplished through cultural refinement. All that is grounded in his own person and manifested in the great constant relationships belongs alike to the ordering of human relationships: it is through this that the Way is established. All that is preserved in his heart and proclaimed in …

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
謨訓之詳者均之人文也道之所由章也
明此以治謂之善治而作之君於四方矣
明此以教謂之善教而作之師於萬世矣
惟我
聖祖肇之于前故
盛德大業之兼隆惟我
皇上述之于後故
大烈耿光之並著天下士民爭相傳頌以爲復
見
===
雍熙太和之化久矣愚也嘗得於父老之所
傳聞而追思
聖祖繼天立極之化得於耳目之所睹記而祗
服
皇上化民成俗之方迺歎曰大哉
聖人之言乎又曰一哉
聖人之心乎夫樂
堯舜之道然後知吾身親見之爲盛也與多士
之列然後知
punctuated: 謨訓之詳者，均之人文也，道之所由章也。明此以治，謂之善治，而作之君於四方矣；明此以教，謂之善教，而作之師於萬世矣。惟我聖祖肇之于前，故盛德大業之兼隆；惟我皇上述之于後，故大烈耿光之並著。天下士民爭相傳頌，以爲復見雍熙太和之化久矣。愚也嘗得於父老之所傳聞，而追思聖祖繼天立極之化；得於耳目之所睹記，而祗服皇上化民成俗之方。迺歎曰：「大哉，聖人之言乎！」又曰：「一哉，聖人之心乎！」夫樂堯舜之道，然後知吾身親見之爲盛也；與多士之列，然後知
translation_en:
…expressed in the fullness of counsels and instructions—all these are cultural refinement, through which the Way is made manifest. To understand this and govern accordingly is called good government: thus one becomes a ruler for all the lands. To understand this and teach accordingly is called good teaching: thus one becomes a teacher for ten thousand generations. Our Sagely Progenitor initiated this in former times; hence his abundant virtue and great achievements flourished together. Our present Emperor has carried it forward in later times; hence his great accomplishments and brilliant glory shine forth together. For a long time now, scholars and commoners throughout the realm have vied in spreading his praises, believing that they have once more witnessed the transforming influence of harmonious prosperity and supreme concord.
Through accounts transmitted by the elders, I, in my ignorance, have reflected upon the transforming influence of the Sagely Progenitor, who succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard. Through what I have witnessed and recorded with my own ears and eyes, I have reverently admired our Emperor’s methods of transforming the people and perfecting their customs. Thereupon I exclaimed: “How great are the sage’s words!” And again: “How single in purpose is the sage’s heart!” Only after delighting in the Way of Yao and Shun does one understand the grandeur of witnessing it in person; only after joining the ranks of the many scholars does one understand…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
王國克生之爲美也今幸際
聖世而居
帝鄉執事固稱爲
首善之地矣其敢無辭以對請先論古帝王治
教之由而後及我
聖祖
皇上之同符者可乎書有之曰平章百姓百姓
昭明賛堯治也詩有之曰古之人無斁譽
髦斯士頌周教也夫聖人之化理天下也
===
必篤近而舉遠由親而逮疎皆不待求諸
彝倫之外故善觀堯之治者不在地平天
成之日而在於慎徽五典敬敷五教之時
善論周之教者不在惇信明義之後而在
於刑于寡妻至于兄弟之始由得其道以
先之故治易行而教易明也三代以降惟
漢俗最淳而其施之于政教者毎得先王
之遺意以孝弟教民教之誠是也然而未
及其要也以孝廉舉士舉之誠是也然而
punctuated: 王國克生之爲美也。今幸際聖世而居帝鄉，執事固稱爲首善之地矣。其敢無辭以對？請先論古帝王治教之由，而後及我聖祖、皇上之同符者，可乎？《書》有之，曰：「平章百姓，百姓昭明。」賛堯治也。《詩》有之，曰：「古之人無斁，譽髦斯士。」頌周教也。夫聖人之化理天下也，必篤近而舉遠，由親而逮疎，皆不待求諸彝倫之外。故善觀堯之治者，不在地平天成之日，而在於慎徽五典、敬敷五教之時；善論周之教者，不在惇信明義之後，而在於刑于寡妻、至于兄弟之始。由得其道以先之，故治易行而教易明也。三代以降，惟漢俗最淳，而其施之于政教者，每得先王之遺意。以孝弟教民，教之誠是也，然而未及其要也；以孝廉舉士，舉之誠是也，然而
translation_en:
…the glory of the kingdom’s bringing forth worthy men. Now, fortunately encountering a sage age and dwelling in the imperial homeland, we are in what you, sir, rightly call the place foremost in moral excellence. How could I dare offer no words in reply? May I first discuss the foundations of government and instruction under the ancient emperors and kings, and then turn to how our Sagely Founder and His Majesty accord with them?

The Book of Documents says: “He harmonized and distinguished the hundred clans, and the hundred clans became illustrious.” This praises Yao’s government. The Book of Odes says: “The men of old were tireless in nurturing these outstanding scholars.” This celebrates the instruction of the Zhou. When sages transform and govern the world, they necessarily attend earnestly to those nearby before raising up those far away, proceeding from their kin to those more distantly connected. In all this, they need seek nothing beyond the constant human relationships. Thus, those who properly examine Yao’s government look not to the day when the earth was brought to order and Heaven’s work accomplished, but to the time when he carefully fostered the five constant relationships and reverently disseminated the five teachings. Those who properly discuss Zhou instruction look not to the later strengthening of trustworthiness and clarification of righteousness, but to its beginnings in setting an example for one’s wife and extending it to one’s brothers. Because they grasped the Way and took the lead through it, government was easy to carry out and instruction easy to make clear.

After the Three Dynasties, the customs of the Han were the most wholesome, and their measures in government and instruction often captured something of the intentions bequeathed by the former kings. Teaching the people filial piety and fraternal respect was indeed right as instruction, yet it did not reach the essential point. Recommending men for office on the grounds of filial piety and incorruptibility was indeed right as selection, yet …

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
未盡其美也今以漢所紀英君考之皆不
能無遺憾焉高祖過沛而宴父老意良厚
矣猛士之思君子以為覇心之存爾彼其
遊雲夢而聞兎狗之嗟招商山而興鴻鵠
之嘆其如本之未純何至於民俗之澆漓
則有借耰鋤而德色取箕箒而誶語如賈
誼之所為太息者矣明帝臨雍而拜老更
禮亦至矣圜橋之聽君子以為彌文之飾
爾彼其撞郎而失居尊之威徵夢而啟後
===
世之惑其如教之未善何至於士習之頺
靡則有博士倚席不講學舍鞠為園蔬如
翟酺輩之所議者矣夫以漢之治教猶未
及古則唐宋之不及漢可知也自唐宋之
外其不及唐宋又可知也夫治跡比于湯
武或議其慙德之不免家法過於漢唐或
惜其武功之不競下逮胡元而彝倫攸斁
極矣天厭其亂以曆數而畀之
聖祖又以傳之
punctuated:
未盡其美也。今以漢所紀英君考之，皆不能無遺憾焉。高祖過沛而宴父老，意良厚矣。猛士之思，君子以為覇心之存爾。彼其遊雲夢而聞兎狗之嗟，招商山而興鴻鵠之嘆，其如本之未純何？至於民俗之澆漓，則有借耰鋤而德色，取箕箒而誶語，如賈誼之所為太息者矣。明帝臨雍而拜老更，禮亦至矣。圜橋之聽，君子以為彌文之飾爾。彼其撞郎而失居尊之威，徵夢而啟後世之惑，其如教之未善何？至於士習之頺靡，則有博士倚席不講，學舍鞠為園蔬，如翟酺輩之所議者矣。

夫以漢之治教猶未及古，則唐宋之不及漢可知也。自唐宋之外，其不及唐宋又可知也。夫治跡比于湯武，或議其慙德之不免；家法過於漢唐，或惜其武功之不競。下逮胡元，而彝倫攸斁極矣。天厭其亂，以曆數而畀之聖祖，又以傳之
translation_en:
…had not fully attained excellence. If we now examine the illustrious rulers recorded in Han history, none was without grounds for regret. When Gaozu passed through Pei and feasted the local elders, his intentions were indeed generous. Yet his longing for mighty warriors was, in the judgment of the gentleman, merely evidence that the ambition of a hegemon remained in his heart. When he journeyed to Yunmeng, he heard the lament about the hare and the hound; when he summoned the recluses of Shangshan, he sighed over the swan soaring aloft. What could be done about the impurity of his underlying motives? As for the deterioration of popular customs, people assumed an air of having bestowed a favor when lending a hoe or rake, and uttered abuse when someone took a basket or broom—precisely the things over which Jia Yi heaved his deep sighs. When Emperor Ming visited the Imperial University and bowed to the venerable elders, the Three Elders and Five Experienced Men, his ritual observance was indeed consummate. Yet the crowds listening around the encircling bridge were, in the gentleman’s judgment, merely an embellishment of elaborate ceremony. He struck a Gentleman of the court and thereby forfeited the dignity of his exalted position; he sought verification of a dream and thereby opened the way to the delusions of later generations. What could be done about the shortcomings of his moral instruction? As for the decline in scholars’ conduct, there were Erudites who set their teaching mats aside and did not lecture, while school premises were given over entirely to vegetable gardens—precisely the matters criticized by Zhai Pu and others.

If even Han government and moral instruction fell short of antiquity, it is plain that the Tang and Song fell short of the Han. As for dynasties beyond the Tang and Song, their inferiority to the Tang and Song is likewise plain. Though achievements in government might compare with those of Tang and Wu, some critics would still contend that their virtue was not free from grounds for shame; though the ruling house’s traditions surpassed those of the Han and Tang, some would still lament the weakness of its military accomplishments. By the time of the non-Han Yuan dynasty, the destruction of the enduring human relationships had reached its extreme. Heaven abhorred its disorder and bestowed the mandate of succession upon the Sagely Progenitor, who in turn transmitted it to…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
聖子神孫
功高萬古而化被億載固未有如
今日之美且盛者也粤稽
聖祖過淮因濠州父老來見與之宴飮而遣之
閔其遭罹兵燹且
諭曰父老宜敎導子弟爲善孝弟勤儉鄉有善
人由家有賢父兄故也斯
言也諄諄乎有家人父子之風雖
諭中原之檄
===
敎民之榜其在天下者已詳而于湯沐之邑
尤加意焉其視徒誇海内之威者相遠矣
聖祖即位之初
諭中書省臣曰兵變以來人習於戰鬪惟知干
戈莫識爼豆恒謂治國之要敎化爲先敎化
之道學校爲本今京師雖有太學而天下學
校未興宜令郡縣皆立學禮延師儒敎授生
徒以講論聖道使人日漸月化以復先王之
舊以革汙染之習斯
punctuated:
聖子神孫，功高萬古，而化被億載，固未有如今日之美且盛者也。粤稽聖祖過淮，因濠州父老來見，與之宴飮而遣之，閔其遭罹兵燹，且諭曰：「父老宜敎導子弟爲善，孝弟勤儉。鄉有善人，由家有賢父兄故也。」斯言也，諄諄乎有家人父子之風。雖諭中原之檄、敎民之榜，其在天下者已詳，而于湯沐之邑尤加意焉。其視徒誇海内之威者，相遠矣。
聖祖即位之初，諭中書省臣曰：「兵變以來，人習於戰鬪，惟知干戈，莫識爼豆。恒謂治國之要，敎化爲先；敎化之道，學校爲本。今京師雖有太學，而天下學校未興，宜令郡縣皆立學，禮延師儒，敎授生徒，以講論聖道，使人日漸月化，以復先王之舊，以革汙染之習。」斯
translation_en:
…to his sagely sons and divine descendants. Their achievements surpass those of all antiquity, and their transforming influence extends through countless ages. Surely there has never been anything as splendid and flourishing as the present day. Looking back, when the Sagely Founder passed the Huai River, elders of Haozhou came to see him. He feasted with them before sending them on their way, pitying them for the devastation they had suffered in war. He also instructed them: “You elders should teach your sons and younger brothers to do good, to be filial and respectful toward elder brothers, diligent and frugal. A village has good people because its households have worthy fathers and elder brothers.” These earnest words had the spirit of fathers and sons speaking within a family. Although his proclamation to the Central Plain and his posted notices instructing the people already set out his teachings for the realm in detail, he devoted particular attention to his native place. How far removed he was from those who merely boasted of their might throughout the empire!
At the beginning of his reign, the Sagely Founder instructed the officials of the Secretariat: “Since the upheavals of war, people have grown accustomed to fighting. They know only shields and spears, and understand nothing of sacrificial stands and vessels. I have always maintained that moral instruction comes first among the essentials of governing a state, and that schools are the foundation of moral instruction. Although the capital now has an Imperial University, schools have not yet been established throughout the realm. Let every prefecture and county establish schools, courteously invite learned Confucian teachers to instruct students, and expound and discuss the Way of the sages. Thus people may gradually be transformed, day by day and month by month, restoring the ancient ways of the former kings and reforming their corrupted habits.” These…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
言也諷諷乎有典謨訓誥之義雖
禮儀定式
孝慈諸錄其教天下者已具而于學校之典尤
特隆焉其視自炫馬上之治者敻異矣
列聖相承重熙累洽曁我
皇上肇迹郢中誕膺
天命故
道化之敷光于四表而特顯于南國考其
崇親明倫勒成大典頃因
===
大狩駐驛承天則
弘仁達孝之實昭矣及
諭父老首敘
皇考積德之由備舉父子長幼之道慮民之未
知也因俗為
文以曉之是即皇極敷言之意也是與
聖祖之治同道者也他若復其田租錄其工役
所以
治民者甚切而其加
punctuated:
言也，諷諷乎有典謨訓誥之義。雖《禮儀定式》《孝慈》諸錄，其教天下者已具，而于學校之典尤特隆焉。其視自炫馬上之治者，敻異矣。
列聖相承，重熙累洽。曁我皇上肇迹郢中，誕膺天命，故道化之敷，光于四表，而特顯于南國。考其崇親明倫，勒成大典。頃因大狩，駐驛承天，則弘仁達孝之實昭矣。及諭父老，首敘皇考積德之由，備舉父子長幼之道，慮民之未知也，因俗為文以曉之。是即皇極敷言之意也，是與聖祖之治同道者也。他若復其田租，錄其工役，所以治民者甚切，而其加
translation_en:
…these words resound [?] with the import of the canons, counsels, instructions, and proclamations of antiquity. Although the Standards of Ritual and Ceremonial and the records on Filial Piety and Parental Kindness already fully provided instruction for the realm, he attached especially great importance to the institutions of schooling. How utterly different this was from those who vaunted their rule from horseback!
Successive sage emperors carried on this legacy, accumulating brilliance and prosperity. Our present Emperor began his rise in Ying and received Heaven’s mandate in its fullness. Thus the moral transformation he spreads shines to the four outermost regions, but is especially manifest in the southern lands. Consider how he honored his parents and clarified human relationships, having these matters inscribed in a great compendium. Recently, on his imperial hunting tour, he stopped at Chengtian, where the reality of his expansive benevolence and consummate filial piety became manifest. When he addressed the local elders, he began by recounting how his deceased imperial father had accumulated virtue, and fully expounded the proper relationships between fathers and sons, elders and juniors. Concerned that the people might not understand, he composed a text suited to their customs to enlighten them. This is precisely the intent of the passage on promulgating instruction in the “Sovereign’s Ultimate Standard”; it follows the same Way as the governance of the Sagely Founder. Other measures, such as remitting their land taxes and recording their labor services, show how earnestly he attended to governing the people, while what he further bestowed…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
惠者蓋甚渥也
獻皇就國之始
親幸孔學
命官講周易
賚之寶鏹更出
內帑以葺廟宇
皇上紀述不忘則崇儒重道之心至矣曁諸臣
以學碑請于
朝特
===
可其奏表章
皇考視學之詳其
文有曰建學所以明倫倫莫大於父子君臣明
父子之親則天下知孝明君臣之義則天下
知忠我
皇考惓惓加意學校正欲敎民以忠孝耳又
曰學孔子之道其可不盡夫彝倫之實爲子盡
孝爲臣盡忠是即孝思維則之意也是與
聖祖之敎同道者也他若增廩生之員加解士
punctuated:
惠者蓋甚渥也。
獻皇就國之始，親幸孔學，命官講周易，賚之寶鏹，更出內帑以葺廟宇。皇上紀述不忘，則崇儒重道之心至矣。曁諸臣以學碑請于朝，特可其奏，表章皇考視學之詳。其文有曰：「建學所以明倫，倫莫大於父子、君臣。明父子之親，則天下知孝；明君臣之義，則天下知忠。我皇考惓惓加意學校，正欲敎民以忠孝耳。」又曰：「學孔子之道，其可不盡夫彝倫之實？爲子盡孝，爲臣盡忠。」是即孝思維則之意也，是與聖祖之敎同道者也。他若增廩生之員，加解士
translation_en:
…the favors bestowed were indeed most generous.
When Emperor Xian first took up residence in his princely domain, he personally visited the Confucian school, ordered an official to lecture on the Book of Changes (Zhouyi), and rewarded him with precious coin. He further drew on his privy treasury to repair the temple buildings. His Majesty recorded these deeds without letting them be forgotten: his devotion to honoring Confucian learning and esteeming the Way was thus unsurpassed. When the officials petitioned the court for a school stele, he specially approved their memorial, making manifest the details of his imperial father's visit to the school. His text said: “Schools are established to illuminate human relationships. Among these, none is greater than that between father and son or ruler and minister. When affection between father and son is made clear, all under Heaven understand filial piety; when the rightful duties between ruler and minister are made clear, all under Heaven understand loyalty. My imperial father devoted unremitting attention to schools precisely because he wished to teach the people loyalty and filial piety.” It also said: “In studying the Way of Confucius, how can one fail to fulfill the substance of the enduring human relationships? As a son, fulfill filial piety; as a minister, fulfill loyalty.” This is precisely the meaning of “taking filial thoughts as one's rule,” and follows the same Way as the teachings of the sagely progenitor. Other measures included increasing the number of stipend students and increasing the provincial candidates’…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之額所以
敎士者甚隆而其致
望者蓋甚殷也自
皇上御極以來垂及四紀九德咸事百度惟貞
萬物阜寧
三靈鬯遂舉天下而囿之菁莪棫樸之化且從
擊壤之歌以詠
帝力焉治敎休明於斯極矣當
聖祖時載筆之賢如宋濂王禕紀述其事而錄
===
于
大明日曆
聖政記至于
金匱石室之藏有不可盡讀者今
皇上功德之隆追媲
聖祖卽使文學侍從之臣有如吉甫奚斯之徒
猶不足摸擬神化形之雅頌而況草莽之
士哉然竊觀
聖祖
punctuated:
之額，所以敎士者甚隆，而其致望者蓋甚殷也。自皇上御極以來，垂及四紀，九德咸事，百度惟貞，萬物阜寧，三靈鬯遂，舉天下而囿之菁莪棫樸之化，且從擊壤之歌以詠帝力焉。治敎休明，於斯極矣。
當聖祖時，載筆之賢如宋濂、王禕，紀述其事而錄于《大明日曆》、《聖政記》，至于金匱石室之藏，有不可盡讀者。今皇上功德之隆，追媲聖祖，卽使文學侍從之臣有如吉甫、奚斯之徒，猶不足摸擬神化，形之雅頌，而況草莽之士哉？然竊觀聖祖
translation_en:
…the quota: the provisions for educating scholars were most generous, and the expectations placed upon them were indeed most earnest. Since His Majesty ascended the throne, nearly four twelve-year cycles have elapsed. All nine virtues have been put into practice; every institution is rightly ordered; all things flourish in peace; and the three numinous powers unfold unhindered. The entire realm has been embraced within the transforming influence celebrated in the odes “Luxuriant Southernwood” (Jing E) and “Dense-Growing Oaks” (Yu Pu). People also join in the “Song of Beating the Ground” to sing of the emperor’s power. Good government and enlightened instruction have here reached their height.
In the time of the Sacred Ancestor, worthy wielders of the brush such as Song Lian and Wang Yi chronicled his deeds in the Daily Record of the Great Ming and the Record of Sagely Government. As for the writings preserved in golden coffers and stone chambers, they are more than one could read in full. Now His Majesty’s exalted achievements and virtue rival those of the Sacred Ancestor. Even if his literary attendants included men such as Jifu and Xi Si, they would still be unable adequately to represent his wondrous transforming influence and give it expression in elegant odes and hymns. How much less could a scholar from the countryside do so! Yet I humbly observe that the Sacred Ancestor…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
皇上化理天下之道莫不有本焉
聖祖固言之矣
曰人君一心治化之本存於中者無堯舜之心
而欲發於政者有堯舜之治不可得也故
聖祖存心有錄
觀心有亭皆所以培植是道而
垂創業之弘規
皇上敬一有箴
心箴有註皆所以發明斯道而
===
章守成之懿軌與堯之克明峻德文之亦臨
亦保蓋不期而同者矣此皆惇彝倫脩治
敎之大端也嘗聞治之極者其卦爲泰正
君子道長之時也聖人常致愼於復隍之
戒洪範之九疇本諸彝倫攸敘者而於錫
民保極之旨尤丁寧焉故究言五福明福
壽之所由臻也
皇上德合天地
化侔陰陽其於保泰綏福之機必有深契于
punctuated: 皇上化理天下之道，莫不有本焉。聖祖固言之矣，曰：「人君一心，治化之本。存於中者無堯舜之心，而欲發於政者有堯舜之治，不可得也。」故聖祖存心有錄，觀心有亭，皆所以培植是道，而垂創業之弘規。皇上敬一有箴，心箴有註，皆所以發明斯道，而章守成之懿軌，與堯之克明峻德、文之亦臨亦保，蓋不期而同者矣。此皆惇彝倫、脩治敎之大端也。嘗聞治之極者，其卦爲泰，正君子道長之時也。聖人常致愼於復隍之戒。《洪範》之九疇，本諸彝倫攸敘者，而於錫民保極之旨尤丁寧焉，故究言五福，明福壽之所由臻也。皇上德合天地，化侔陰陽，其於保泰綏福之機，必有深契于
translation_en:
…the ways by which Your Majesty transforms and governs all under Heaven invariably have a foundation. The sagely founder indeed expressed it: “The ruler’s mind alone is the foundation of government and moral transformation. If what he harbors within is not the mind of Yao and Shun, yet he wishes what issues forth in his administration to be the government of Yao and Shun, this cannot be attained.” Thus the sagely founder had a record concerning the preservation of the mind and a pavilion for contemplating the mind. These served to nurture this Way and bequeath the grand pattern for founding the dynasty. Your Majesty has an admonition on reverently maintaining oneness and commentaries on admonitions concerning the mind. These serve to elucidate this Way and manifest the excellent model for preserving the inherited achievement. They accord, without deliberate contrivance, with Yao’s ability to “make manifest his lofty virtue” and King Wen’s “watching over and protecting.” These are all essential means of strengthening the enduring human relationships and perfecting government and instruction.

I have heard that the hexagram representing government at its height is Peace (Tai), precisely the time when the way of the noble man flourishes. The sage nevertheless remains ever mindful of the warning that “the city wall falls back into the moat.” The nine divisions of the Great Plan (Hongfan) are rooted in the proper ordering of the enduring human relationships, and are especially emphatic about the purport of bestowing blessings upon the people and preserving the supreme standard. Hence the text discusses the five blessings fully, making clear how blessings and longevity are attained. Your Majesty’s virtue accords with Heaven and Earth, and your transforming influence matches yin and yang. As for the crucial means of preserving peace and securing blessings, there must surely be a profound accord within…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
宸衷而交盡其道者固非管窺所能及然區區
獻曝之忱皆於佔畢間得之不識亦可
進而
聞之否也
第二問
陳述齡
同考試官敎諭陳批求忠於孝移孝於忠
無異道也我
祖宗示萬世臣子之極
===
謨訓具在子能受簡而敬陳之是達觀其深矣
同考試官敎諭吳批漢儒忠經之作與孝
經相發明至我
祖宗貽訓忠孝之道益顯是篇獨得其典要豈徒佔畢之士巳哉
考試官敎授蔣批臣子事君父之道子
能領會於
典章經傳之間執此以往庶幾平可謂能臣子矣願爲推轂不辭焉
考試官敎授桂批忠孝一道我
祖宗垂訓之意正如此此篇出入經傳發明
punctuated:
宸衷，而交盡其道者，固非管窺所能及。然區區獻曝之忱，皆於佔畢間得之，不識亦可進而聞之否也？

第二問
陳述齡

同考試官敎諭陳批：求忠於孝，移孝於忠，無異道也。我祖宗示萬世臣子之極，謨訓具在。子能受簡而敬陳之，是達觀其深矣。

同考試官敎諭吳批：漢儒忠經之作，與孝經相發明。至我祖宗貽訓，忠孝之道益顯。是篇獨得其典要，豈徒佔畢之士巳哉！

考試官敎授蔣批：臣子事君父之道，子能領會於典章經傳之間。執此以往，庶幾平，可謂能臣子矣。願爲推轂，不辭焉。

考試官敎授桂批：忠孝一道，我祖宗垂訓之意正如此。此篇出入經傳，發明
translation_en:
…within Your Majesty’s imperial heart, and fully realizing these principles together, surely lie beyond my narrow understanding. Yet this humble sincerity in offering what little I have—as one might offer the warmth of the sun—comes entirely from my reading. I do not know whether it, too, may be presented for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Second Policy Question
Chen Shuling 陳述齡

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: To seek loyalty in filial devotion and to transfer filial devotion to loyalty are not different ways. Our imperial ancestors established the ultimate standard for subjects and sons for all ages; their counsels and instructions remain fully preserved. Having received the writing tablets, you have respectfully set these forth: this shows a penetrating understanding of their depth.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: The Classic of Loyalty, composed by Han Confucians, and the Classic of Filial Piety illuminate one another. With the instructions bequeathed by our imperial ancestors, the way of loyalty and filial devotion became still clearer. This essay has uniquely grasped their essential principles. Surely its author is more than a scholar confined to textual study!

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: You have grasped, through institutions and regulations, the classics and their commentaries, the way in which subjects and sons should serve their rulers and fathers. Carry this understanding forward, and you may come close to the ideal [?]; you may then be called an able subject and son. I am willing to recommend you and will not decline to do so.

Comment by Examiner Gui, Professor: Loyalty and filial devotion constitute a single way. This is precisely the intent of the instructions handed down by our imperial ancestors. This essay ranges through the classics and their commentaries, elucidating…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
聖謨非口耳之學所能及資適逢世於子日望之
君子之於天下無所逃者義也不可解者
心也素位而行者分也易地而皆然者道
也懷義以事君謂之忠因心以事親謂之
孝分殊而推行之謂之守經道一而會通
之謂之達變人見君子之事親也而不知
其有忠存焉故曰孝者所以事君也人見
君子之事君也而不知其有孝存焉故曰
家有嚴君父母之謂也明於此然後可與
===
論忠孝之說矣世有恒言皆曰天下不皆
舜而後舜有孝之名天下不皆忠而後周
公有忠之名夫舜之事瞽瞍非以孝自異
也盡吾心而已盡吾心而親不吾愛是吾
罪也幸而愛之是親之德也天下不知舜
有焚廩捐階之危而仰其有底豫之化雖
象之傲吾何知焉周公之於成王亦非以
忠自異也盡吾義而已盡吾義而君不吾
諒是吾過也幸而諒之是君之明也天下
punctuated:
聖謨，非口耳之學所能及。資適逢世，於子日望之。

君子之於天下，無所逃者義也，不可解者心也，素位而行者分也，易地而皆然者道也。懷義以事君謂之忠，因心以事親謂之孝，分殊而推行之謂之守經，道一而會通之謂之達變。人見君子之事親也，而不知其有忠存焉，故曰：「孝者所以事君也。」人見君子之事君也，而不知其有孝存焉，故曰：「家有嚴君，父母之謂也。」明於此，然後可與論忠孝之說矣。世有恒言，皆曰：「天下不皆舜，而後舜有孝之名；天下不皆忠，而後周公有忠之名。」夫舜之事瞽瞍，非以孝自異也，盡吾心而已。盡吾心而親不吾愛，是吾罪也；幸而愛之，是親之德也。天下不知舜有焚廩捐階之危，而仰其有底豫之化。雖象之傲，吾何知焉？周公之於成王，亦非以忠自異也，盡吾義而已。盡吾義而君不吾諒，是吾過也；幸而諒之，是君之明也。天下
translation_en:
…the sage counsels, beyond the reach of learning confined to the lips and ears. May your abilities meet a favorable age [?]; this is what I daily hope for you.

For the gentleman in the world, what he cannot evade is righteousness; what he cannot set aside is his moral heart; acting according to his station is his allotted duty; and what holds true even when positions are exchanged is the Way. Serving one’s ruler with righteousness in one’s heart is called loyalty; serving one’s parents from the heart is called filial piety. Carrying these out according to distinct duties is called upholding the constant norm; comprehending their interconnection through the unity of the Way is called mastering adaptation to circumstances. People see the gentleman serving his parents but do not know that loyalty resides in this. Thus it is said: “Filial piety is the means by which one serves one’s ruler.” People see the gentleman serving his ruler but do not know that filial piety resides in this. Thus it is said: “Within the family there are stern rulers: this refers to the father and mother.” Only once someone understands this can one discuss loyalty and filial piety with him.

There is a common saying: “Only because not everyone under Heaven is a Shun does Shun have a reputation for filial piety; only because not everyone under Heaven is loyal does the Duke of Zhou have a reputation for loyalty.” When Shun served Gusou, he did not seek to distinguish himself through filial piety. He merely gave his whole heart: “If I give my whole heart and my parent does not love me, that is my fault. If, fortunately, he does love me, that is my parent’s virtue.” The world knows nothing of Shun’s peril when the granary was set ablaze and the ladder removed, but admires his transforming influence in bringing his father to contentment. “Even with Xiang’s arrogance, what notice do I take of it?”

Likewise, in his relationship with King Cheng, the Duke of Zhou did not seek to distinguish himself through loyalty. He merely fulfilled his obligations of righteousness: “If I fulfill my obligations and my ruler does not understand me, that is my failing. If, fortunately, he does understand me, that is my ruler’s discernment.” All under Heaven…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
不知公有破斧缺斨之勞而致其袞衣之
思雖管蔡之謗吾無患焉故舜之大孝周
公之純忠卒以是稱於天下而後世誦之
不衰自舜與周公觀之則皆吾分之常而
已矣故舜之孝非不足於忠而周公之忠
亦非不足於孝也以敘百揆以徽五典而
唐虞之際於斯盛焉舜之忠又何純也善
繼其志善述其事而文武之德於是成焉
周公之孝又何大也書紀舜之祗載而表
夔夔之誠孟子固以盡臣道與之可謂深
知舜者矣詩詠周公之碩膚而頌几几之
美夫子且以達孝與之可謂深知周公者
矣夫君親之倫原諸性者也忠孝之道根
諸心者也以心盡倫以倫盡性而君子之
道備矣是故由事親而充之則其為祗服
為幾諫為幹蠱用譽為就養無方子道也
凡屬乎子道者皆孝也由事君而推之則
其為承順為責難為鞠躬盡瘁為見危授
punctuated:
不知公有破斧缺斨之勞，而致其袞衣之思，雖管蔡之謗，吾無患焉。故舜之大孝、周公之純忠，卒以是稱於天下，而後世誦之不衰。自舜與周公觀之，則皆吾分之常而已矣。故舜之孝，非不足於忠；而周公之忠，亦非不足於孝也。以敘百揆，以徽五典，而唐虞之際於斯盛焉，舜之忠又何純也！善繼其志，善述其事，而文武之德於是成焉，周公之孝又何大也！書紀舜之祗載，而表夔夔之誠，孟子固以盡臣道與之，可謂深知舜者矣。詩詠周公之碩膚，而頌几几之美，夫子且以達孝與之，可謂深知周公者矣。
夫君親之倫，原諸性者也；忠孝之道，根諸心者也。以心盡倫，以倫盡性，而君子之道備矣。是故由事親而充之，則其為祗服，為幾諫，為幹蠱用譽，為就養無方，子道也。凡屬乎子道者，皆孝也。由事君而推之，則其為承順，為責難，為鞠躬盡瘁，為見危授
translation_en:
…do not know the Duke’s toil, in which axes were broken and hatchets chipped, yet they cherish thoughts of him in his ceremonial robes. Even amid the slanders of Guan and Cai, he could say, “I have nothing to fear.” Thus Shun’s great filial devotion and the Duke of Zhou’s pure loyalty ultimately won them acclaim throughout the world, and later generations have praised them without cease. From the standpoint of Shun and the Duke of Zhou themselves, however, these were merely the ordinary duties of their station.
