Shun’s filial devotion therefore did not mean that he was deficient in loyalty, nor did the Duke of Zhou’s loyalty mean that he was deficient in filial devotion. By ordering the hundred affairs of government and bringing harmony to the five cardinal relationships, Shun brought the age of Tang and Yu to its flourishing height. How pure, then, was Shun’s loyalty! By ably carrying on their aspirations and continuing their undertakings, the Duke of Zhou brought the virtue of Kings Wen and Wu to completion. How great, then, was the Duke of Zhou’s filial devotion! The Book of Documents records Shun’s reverent discharge of his duties and makes manifest the sincerity of his humble reverence. Mengzi indeed credited him with fully realizing the way of a minister: he may be said to have understood Shun deeply. The Book of Odes sings of the Duke of Zhou’s great achievements and praises the beauty of his dignified bearing. Confucius also credited him with consummate filial devotion: he may be said to have understood the Duke of Zhou deeply.
The relationships with sovereign and parents originate in human nature; the ways of loyalty and filial devotion are rooted in the heart. By bringing the heart fully to bear upon these relationships, and through these relationships fully realizing one’s nature, the way of the gentleman becomes complete. Thus, extending the principle of serving one’s parents encompasses reverent obedience, gentle remonstrance, correcting their faults and thereby earning praise, and providing for their needs without a fixed method: these constitute the way of a son. Everything belonging to the way of a son is filial devotion. Extending the principle of serving one’s sovereign encompasses compliance, urging him to undertake what is difficult, bending oneself to service and exhausting one’s strength, and, in the face of danger, offering…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
命臣道也凡屬乎臣道者皆忠也書曰敬
敷五教曰天敘五典夫人之有五倫乆矣
而君親爲重至孔子始言之故傳曰父母
生之恩莫大焉君親臨之厚莫重焉此忠
孝之名所由以立通乎古今不可易也考
之記籍其論忠孝多矣曰邇之事父遠之
事君曰爲人臣止於敬爲人子止於孝曰
事父母能竭其力事君能致其身言乎其
分之殊也曰夫孝始於事親中於事君曰
===
資於事父以事君而敬同曰事親孝則忠
可移於君言乎其理之一也至於魯論所
紀如以無違對懿子以敬養告子游以色
難語子夏似若言孝而不及忠者然勿欺
而犯之訓子路甞聞之事上之敬子産以
此見稱而以道事君之誼則又斥由求之
爲具臣矣然則聖人之所爲訓固無所不
備也夫道在天下所恃以常存者惟心而
已是爲天經是爲地義是爲民之秉彜古
punctuated:
命，臣道也。凡屬乎臣道者，皆忠也。《書》曰：「敬敷五教。」曰：「天敘五典。」夫人之有五倫乆矣，而君親爲重，至孔子始言之。故傳曰：「父母生之，恩莫大焉；君親臨之，厚莫重焉。」此忠孝之名所由以立，通乎古今不可易也。考之記籍，其論忠孝多矣。曰：「邇之事父，遠之事君。」曰：「爲人臣，止於敬；爲人子，止於孝。」曰：「事父母，能竭其力；事君，能致其身。」言乎其分之殊也。曰：「夫孝，始於事親，中於事君。」曰：「資於事父以事君，而敬同。」曰：「事親孝，則忠可移於君。」言乎其理之一也。
至於《魯論》所紀，如以「無違」對懿子，以「敬養」告子游，以「色難」語子夏，似若言孝而不及忠者。然「勿欺而犯」之訓，子路甞聞之；事上之敬，子産以此見稱；而以道事君之誼，則又斥由、求之爲具臣矣。然則聖人之所爲訓，固無所不備也。夫道在天下，所恃以常存者，惟心而已。是爲天經，是爲地義，是爲民之秉彜。古
translation_en:
…to give up one’s life: these belong to the way of a minister. Everything belonging to the way of a minister is loyalty. The Book of Documents says, “Reverently disseminate the five teachings,” and, “Heaven has ordered the five constant relationships.” The five human relationships have long existed, with those involving ruler and parents carrying the greatest weight; yet it was only with Confucius that this was first articulated. Thus the transmitted text says, “Parents give one life: no kindness is greater. The ruler personally presides over one: no beneficence is weightier.” This is how the terms loyalty and filial piety came to be established; they hold good throughout antiquity and the present and cannot be changed. Examining the written records, we find many discussions of loyalty and filial piety. They say, “Close at hand, serve one’s father; farther afield, serve one’s ruler”; “As a minister, abide in reverence; as a son, abide in filial piety”; and “In serving parents, exert all one’s strength; in serving the ruler, devote one’s person.” These speak of the distinctions between their respective duties. They also say, “Filial piety begins with serving parents and continues with serving the ruler”; “Draw upon service to one’s father in serving one’s ruler: the reverence is the same”; and “If one serves one’s parents filially, that loyalty can be transferred to the ruler.” These speak of the unity of their underlying principle.
As for what is recorded in the Lu Analects, such as answering Yizi with “Do not transgress,” instructing Ziyou about “providing support with reverence,” and telling Zixia that “maintaining the proper countenance is difficult,” these appear to discuss filial piety without touching on loyalty. Yet Zilu had heard the instruction, “Do not deceive him, but confront him”; Zichan was praised for his reverence in serving his superiors; and, concerning the obligation to serve one’s ruler according to the Way, Confucius also reproached You and Qiu as ministers who merely filled their posts. Thus the sage’s teachings were indeed comprehensive, leaving nothing unaddressed. For the Way to endure in the world, it depends solely upon the heart. This is Heaven’s constant norm, Earth’s proper order, and the enduring moral nature held by the people. The ancients…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
人作經皆以明此心也孝經一書成於曾
子門人之手首論孝之終始則敷陳天子
諸侯卿大夫士庶人之職而末結之曰孝
無終始其論孝無餘道矣或議其非純爲
夫子之言蓋其言出於夫子而煨燼之餘
或有遺爾若忠經一書乃漢儒馬融擬孝
經而作者也自天子以至兆人凡十有八
章蓋與孝經相爲表裏雖其論天子之忠
兆人之忠不專爲人臣者訓然其意亦善
===
矣或疑其據引敷析不能盡當未免僭經
之失要之欲明常道何嘗有戾於經耶我
成祖文皇帝懲元綱常之亂
作孝順事實其紀孝行凡二百有七人帝王
之孝有若舜之齊慄文王之問安者焉賢
哲之孝有若曾參之養志仲由之盡力者
焉處常之孝有若黃香李密焉處變之孝
有若伯奇閔損焉其他爲孝不同皆可以
教天下之爲人子者也我
punctuated:
人作經，皆以明此心也。《孝經》一書，成於曾子門人之手，首論孝之終始，則敷陳天子、諸侯、卿大夫、士庶人之職，而末結之曰：「孝無終始。」其論孝無餘道矣。或議其非純爲夫子之言，蓋其言出於夫子，而煨燼之餘，或有遺爾。若《忠經》一書，乃漢儒馬融擬《孝經》而作者也。自天子以至兆人，凡十有八章，蓋與《孝經》相爲表裏。雖其論天子之忠、兆人之忠，不專爲人臣者訓，然其意亦善矣。或疑其據引敷析不能盡當，未免僭經之失。要之，欲明常道，何嘗有戾於經耶？
我成祖文皇帝懲元綱常之亂，作《孝順事實》。其紀孝行，凡二百有七人。帝王之孝，有若舜之齊慄、文王之問安者焉；賢哲之孝，有若曾參之養志、仲由之盡力者焉；處常之孝，有若黃香、李密焉；處變之孝，有若伯奇、閔損焉。其他爲孝不同，皆可以教天下之爲人子者也。我
translation_en:
…the men who composed the classics all sought to illuminate this heart. The Classic of Filial Piety (Xiaojing) was compiled by the disciples of Zengzi. It first discusses the beginning and culmination of filial piety, then sets forth the duties of the Son of Heaven, the feudal lords, ministers and grand masters, and the shi and common people, and concludes by saying: “Filial piety has neither end nor beginning.” Its discussion leaves nothing further to be said about filial piety. Some contend that it does not consist entirely of the Master's words. Its sayings did indeed come from the Master, but some may have been lost in the aftermath of the burning of the books. As for the Classic of Loyalty (Zhongjing), it was composed by the Han scholar Ma Rong in imitation of the Classic of Filial Piety. Its eighteen chapters extend from the Son of Heaven down to the multitude of the people, complementing the Classic of Filial Piety as outer and inner aspects of a whole. Although its discussions of the loyalty of the Son of Heaven and of the multitude are not instructions exclusively for subjects serving a ruler, its intent is nevertheless good. Some question whether its citations and expositions are entirely appropriate, suggesting that it cannot escape the fault of presumptuously claiming the standing of a classic. Ultimately, however, its aim is to clarify the constant Way: how could it ever be at odds with the classics?
Our Emperor Wen, Chengzu, taking warning from the disorder of the cardinal relationships and constant virtues under the Yuan, composed the True Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi). It records the filial conduct of 207 people. Among emperors and kings, there are examples such as Shun's reverent apprehension and King Wen's inquiries after his father's well-being. Among worthies and sages, there are examples such as Zeng Shen's nurturing of his father's aspirations and Zhong You's exerting himself to the utmost for his parents. Huang Xiang and Li Mi exemplify filial piety in ordinary circumstances; Bo Qi and Min Sun exemplify it amid adversity. The others practised filial piety in differing ways, but all can serve to instruct everyone under Heaven who is a child of parents. Our …

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
宣宗章皇帝思古明良之戒
作為臣鑒其敘臣事凡二百八十餘人善可
為法則始於鄭子產焉惡可為戒則始於
漢田蚡焉漢之蕭曹唐之房杜皆善之類
也唐之李林甫盧杞宋之呂惠卿蔡京皆
惡之類也其他為事不同固所以教天下
之為人臣者也然二書祇舉其重而於彝
倫之訓尚有未備故
章皇帝復
===
命儒臣編緝
五倫書以
頒示臣民其敘臣道也始於輔德終於恬退
又以補臣鑒之所未足而特予其善也其
敘子道也始於伯奇終於劉氏又以明事
實之所嘗載而特致其詳也
聖訓神謨昭映方策所以示彰癉於既往垂勸
懲于將來雖古帝王之誕告萬方訓迪百
官者何以加此天下臣民彬彬向風爭自
punctuated:
宣宗章皇帝思古明良之戒，作《為臣鑒》。其敘臣事，凡二百八十餘人。善可為法，則始於鄭子產焉；惡可為戒，則始於漢田蚡焉。漢之蕭曹、唐之房杜，皆善之類也；唐之李林甫、盧杞，宋之呂惠卿、蔡京，皆惡之類也。其他為事不同，固所以教天下之為人臣者也。
然二書祇舉其重，而於彝倫之訓尚有未備，故章皇帝復命儒臣編緝《五倫書》，以頒示臣民。其敘臣道也，始於輔德，終於恬退，又以補《臣鑒》之所未足，而特予其善也。其敘子道也，始於伯奇，終於劉氏，又以明《事實》之所嘗載，而特致其詳也。
聖訓神謨，昭映方策，所以示彰癉於既往，垂勸懲于將來。雖古帝王之誕告萬方、訓迪百官者，何以加此？天下臣民彬彬向風，爭自
translation_en:
… Emperor Xuanzong Zhang reflected on the admonitions of antiquity concerning enlightened rulers and worthy ministers and composed the Mirror for Ministers (Wei chen jian). Its accounts of ministers’ deeds cover more than 280 people. Those whose goodness could serve as a model begin with Zichan of Zheng; those whose wickedness could serve as a warning begin with Tian Fen of the Han. Xiao He and Cao Can of the Han, and Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui of the Tang, all belong to the good category. Li Linfu and Lu Qi of the Tang, and Lü Huiqing and Cai Jing of the Song, all belong to the wicked category. The others differed in their conduct, but their accounts likewise serve to instruct all who act as ministers throughout the realm.
Yet these two books addressed only the most important matters, leaving their instruction in the enduring human relationships incomplete. Emperor Zhang therefore again ordered Confucian officials to compile the Book of the Five Relationships (Wulun shu), for promulgation to his ministers and people. Its account of the minister’s way begins with assisting the ruler’s virtue and ends with retiring contentedly. It thus supplements what the Mirror for Ministers left incomplete, giving particular approval to good conduct. Its account of the child’s way begins with Boqi and ends with a person of the Liu clan [?]. It further elucidates what the Accounts of Filial Piety and Obedience had recorded, treating it in particular detail.
These sagely instructions and inspired counsels shine forth from the written pages. They display praise and censure of the past and bequeath encouragement and warning to the future. Even the ancient emperors and kings, in their great proclamations to the myriad regions and their instruction of the hundred officials, could hardly surpass this. Throughout the realm, ministers and people respond with cultured refinement to this transforming influence, vying themselves to …

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
效其忠孝之誠寧有紀極哉夫
皇建其有極用敷錫厥庶民則啟迪之本也是
訓是行以近
天子之光則率從之機也如是而有淫朋比德
焉者否矣夫人莫不有忠孝之心也亦莫
不欲忠孝之名在其身也天下之為父者
願得以為子天下之為君者願得以為臣
然而忠孝之道日以衰熄者由倡之無術
而適之非其路也或曰念顧復之恩而為
===
孝則其孝必不至懷祿位之寵而為忠則
其忠必不盡此責備之意非通俗之見也
樹木以時伐禽獸以時殺君子與其孝則
天下相慕而為孝者多矣見路馬而不齒
過闕而必下車君子許其忠則天下相效
而為忠者衆矣或者又曰承親以成名不
必更求其忠從王以用譽不必復考其孝
此又執一之談非議道之心也不順乎親
不可以為子以事君未能矣不獲乎上不
punctuated: 效其忠孝之誠，寧有紀極哉？夫「皇建其有極，用敷錫厥庶民」，則啟迪之本也；「是訓是行，以近天子之光」，則率從之機也。如是而有淫朋比德焉者，否矣。夫人莫不有忠孝之心也，亦莫不欲忠孝之名在其身也。天下之為父者願得以為子，天下之為君者願得以為臣。然而忠孝之道日以衰熄者，由倡之無術而適之非其路也。或曰：「念顧復之恩而為孝，則其孝必不至；懷祿位之寵而為忠，則其忠必不盡。」此責備之意，非通俗之見也。樹木以時伐，禽獸以時殺，君子與其孝，則天下相慕而為孝者多矣；見路馬而不齒，過闕而必下車，君子許其忠，則天下相效而為忠者衆矣。或者又曰：「承親以成名，不必更求其忠；從王以用譽，不必復考其孝。」此又執一之談，非議道之心也。不順乎親，不可以為子，以事君未能矣；不獲乎上，不
translation_en:
…to demonstrate the sincerity of their loyalty and filial devotion—could there be any limit to this? “The sovereign establishes the supreme standard and thereby extends its blessings to the common people”: this is the foundation of their enlightenment. “Follow these instructions and put them into practice, thereby drawing near to the radiance of the Son of Heaven”: this is what moves them to follow. With matters thus ordered, could there still be those who form depraved factions and band together in wickedness? No.

Everyone possesses a heart capable of loyalty and filial devotion, and everyone wishes to enjoy a reputation for these virtues. Every father in the realm wishes to have such a person as his son; every ruler wishes to have such a person as his minister. Yet the way of loyalty and filial devotion declines and fades daily because the means of promoting it are inadequate and the path taken toward it is wrong. Some say: “If one practices filial devotion out of gratitude for the kindness of parental care, that devotion will necessarily fall short of perfection; if one practices loyalty out of attachment to the favor of salary and rank, that loyalty will necessarily fall short of completeness.” This expresses a demand for perfection; it is not a view suited to ordinary people.

When someone fells trees and kills birds and beasts only at the proper seasons, and the gentleman approves his filial devotion, many throughout the realm will emulate him and practice filial devotion. When someone refrains from examining the teeth of the ruler’s carriage horses to determine their age, and invariably dismounts from his carriage when passing the palace gate towers, and the gentleman acknowledges his loyalty, many throughout the realm will imitate him and practice loyalty.

Others say: “If someone has won a reputation by serving his parents, there is no need further to demand loyalty of him; if someone has gained renown by following his king, there is no need also to examine his filial devotion.” This, too, is a one-sided argument, not the disposition of someone seeking to discuss the Way. One who is not obedient to his parents cannot fulfill the role of a son and is as yet incapable of serving his ruler. One who has not gained the confidence of his superiors cannot…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
可以治民以事父未能矣蓋嘗尚論於古
然後知忠孝之不可得兼且悲其時之不
幸也是故王祥能屈意以事母而不能自
立於勸進之黨李密能陳情以辭位而不
能知其稱偽朝之謬趙苞能禦虜存郡不
能不悔棄親之咎溫嶠能慷慨赴難不能
不貽絕裾之譏彼其所能者於情有所見
也其所不能者於道有所不足也甚哉忠
孝之難也故有舜之孝必能為周公有周
===
===
公之忠必能為舜若持是以律天下則舜
與周公皆所不能而天下之道亦無望其
會而通之矣古云求忠臣必於孝子之門
固知忠孝非二道也求人の方忠未有可
徵則亦徵之於孝而已君子之孝非有覬
於忠而為之也本吾之心行吾之義而循
其所當為則事親不失為孝子事君不失
為忠臣雖未及舜與周公是亦舜與周公
之徒也此愚聞之經籍而又備得之于
punctuated: 可以治民，以事父未能矣。蓋嘗尚論於古，然後知忠孝之不可得兼，且悲其時之不幸也。是故王祥能屈意以事母，而不能自立於勸進之黨；李密能陳情以辭位，而不能知其稱偽朝之謬；趙苞能禦虜存郡，不能不悔棄親之咎；溫嶠能慷慨赴難，不能不貽絕裾之譏。彼其所能者，於情有所見也；其所不能者，於道有所不足也。甚哉，忠孝之難也！故有舜之孝，必能為周公；有周公之忠，必能為舜。若持是以律天下，則舜與周公皆所不能，而天下之道亦無望其會而通之矣。古云：「求忠臣，必於孝子之門。」固知忠孝非二道也。求人の方，忠未有可徵，則亦徵之於孝而已。君子之孝，非有覬於忠而為之也。本吾之心，行吾之義，而循其所當為，則事親不失為孝子，事君不失為忠臣。雖未及舜與周公，是亦舜與周公之徒也。此愚聞之經籍，而又備得之于
translation_en:
…cannot govern the people, and is not yet capable of serving his father. I have reflected upon the men of antiquity; only then did I understand that loyalty and filial piety cannot always both be fulfilled, and lament the misfortune of their times. Thus Wang Xiang could bend his will to serve his mother, yet could not stand apart from the faction urging accession to the throne. Li Mi could explain his circumstances to decline office, yet could not recognize the error of calling his former dynasty an illegitimate court. Zhao Bao could repel the invaders and preserve his commandery, yet could not escape remorse for the fault of abandoning his mother. Wen Jiao could resolutely hasten to meet a crisis, yet could not avoid the reproach of cutting off his robe’s hem to leave his mother behind. What these men could accomplish reflected some insight into human feelings; what they could not accomplish reflected a deficiency in their understanding of the Way. How difficult loyalty and filial piety are! Thus, one who possesses Shun’s filial piety must be capable of being a Duke of Zhou; one who possesses the Duke of Zhou’s loyalty must be capable of being a Shun. Yet if we hold everyone in the world to this standard, even Shun and the Duke of Zhou could not meet it, and there would be no hope of bringing the ways of the world together into a coherent whole.

An ancient saying runs: “To seek a loyal minister, one must look at the gate of a filial son.” We know, indeed, that loyalty and filial piety are not two separate Ways. As a method of seeking worthy men [?], when there is as yet no evidence by which to judge loyalty, one can only look for evidence in filial conduct. The gentleman practices filial piety without aspiring thereby to a reputation for loyalty. Taking my own heart as the foundation, carrying out what righteousness requires of me, and following what I ought to do, I will remain a filial son in serving my parents and a loyal minister in serving my ruler. Even if I fall short of Shun and the Duke of Zhou, I will still be a follower of Shun and the Duke of Zhou. This is what I, in my ignorance, have learned from the classics and other writings, and have further learned in full from …

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
聖訓者也然而未之逮也願因執事之言而自
考焉
第三問
范宗鎮
同考試官教諭黃批文武全材不可襲取作
者不為高論而當於事情蓋經世之言也錄之
考試官教授蔣批有眞材斯有全材此
用人之正義也篇中侃侃正論有味乎其言矣
考試官教授桂批官人務切實用則文
===
武自得其人書生而談世務得失較然必良士也
天之生材有二曰有全材有眞材惟其所
任使而無所不能者全材也效其所能而
不蔽其所不能者眞材也得全材則體無
不備用無不周天下無不可為之事所謂
可以為文可以為武者是矣得眞材則
取其所長舍其所短授之事而事亦治焉
所謂文能附衆武能威敵者是矣顧世
之須材甚殷而人之為材不同自天上之
punctuated:
聖訓者也。然而未之逮也，願因執事之言而自考焉。

第三問
范宗鎮

同考試官教諭黃批：「文武全材，不可襲取。作者不為高論而當於事情，蓋經世之言也，錄之。」
考試官教授蔣批：「有眞材，斯有全材，此用人之正義也。篇中侃侃正論，有味乎其言矣。」
考試官教授桂批：「官人務切實用，則文武自得其人。書生而談世務，得失較然，必良士也。」

天之生材有二，曰有全材，有眞材。惟其所任使而無所不能者，全材也；效其所能而不蔽其所不能者，眞材也。得全材，則體無不備，用無不周，天下無不可為之事，所謂可以為文、可以為武者是矣。得眞材，則取其所長，舍其所短，授之事而事亦治焉，所謂文能附衆、武能威敵者是矣。顧世之須材甚殷，而人之為材不同，自天上之
translation_en:
…the sagely instructions. Yet I have not attained this. I wish to take your words, honored sir, as grounds for examining myself.

Third Question
Fan Zongzhen

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “All-round civil and military talent cannot be acquired through imitation. The author avoids lofty theorizing and accords with the realities of affairs. These are indeed words suited to governing the world. Let this essay be included.”

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: “Only where there is genuine talent can there be all-round talent: this is the correct principle for employing men. The essay’s forthright and sound arguments give its words much to savor.”

Comment by Examiner Gui, Professor: “When appointments are made with close attention to practical usefulness, suitable men will naturally be found for both civil and military duties. A scholar who discusses worldly affairs with such clarity about successes and failures must be a worthy man.”

The talents Heaven produces are of two kinds: all-round talent and genuine talent. Those capable of everything, whatever duties they are assigned, possess all-round talent. Those who put their abilities into effect without concealing their limitations possess genuine talent. When one obtains men of all-round talent, nothing is lacking in their capacities and nothing lies beyond their practical abilities; there is no undertaking in the world that cannot be accomplished. These are what is meant by men who can serve in both civil and military affairs. When one obtains men of genuine talent, one draws upon their strengths and sets aside their weaknesses; entrusted with tasks, they too bring those tasks to good order. These are what is meant by men whose civil abilities can win the allegiance of the multitude, or whose military abilities can overawe the enemy. Yet the world’s need for talent is very pressing, while people differ in their abilities. Since the person on high…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
人操望治之心以求備於下下之人挾従
事之智以借資於上於是張不慙之言襲
不情之譽遂灑然信而任之不效明矣語
曰騏驥驊騮一日而馳千里捕䑕不如狸
狌言無全材也又曰齊紫敗素而賈什倍
言無真材也要之捕䑕之技曾無損於騏
驥驊騮以素為紫孔子惡之失其真矣故
全材為上真材次之自處乎材不材之間
而虛憍以鬭其捷非材也執事發策惟求
===
材為兢兢此以人事君之義也生也柰何
以布衣而操衡石之議干執秩者之權乎
請誦所聞而執事擇焉可也夫天以陽生
萬物以陰肅萬物而陰陽互為其根聖人
以文綏四方以武定四方而文武互為其
用記曰陰陽長短終始相巡以致天下之
和天道運而無所積者胥此矣傳曰文武
並用長久之術帝道運而無所積者胥此
矣是故陽變陰合異流而同源文事武備
punctuated:
人操望治之心，以求備於下；下之人挾従事之智，以借資於上。於是張不慙之言，襲不情之譽，遂灑然信而任之，不效明矣。語曰：「騏驥驊騮，一日而馳千里，捕䑕不如狸狌。」言無全材也。又曰：「齊紫敗素，而賈什倍。」言無真材也。要之，捕䑕之技，曾無損於騏驥驊騮；以素為紫，孔子惡之，失其真矣。故全材為上，真材次之。自處乎材不材之間，而虛憍以鬭其捷，非材也。執事發策，惟求材為兢兢，此以人事君之義也。生也柰何以布衣而操衡石之議，干執秩者之權乎？請誦所聞，而執事擇焉可也。

夫天以陽生萬物，以陰肅萬物，而陰陽互為其根。聖人以文綏四方，以武定四方，而文武互為其用。《記》曰：「陰陽長短，終始相巡，以致天下之和。」天道運而無所積者，胥此矣。《傳》曰：「文武並用，長久之術。」帝道運而無所積者，胥此矣。是故陽變陰合，異流而同源；文事武備，
translation_en:
…the ruler, intent upon attaining good government, demands complete ability from those below; those below use their practical cunning to secure support from above. Thus they proclaim shameless boasts and take on undeserved reputations, whereupon he readily trusts and employs them. That they will prove ineffectual is plain. A saying goes: “Fine steeds such as Qiji and Hualiu can gallop a thousand li in a day, yet at catching rats they are inferior to wildcats and weasels.” This means that no talent is all-encompassing. Another says: “The purple cloth of Qi spoils plain white silk, yet sells for ten times its price.” This speaks of the absence of genuine talent. Ultimately, their inability to catch rats does not detract from Qiji and Hualiu. But dyeing plain silk purple—Confucius detested this—destroys its genuineness. Thus complete talent ranks highest, and genuine talent comes next. To place oneself somewhere between ability and inability, competing for advantage through empty conceit, is no talent at all. In setting these policy questions, you, honored examiners, are most earnestly concerned with seeking talent. This accords with the principle of serving the ruler by finding worthy men. How could I, a mere student in commoner's dress, presume to weigh men's merits and encroach upon the authority of those holding office? Allow me simply to recite what I have learned, for you to select what is worthwhile.

Heaven brings the myriad things to life through yang and subjects them to restraint through yin; yin and yang are each the root of the other. The sage brings peace to the four quarters through civil means and settles them through military force; civil and military means each enable the other's operation. The Record of Rites says: “Yin and yang wax and wane, their endings and beginnings following one another, thereby bringing harmony to all under Heaven.” This is how the Way of Heaven moves without stagnation. The Commentary says: “Employing civil and military means together is the method of enduring rule.” This is how the imperial Way moves without stagnation. Thus yang transforms and yin combines: their streams differ, but their source is one; civil affairs and military preparedness…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
異用而同體聖人之於天道一也書契而
下四代之文可稽天地合而草木蕃王者
興而名世作舜之治也以禹湯之治也以
伊尹武王之治也以周公天之降材殊矣
禹以文命而格苗伊尹以一德而載亳周
公以禮樂而東征是皆材以德全而誠與
材合者也故用之禮義則順治用之於戰
勝則無敵後世頌有虞商周之治而稱大
禹伊尹周公之德不衰有由然矣乃若山
===
甫六月之師仲尼夾谷之會豈其材不類
哉而有遇有不遇論其世可知也晉之蒐
以詩書而將穀鄚之捷以文辭而使僑春
秋更霸其材亦有足多者自玆以還不少
槩見諸吕發難周勃左袒平之當是時功
無居勃右者而高帝以為可屬大事知勃
矣雖史臣謂其木彊少文惡可以是病勃
哉契丹大入寇準請帝自將卻之當是時
策無出準上者眞宗以為社稷之臣知準
punctuated: 異用而同體，聖人之於天道一也。書契而下，四代之文可稽。天地合而草木蕃，王者興而名世作。舜之治也以禹，湯之治也以伊尹，武王之治也以周公，天之降材殊矣。禹以文命而格苗，伊尹以一德而載亳，周公以禮樂而東征，是皆材以德全而誠與材合者也。故用之禮義則順治，用之於戰勝則無敵。後世頌有虞、商、周之治，而稱大禹、伊尹、周公之德不衰，有由然矣。乃若山甫六月之師，仲尼夾谷之會，豈其材不類哉？而有遇有不遇，論其世可知也。晉之蒐，以詩書而將；穀鄚之捷，以文辭而使僑。春秋更霸，其材亦有足多者。自玆以還，不少槩見。諸吕發難，周勃左袒平之。當是時，功無居勃右者，而高帝以為可屬大事，知勃矣。雖史臣謂其木彊少文，惡可以是病勃哉？契丹大入，寇準請帝自將卻之。當是時，策無出準上者，眞宗以為社稷之臣，知準
translation_en:
…differ in their uses but share one substance: the sage is at one with the Way of Heaven. From the advent of written records onward, the cultural accomplishments of the four dynastic ages can be examined. When Heaven and Earth unite, plants flourish; when a true king arises, men renowned in their age emerge. Shun governed through Yu, Tang through Yi Yin, and King Wu through the Duke of Zhou. Remarkable indeed were the talents Heaven bestowed! Yu brought the Miao to submission through his civil virtue; Yi Yin, through his single-minded virtue, established rule at Bo [?]; and the Duke of Zhou campaigned eastward with rites and music. In all these men, talent was perfected by virtue, and sincerity united with talent. Thus, employed in rites and righteousness, they brought orderly government; employed in warfare, they were invincible. There is good reason why later generations have praised the government of Youyu, Shang, and Zhou, and have never ceased extolling the virtues of the Great Yu, Yi Yin, and the Duke of Zhou.

As for Shanfu’s campaign in the sixth month [?] and Zhongni’s meeting at Jiagu, were their talents not of the same kind? Yet some found their opportunity and others did not; the reasons become clear when we consider their times. At Jin’s military review, a commander was chosen for his command of the Odes and Documents; following the victory at Gumo [?], Qiao was employed as an envoy for his literary eloquence. As successive powers held the hegemony during the Spring and Autumn period, there were also men whose talents deserved considerable praise. From that time onward, such examples were by no means rare.

When the Lü clan rose in revolt, Zhou Bo quelled it by having men bare their left arms. At that time, no one surpassed Bo in achievement. Emperor Gao had judged that he could be entrusted with great affairs: he understood Bo. Although the historian described him as blunt and unrefined, how could this be held against him? When the Khitan invaded in force, Kou Zhun asked the emperor to take personal command and repel them. At that time, no one’s strategy surpassed Zhun’s. Emperor Zhenzong regarded him as a minister who upheld the altars of soil and grain: he understood Zhun…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
矣雖張詠謂其不學無術惡可以是少準
哉善談老易人以管葛擬之殷浩文矣以
姚襄爲前驅襄遂不利於浩浩何爲者也
言事慷慨人以公輔器之房琯文矣任劉
秩爲車戰遂喪師陳濤斜琯何爲者也要
之質勝文者不處其華而事專乎報主卽
文之不足狐裘而羔袖者耳此勃之敦厚
準之峭直不能不賴之以爲安危也文勝
質者不處其實而志存乎徼功卽文之有
===
餘羊質而虎皮者耳此浩之虛名琯之高
論卒無益於勝敗也乃若孔明之書觀大
指而勍敵受其巾幗仲淹之志抱先憂而
强虜憚其甲兵玆其俶儻者邪而炎精巳
缺貝錦遂行視古昔遠矣維我
皇上中興文治武功邁周而與唐協德比年南
比露師
上方側席冢宰操吏治司馬辨官材皇皇然求
得人以稱
punctuated:
矣。雖張詠謂其不學無術，惡可以是少準哉？善談《老》《易》，人以管、葛擬之，殷浩文矣；以姚襄爲前驅，襄遂不利於浩，浩何爲者也？言事慷慨，人以公輔器之，房琯文矣；任劉秩爲車戰，遂喪師陳濤斜，琯何爲者也？要之，質勝文者，不處其華，而事專乎報主；卽文之不足，狐裘而羔袖者耳。此勃之敦厚、準之峭直，不能不賴之以爲安危也。文勝質者，不處其實，而志存乎徼功；卽文之有餘，羊質而虎皮者耳。此浩之虛名、琯之高論，卒無益於勝敗也。乃若孔明之書觀大指，而勍敵受其巾幗；仲淹之志抱先憂，而强虜憚其甲兵：玆其俶儻者邪？而炎精巳缺，貝錦遂行，視古昔遠矣。
維我皇上中興，文治武功邁周，而與唐協德。比年南比露師，上方側席，冢宰操吏治，司馬辨官材，皇皇然求得人以稱
translation_en:
…indeed. Though Zhang Yong said that Kou Zhun lacked learning and practical skill, how could this justify belittling him? Yin Hao spoke expertly on the Laozi and the Book of Changes, and people compared him to Guan Zhong and Zhuge Liang: he certainly possessed cultural refinement. Yet he made Yao Xiang his vanguard commander, and Xiang then turned against him. What, then, did Hao accomplish? Fang Guan spoke passionately on affairs, and people regarded him as fit for the highest ministerial offices: he certainly possessed cultural refinement. Yet he appointed Liu Zhi to conduct chariot warfare and consequently lost his army at Chentaoxie. What, then, did Guan accomplish?
In essence, those whose substance exceeds their refinement do not dwell on outward splendor, but devote themselves solely to repaying their sovereign. Any deficiency in refinement is merely like a fox-fur robe with lambskin sleeves. Thus, with Zhou Bo’s earnestness and Kou Zhun’s stern uprightness, one could not but rely upon them when the state’s security was at stake. Those whose refinement exceeds their substance do not ground themselves in reality, but set their ambitions on seeking distinction. Their excess of refinement is merely a sheep’s substance beneath a tiger’s skin. Thus Hao’s empty reputation and Guan’s lofty discourse ultimately did nothing to secure victory or avert defeat.
As for Kongming, he read books for their broad purport, yet his formidable enemy received the woman’s headdress he sent; Zhongyan cherished the resolve to be first to bear anxiety, and powerful foes feared his forces. Were these not men of exceptional ability? Yet the fiery essence of the Han had already waned, and slanders woven like patterned brocade prevailed. How far these circumstances fell short of antiquity!
Our Emperor has brought about a restoration: his civil governance and military achievements surpass those of Zhou, and his virtue accords with that of Tang. In recent years, armies have been deployed in the south [?]. His Majesty now sits with anxious expectation; the Minister of Personnel directs the administration of officials, and the Minister of War assesses their abilities. They earnestly seek suitable men to fulfill…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
上意於是學士談兵材官講業思得一當
聖主著功名於當時乃今島夷就禽匈奴遠遯
皆一切受成於
上而諸臣亦頗有勞矣頃者
詔求文武之材可備邊者注臣各舉所知顧其
間長短異齊華實異致則糾察之術今之
當務也愚嘗謂文武之判久矣俎豆干戈
不同其業搢紳介胄不同其官閭閻卒伍
不同其治疏附禦侮不同其職文之於武
===
也猶舟之於行陸也狐白之於當暑也尸
祝之於庖也故疆場之事各有司存策便
宜核殿最給餽餉拊士眾則有督府有撫
臣皆運籌者之有事也援枹鼓冒矢石執
訊獲醜批亢擣虛則有總戎有偏裨皆受
甲者之有事也乃今之弊有二一曰好名
吏以詩書發冢則援武事以示可用將以
騎射為業則掠儒術以示有文見者羣然
譽之某善陳某善辭及試之事寬則蝡蝹
punctuated:
上意。於是學士談兵，材官講業，思得一當聖主，著功名於當時。乃今島夷就禽，匈奴遠遯，皆一切受成於上，而諸臣亦頗有勞矣。頃者，詔求文武之材可備邊者，注臣各舉所知。顧其間長短異齊，華實異致，則糾察之術，今之當務也。
愚嘗謂文武之判久矣。俎豆干戈，不同其業；搢紳介胄，不同其官；閭閻卒伍，不同其治；疏附禦侮，不同其職。文之於武也，猶舟之於行陸也，狐白之於當暑也，尸祝之於庖也。故疆場之事，各有司存。策便宜，核殿最，給餽餉，拊士眾，則有督府，有撫臣，皆運籌者之有事也。援枹鼓，冒矢石，執訊獲醜，批亢擣虛，則有總戎，有偏裨，皆受甲者之有事也。
乃今之弊有二。一曰好名。吏以詩書發冢，則援武事以示可用；將以騎射為業，則掠儒術以示有文。見者羣然譽之，某善陳，某善辭。及試之事，寬則蝡蝹
translation_en:
…the imperial wishes. Thus scholars discuss warfare, and military officers study their profession, hoping to win the sage ruler’s approval and establish achievements and a name in their own time. Now the island barbarians have been captured, and the Xiongnu have fled far away. In all these matters, the completed plans have come from His Majesty, although his ministers too have rendered considerable service. Recently, an edict sought men of civil and military ability fit to defend the frontiers, directing the ministers [?] each to recommend those they knew. Yet their strengths and weaknesses differ in degree, and outward display and genuine substance take different forms. Methods for scrutinizing them are therefore an urgent concern today.
I have long maintained that the division between civil and military affairs is ancient. Those who handle sacrificial vessels and those who wield shields and spears pursue different occupations; those wearing officials’ sashes and those wearing armor and helmets hold different offices; governing common households differs from governing troops; drawing the distant into allegiance differs in function from resisting aggression. Employing civil expertise in military affairs is like using a boat to travel overland, wearing white fox fur in summer, or putting a ritual impersonator or invocator to work in the kitchen. Thus, in frontier affairs, each responsibility has its designated officers. Planning expedient measures, assessing the worst and best performances, supplying provisions, and caring for the troops are the responsibilities of supreme commanders and grand coordinators: all are matters for those who devise strategy. Taking up drumsticks to beat the drums, braving arrows and stones, capturing enemies for interrogation and taking prisoners, striking vital points and attacking weaknesses are the responsibilities of chief military commanders and subordinate generals: all are matters for those who don armor.
There are now two abuses. The first is a fondness for reputation. Civil officials who use the Odes and Documents to rob tombs invoke military affairs to demonstrate their usefulness; generals whose profession is mounted archery appropriate Confucian learning to demonstrate their literary cultivation. Observers join in praising them: “So-and-so is skilled in battle formations; so-and-so is skilled with words.” But when they are tested in actual affairs, in easy circumstances they merely dawdle [?]…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
急則狼顧失故步矣諺有之曰今之相者
舉肥是皆舉肥之類也此好名者之過也
一曰喜功三軍之司命在將將之譴舉在
督府與撫臣法也頃歲不然將有功則督
府撫臣爲最而上賞先之矣夫武夫効命
彼顧勦其功卽有不戒不得不分其罪失
得入其心而威福奪其氣寛則蠕望急則
狼顧失本謀矣諺有之曰利令智昏是皆
智昏之類也此喜功者之過也然則吾何
===
以糾察之亦惟核名實均刑賞而已必也
以吏事責諸吏以兵事責諸將不能吏無
取其誇大不能將無取其雍容夫然則任
職者著其誠聞風者去其僞名實核而眞
材出矣以立功屬諸將以程功屬督府及
撫臣將有功彼不得覬其賞將有罪彼不
得逭其罰夫然則利害不怵而智自明功
罪不掩而士用命刑賞均而貞材奮矣由
是而求之庶幾可得全材矣乎愚嘗聞荊
punctuated:
急則狼顧，失故步矣。諺有之曰：「今之相者舉肥。」是皆舉肥之類也。此好名者之過也。
一曰喜功。三軍之司命在將，將之譴舉在督府與撫臣，法也。頃歲不然，將有功，則督府撫臣爲最，而上賞先之矣。夫武夫効命，彼顧勦其功，卽有不戒，不得不分其罪。失得入其心，而威福奪其氣，寛則蠕望，急則狼顧，失本謀矣。諺有之曰：「利令智昏。」是皆智昏之類也。此喜功者之過也。然則吾何以糾察之？亦惟核名實、均刑賞而已。必也以吏事責諸吏，以兵事責諸將。不能吏，無取其誇大；不能將，無取其雍容。夫然則任職者著其誠，聞風者去其僞，名實核而眞材出矣。以立功屬諸將，以程功屬督府及撫臣。將有功，彼不得覬其賞；將有罪，彼不得逭其罰。夫然則利害不怵而智自明，功罪不掩而士用命，刑賞均而貞材奮矣。由是而求之，庶幾可得全材矣乎？愚嘗聞荊
translation_en:
…when matters become urgent, they glance about like wolves and lose their accustomed footing. As the proverb says, “Appraisers nowadays choose the fat.” These are all examples of choosing the fat. Such is the fault of those who crave reputation.
The other fault is eagerness to claim merit. The lives of the armies depend upon their generals; censuring and recommending generals rests with the supreme commanders and grand coordinators. This is the established rule. In recent years, however, things have been otherwise: when a general achieves merit, the supreme commander and grand coordinator receive the highest assessment and take precedence in receiving the highest rewards. The fighting men risk their lives, yet those officials appropriate their achievements. Then, if some failure of vigilance occurs, they cannot avoid sharing the blame. Thoughts of gain and loss enter their minds, while the power to punish and reward robs them of their spirit. When circumstances are easy, they hesitate and watch [?]; when urgent, they glance about like wolves, losing their original plans. As the proverb says, “Profit clouds judgment.” These are all examples of clouded judgment. Such is the fault of those eager to claim merit.
How, then, should we investigate and correct these abuses? Only by checking reputation against actual performance and making punishments and rewards equitable. Administrative duties must be demanded of civil officials, and military duties of generals. If someone cannot administer, do not value his grandiose claims; if someone cannot command, do not value his dignified bearing. In this way, those holding office will manifest their sincerity, and those who hear of this practice will abandon their pretence. Once reputation is checked against reality, genuine talent will emerge.
Entrust the achievement of military merit to the generals, and its assessment to the supreme commanders and grand coordinators. When a general has merit, those officials must not covet his reward; when a general is culpable, they must not evade their own punishment. Then, undismayed by considerations of advantage and harm, their judgment will naturally become clear. With neither achievements nor offences concealed, the soldiers will exert themselves to the utmost. When punishments and rewards are equitable, men of upright ability will bestir themselves. If we seek men by these means, might we perhaps obtain men of all-round ability? I have heard that in Jing …

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
人之攻玉者三而可以材喻全材則圭璋
也上也大禹伊尹周公是已真材則琥璜
也瑜不掩瑕者也其次也周勃寇準是已
務誇大習雍容而材焉碔也砆斯爲下矣
其殷浩房琯之流與圭璋特矣琥璜猶可
爵也藉令以碔爲圭璋其失遠矣要之求
圭璋則圭璋進顧科察之何如耳豈借材
而後足用哉若曰文武爲憲楚有人焉則
吾豈敢
===
第四問
李鳴
同考試官教諭譚 批楚士辭章性命之學
二子先鳴此篇能檃栝其業而稱述之蓋論世
而知其人矣
同考試官教諭鍾 批宋儒見道之言與騷
人感憤之辭有間子能審其所尚故披卷而樂
誦之
考試官教授蔣 批離騷太極蓋楚之大
punctuated:
人之攻玉者三，而可以材喻。全材則圭璋也，上也，大禹、伊尹、周公是已。真材則琥璜也，瑜不掩瑕者也，其次也，周勃、寇準是已。務誇大、習雍容而材焉，碔也，砆，斯爲下矣，其殷浩、房琯之流與？圭璋特矣，琥璜猶可爵也。藉令以碔爲圭璋，其失遠矣。要之，求圭璋則圭璋進，顧科察之何如耳，豈借材而後足用哉？若曰「文武爲憲，楚有人焉」，則吾豈敢？

第四問
李鳴

同考試官教諭譚批：楚士辭章、性命之學，二子先鳴。此篇能檃栝其業而稱述之，蓋論世而知其人矣。

同考試官教諭鍾批：宋儒見道之言與騷人感憤之辭有間。子能審其所尚，故披卷而樂誦之。

考試官教授蔣批：《離騷》《太極》，蓋楚之大
translation_en:
…the jade worked by the people [of Jing] falls into three categories, which may serve as analogies for talent. Complete talent is like the gui tablet and zhang blade of ceremonial jade: it is the highest category, exemplified by Yu the Great, Yi Yin, and the Duke of Zhou. Genuine talent is like the hu tiger-shaped jade and huang arc-shaped jade: its fine qualities do not conceal its flaws. This is the next category, exemplified by Zhou Bo and Kou Zhun. Those who cultivate boastfulness and practice an air of dignified ease, passing these off as talent, are like stones that merely resemble jade [?]. These constitute the lowest category—men such as Yin Hao and Fang Guan, perhaps? The gui and zhang are exceptional; those resembling the hu and huang may still be granted rank. If one were to mistake imitation jade for a gui or zhang, the error would be great indeed. In essence, if one seeks gui and zhang, gui and zhang will come forward; everything depends on how candidates are classified and scrutinized. Must talent be borrowed from elsewhere before there is enough to employ? But as for saying, “Taking Kings Wen and Wu as models, Chu has men worthy of the task,” how would I dare?

Fourth Policy Question
Li Ming

Comment by Associate Examiner Tan, Instructor: Among the scholars of Chu, these two masters first achieved distinction in literary composition and in the study of human nature and destiny, respectively. This essay distills and commends their achievements. Its author has indeed understood the men by considering the age in which they lived.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhong, Instructor: There is a difference between the words through which a Song Confucian expressed his insight into the Way and the impassioned, indignant language of the poet of the Songs of Chu. You have carefully discerned what each esteemed; thus, on opening your paper, I took pleasure in reading it aloud.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: Encountering Sorrow and the Supreme Ultimate are surely among Chu’s great…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
獻足徵者此篇能遡其源委條答無遺博雅
之士也敬服敬服
考試官教授桂批是博古而志於道者
詩以徴志則詞賦之體備焉而凡求之以
藝焉者淺矣文以明道則性命之理順焉
而凡泥之以言焉者惑矣蓋苟可寓吾忠
君之志雖其詩之工否弗論可也而況其
工於詩者乎苟可昭吾明道之實雖其文
之粹否弗論可也而況其粹於言者乎迹
===
窮而志彌章故不詭於其俗位卑而道益
邃故不淆於其真是以作者自得其師而
述者競守其轍鑒之不精則附麗爲正而
纖巧爲妍索之未融則虛寂爲宗而蕪蔓
爲主茲吾有取於屈平之騷茂叔之圖皆
可謂千載一人而欲以楚材例論之無亦
觀諸生所趨向而嘗試之歟蓋平之有騷
也由風雅而載變者蘇軾讀之自謂得體
此楚詩之昉也營道著圖秘不示人朱震
punctuated:
獻足徵者，此篇能遡其源委，條答無遺，博雅之士也。敬服，敬服！

考試官教授桂批：是博古而志於道者。

詩以徴志，則詞賦之體備焉，而凡求之以藝焉者淺矣。文以明道，則性命之理順焉，而凡泥之以言焉者惑矣。蓋苟可寓吾忠君之志，雖其詩之工否弗論可也，而況其工於詩者乎？苟可昭吾明道之實，雖其文之粹否弗論可也，而況其粹於言者乎？迹窮而志彌章，故不詭於其俗；位卑而道益邃，故不淆於其真。是以作者自得其師，而述者競守其轍。鑒之不精，則附麗爲正，而纖巧爲妍；索之未融，則虛寂爲宗，而蕪蔓爲主。茲吾有取於屈平之騷、茂叔之圖，皆可謂千載一人，而欲以楚材例論之，無亦觀諸生所趨向而嘗試之歟？蓋平之有騷也，由風雅而載變者，蘇軾讀之，自謂得體，此楚詩之昉也。營道著圖，秘不示人，朱震
translation_en:
…worthies whose achievements are amply attested. This essay traces their origins and development, answering point by point without omission. Its author is a man of broad learning and refined understanding. My respects, my respects!

Examiner Gui, Instructor, comments: This is someone versed in antiquity whose aspirations are set upon the Way.

Poetry expresses aspirations, and thus the forms of verse and rhapsody find their full realization in it; anyone who seeks in it only literary technique is shallow. Prose elucidates the Way, and thus the principles of human nature and destiny find orderly expression in it; anyone who remains confined to its words is deluded. If my aspiration to be loyal to my ruler can be lodged in a poem, it is permissible to leave aside whether the poem is accomplished or not. How much more so when it is accomplished! If my actual understanding of the Way can be made manifest, it is permissible to leave aside whether the prose is pure or not. How much more so when its language is pure!

Though his worldly course was thwarted, his aspirations became ever more manifest; hence he did not bend to the customs of his age. Though his position was lowly, his understanding of the Way grew ever more profound; hence he did not compromise its truth. Thus the originators each found their own teacher, while those who transmitted their work vied to follow their tracks. When discernment lacks precision, ornamental embellishment is taken for correctness and minute ingenuity for beauty. When inquiry has not reached an integrated understanding, emptiness and stillness are taken as the guiding doctrine, and tangled prolixity becomes the principal pursuit.

Here I find much to esteem in Qu Ping’s Encountering Sorrow and Maoshu’s Diagram. Each man may be called one who appears but once in a thousand years. Yet you wish to discuss them under the general category of talent from Chu: might this be an attempt to observe the inclinations of us students and put us to the test? For Qu Ping’s Encountering Sorrow carried forward and transformed the Airs and Elegantiae. On reading it, Su Shi said that he had grasped its essential form. This was the beginning of Chu poetry. The master of Yingdao composed the Diagram and kept it secret, showing it to no one. Zhu Zhen…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
撰進易解謂傳自种穆非由人授此楚易
之符也彼謂辭賦之祖是槩之以藝而不
識風人之旨謂得孔孟之傳固歸之於理
云爾而性與天道之妙正未易聞也今觀
騷經所著以離愁幽思之懷而叫號穹壤
之間以憤激沉鬱之氣而超脫塵埃之表
述九歌類於舛序遠遊幾於放命卜居近
於太詭跡崑崙涉於非經太一之篇繼以
湘君則傷於靡惜誦之章繼以懷沙則疑
===
於矯平之赴湘流也揚雄誚以湛身而斑
固議為揚巳似無當於溫柔敦厚之意者
然三百篇之後賴有此耳舍騷而曰可與
論詩則終無詩矣太極圖所述明朕兆之
微以極天地性命之變剖幽微之象以推
禮樂刑政之施行五殊而遺相制推二本
而遺相間言中正則違利貞語動靜則涉
生滅初舉太極皆踵彖象之緒餘復加無
極如襲道德之宗旨周子之立圖也張敬
punctuated:
撰進《易解》，謂傳自种穆，非由人授，此楚易之符也。彼謂辭賦之祖，是槩之以藝，而不識風人之旨；謂得孔孟之傳，固歸之於理云爾，而性與天道之妙，正未易聞也。今觀《騷經》所著，以離愁幽思之懷，而叫號穹壤之間；以憤激沉鬱之氣，而超脫塵埃之表。述《九歌》，類於舛序；《遠遊》，幾於放命；《卜居》，近於太詭；跡崑崙，涉於非經。《太一》之篇繼以《湘君》，則傷於靡；《惜誦》之章繼以《懷沙》，則疑於矯。平之赴湘流也，揚雄誚以湛身，而斑固議為揚巳，似無當於溫柔敦厚之意者。然三百篇之後，賴有此耳。舍《騷》而曰可與論詩，則終無詩矣。
《太極圖》所述，明朕兆之微，以極天地性命之變；剖幽微之象，以推禮樂刑政之施。行五殊而遺相制，推二本而遺相間；言中正則違利貞，語動靜則涉生滅。初舉太極，皆踵彖象之緒餘；復加無極，如襲《道德》之宗旨。周子之立圖也，張敬
translation_en:
…compiled and submitted his Explanation of the Changes, saying that it had been transmitted from Zhong and Mu, rather than received through personal instruction [?]. This is the identifying token of Chu’s tradition of the Changes. To call him the progenitor of rhapsodies is to judge him merely by literary artistry, without recognizing the intent of a poet of the Airs. To say that the other received the transmission of Confucius and Mencius certainly assigns him to the realm of principle; yet the subtleties of human nature and the Way of Heaven are by no means easily apprehended.
Now consider what is set forth in the Classic of Encountering Sorrow: with a heart full of the sorrow of separation and secluded thoughts, he cries out between Heaven and Earth; with a spirit of indignation and brooding anguish, he rises above the dust of the world. His composition of the Nine Songs seems to confuse the proper order; Far Roaming verges on defying Heaven’s command; Divination on Where to Dwell approaches excessive eccentricity; and his journeys to Kunlun stray beyond canonical teachings. Following the poem on the Great One with the Lord of the Xiang tends toward extravagance; following Lament for My Recitation with Embracing Sand invites suspicion of affectation. When Qu Ping threw himself into the Xiang River, Yang Xiong reproached him for drowning himself, while Ban Gu criticized him for self-aggrandizement. These things seem at odds with the ideal of gentleness and kindness, sincerity and generosity. Yet after the three hundred poems, it is this work alone on which we can rely. If one discards Encountering Sorrow and claims to be qualified to discuss poetry, one will ultimately have no understanding of poetry.
What the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate sets forth illuminates the faintest incipient signs, thereby fathoming the transformations of Heaven and Earth, human nature and destiny. It analyzes hidden and subtle configurations, thereby extending its account to the implementation of ritual, music, punishments, and government. It distinguishes the five phases but omits their mutual restraint; it traces things to two roots but omits their interpenetration. Its discussion of centrality and correctness runs counter to benefit and constancy; its account of activity and stillness verges on arising and extinction. In first invoking the Supreme Ultimate, it merely follows the lingering threads of the Commentaries on the Judgments and Images; in further adding the Non-Ultimate, it seems to adopt the central teaching of the Classic of the Way and Virtue. As for Master Zhou’s establishment of the diagram, Zhang Jing…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
夫初疑其迂而陸九淵力排其非似無當
於潔靜精微之妙者然千百年之傳僅有
此耳舎是而曰我能學易則終無易矣夫
詩之爲教也發乎性情止乎禮義以端淫
佚之思以暢和平之感故曰可以興可以
觀可以羣可以怨此詩之本原也彼無得
於騷者直以宗國之屬未免出於抗激而
不知鴟鴞之誦夫子傳於東周載馳之篇
室女遣於旣嫁彼固懷君之切而不忍忘
===
爾至於上稱帝嚳下道齊桓中述湯武明
道德之廣崇治亂之條貫其于時事有遺
憾焉聖人所不廢也史遷曰國風好色而
不淫小雅怨誹而不亂離騷兼之矣雖謂
詩未亡可也若易之爲道也行乎陰陽通
乎鬼神以昭變化之象以決悔吝之途故
曰其旨遠其辭文其言曲而中其事肆而
隱此易之要領也彼無見於圖者皆以爲
無極之語不當涉於虛寂而不知一元流
punctuated:
夫初疑其迂，而陸九淵力排其非，似無當於潔靜精微之妙者。然千百年之傳，僅有此耳。舎是而曰我能學易，則終無易矣。夫詩之爲教也，發乎性情，止乎禮義，以端淫佚之思，以暢和平之感，故曰：「可以興，可以觀，可以羣，可以怨。」此詩之本原也。彼無得於騷者，直以宗國之屬未免出於抗激，而不知《鴟鴞》之誦，夫子傳於東周；《載馳》之篇，室女遣於旣嫁。彼固懷君之切，而不忍忘爾。至於上稱帝嚳，下道齊桓，中述湯武，明道德之廣崇、治亂之條貫，其于時事有遺憾焉，聖人所不廢也。史遷曰：「國風好色而不淫，小雅怨誹而不亂，離騷兼之矣。」雖謂詩未亡，可也。

若易之爲道也，行乎陰陽，通乎鬼神，以昭變化之象，以決悔吝之途，故曰：「其旨遠，其辭文，其言曲而中，其事肆而隱。」此易之要領也。彼無見於圖者，皆以爲無極之語不當涉於虛寂，而不知一元流
translation_en:
…[Zhang Jing]fu initially suspected it of being far-fetched, while Lu Jiuyuan vigorously attacked its errors: it seemed not to accord with the subtle excellence of purity, stillness, precision, and profundity. Yet in the transmission of a thousand years and more, this alone remains. To discard it and say, “I can study the Changes,” would ultimately leave no Changes at all. The teaching of the Odes issues from human nature and feelings and stays within ritual propriety and righteousness, correcting licentious thoughts and giving free expression to harmonious and peaceful feelings. Hence it is said: “They can stimulate, enable observation, bring people together, and express grievances.” These are the fundamental sources of the Odes. Those who gain nothing from Encountering Sorrow simply consider its attachment to the ancestral state inevitably defiant and impassioned. They fail to recognize that Confucius transmitted the recitation of “The Owl” in the Eastern Zhou, and that a woman sent forth the poem “Galloping” after her marriage [?]. The poet’s longing for his lord was simply so intense that he could not bear to forget him. As for its references reaching back to Di Ku and down to Duke Huan of Qi, with Tang and Wu recounted in between, it illuminates the breadth and loftiness of the Way and virtue, and the connected principles of order and disorder. Its lingering regrets concerning the affairs of its time are something the sage would not reject. Sima Qian said: “The Airs of the States delight in beauty without licentiousness; the Lesser Odes express resentment and criticism without disorder. Encountering Sorrow combines both.” One may therefore even say that the Odes have not perished.

As for the Way of the Changes, it operates through yin and yang and communicates with ghosts and spirits, revealing the images of transformation and determining the courses that lead to remorse and regret. Hence it is said: “Its purport is far-reaching; its language is patterned; its words are indirect yet apt; its matters are openly set forth yet conceal deeper meanings.” These are the essentials of the Changes. Those who find no insight in the Diagram all consider that the expression “the Limitless” ought not to stray into emptiness and quiescence. They fail to understand that the unitary primal force flows…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
行即無聲無臭之理五氣順布乃資始資
生之端彼固見道之妙而不容秘爾至於
首畫乾坤次分陰陽終具善惡究性命之
淵微動靜之機緘其于聖德無餘蘊焉古
人所未發也胡宏曰書約而道大文質而
義精圖盡之矣雖謂易猶在可也蓋原忠
不售而辭卒垂于世其徒宋玉景差閔原
之志而作大招與九辨諸賦亦得騷之旨
而揚其波瀾者也其後百年而賈誼遠謫
===
長沙復為賦以悼之微數子則騷又絕響
矣茂叔位不顯而道遂昭于時其徒有程
顥兄弟受茂叔之業而作易傳及定性諸
篇寔得圖之旨而發其蘊奧者也其後再
傳而朱熹張栻講業嶽麓復因是圖而推
廣之微二子則圖將失傳矣君子非文之
難難于寓忠非言之難難于明道使皆如
其所志則平能竟抱江魚之怨茂叔能終
遂庭草之樂哉平也內蒙子蘭之毀外被
punctuated:
行，即無聲無臭之理；五氣順布，乃資始資生之端。彼固見道之妙而不容秘爾。至於首畫乾坤，次分陰陽，終具善惡，究性命之淵微、動靜之機緘，其于聖德無餘蘊焉，古人所未發也。胡宏曰：「書約而道大，文質而義精。」圖盡之矣，雖謂易猶在可也。
蓋原忠不售，而辭卒垂于世。其徒宋玉、景差閔原之志，而作大招與九辨諸賦，亦得騷之旨而揚其波瀾者也。其後百年，而賈誼遠謫長沙，復為賦以悼之。微數子，則騷又絕響矣。茂叔位不顯，而道遂昭于時。其徒有程顥兄弟，受茂叔之業，而作易傳及定性諸篇，寔得圖之旨而發其蘊奧者也。其後再傳，而朱熹、張栻講業嶽麓，復因是圖而推廣之。微二子，則圖將失傳矣。
君子非文之難，難于寓忠；非言之難，難于明道。使皆如其所志，則平能竟抱江魚之怨，茂叔能終遂庭草之樂哉？平也，內蒙子蘭之毀，外被
translation_en:
…in its circulation is precisely the principle that has neither sound nor smell; the orderly distribution of the five vital energies is the source from which things receive their beginnings and their life. He indeed perceived the subtlety of the Way and could not keep it secret. As for first depicting Qian and Kun, next distinguishing yin and yang, and finally encompassing good and evil, it probes the profound subtleties of human nature and destiny and the hidden workings of movement and stillness. It leaves none of the profundities of sagely virtue unrevealed, disclosing what the ancients had not brought forth. Hu Hong said: “The writing is concise, yet the Way it conveys is vast; its language is plain, yet its meaning is refined.” The Diagram encompasses all this. One may even say that the Book of Changes still lives within it.
Qu Yuan’s loyalty found no acceptance, yet his writings were ultimately handed down to the world. His followers Song Yu and Jing Cu sympathized with his aspirations and composed such rhapsodies as the Great Summons and the Nine Avowals. They too grasped the purport of Encountering Sorrow (Li sao) and carried forward its surging currents. A hundred years later, Jia Yi was banished far away to Changsha and again composed a rhapsody to mourn him. Without these few men, Encountering Sorrow would have ceased to find an answering voice. Maoshu’s official position was undistinguished, yet his Way became manifest in his age. Among his disciples were Cheng Hao and his brother, who received Maoshu’s teaching and composed the Commentary on the Book of Changes and such writings as Settling the Nature. They truly grasped the purport of the Diagram and revealed its profound meanings. After two further generations of transmission, Zhu Xi and Zhang Shi taught and studied at Yuelu, again using this Diagram as the basis for further elaboration. Without these two men, the Diagram’s transmission would have been lost.
For the gentleman, the difficulty lies not in composing literature but in embodying loyalty within it; not in speaking but in illuminating the Way. Had each attained his aspirations, could Ping have ended with the grievance of becoming food for the river’s fish, or Maoshu have ultimately fulfilled his delight in the grass of his courtyard? Ping—that is, Qu Yuan—suffered Zilan’s disparagement within the court, and outside it was subjected to…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
靳尚之謗澤畔行吟乃與漁父伍爾假令
兩君見庸謀行職脩光復舊物固其材也
不然入而圖議政事決定國疑出而鑒察
羣下應對諸侯亦庶幾一國之士哉敦頤
始寄分寧之簿晚司監稅之額弄丸餘暇
卒老濂溪間耳設如韓富同列建立師道
志伊學顏固其餘也不然恥於媚人而澤
及冤抑銳於尚友而惠及惸獨將不得為
一代之英哉誼以洛陽年少見用漢室平
===
之流也絳灌之訐且以紛更阻之其去憲
令之讒幾何雖文帝之明其聰惑矣然其
改正朔易服色定官制蚤諭儲教盡行治
安之策亦周官之遺而文學之望也而世
獨以其志廣用疏目為迂闊嗚呼當時將
相功臣之列誰為出誼之右者哉濂溪既
沒洛蜀諸黨自相攻擊而元豐憸壬之輩
潛乘厥釁至於涪陵見謫黨禁日嚴侂胄
肆志開禧之時力錮偽學而君子遂屏迹
punctuated:
靳尚之謗，澤畔行吟，乃與漁父伍爾。假令兩君見庸，謀行職脩，光復舊物，固其材也。不然，入而圖議政事，決定國疑；出而鑒察羣下，應對諸侯，亦庶幾一國之士哉！
敦頤始寄分寧之簿，晚司監稅之額，弄丸餘暇，卒老濂溪間耳。設如韓富同列，建立師道，志伊學顏，固其餘也。不然，恥於媚人而澤及冤抑，銳於尚友而惠及惸獨，將不得為一代之英哉！
誼以洛陽年少見用漢室，平之流也。絳灌之訐，且以紛更阻之，其去憲令之讒幾何？雖文帝之明，其聰惑矣。然其改正朔，易服色，定官制，蚤諭儲教，盡行治安之策，亦周官之遺而文學之望也。而世獨以其志廣用疏，目為迂闊。嗚呼！當時將相功臣之列，誰為出誼之右者哉？
濂溪既沒，洛蜀諸黨自相攻擊，而元豐憸壬之輩潛乘厥釁。至於涪陵見謫，黨禁日嚴，侂胄肆志，開禧之時力錮偽學，而君子遂屏迹
translation_en:
…the slanders of Jin Shang. Chanting as he walked beside the marsh, he came to keep company only with a fisherman. Had the two rulers employed him, his plans been implemented, and his duties duly performed, restoring the former patrimony would certainly have been within his abilities. Failing that, had he deliberated on affairs of government and resolved the state's uncertainties at court, and inspected subordinate officials and answered the feudal lords abroad, would he not still have approached the standing of an outstanding man of his state?
Dunyi initially held the post of Registrar in Fenning and later supervised tax receipts. In the leisure left by handling affairs as deftly as juggling balls, he merely grew old beside Lianxi. Had he ranked alongside Han Qi and Fu Bi, establishing the Way of the teacher, aspiring to Yi Yin, and emulating Yan Hui would surely have been well within his powers. Failing that, ashamed to flatter others, he might have extended his beneficence to those wronged and oppressed; eager to take worthy men of the past as his friends, he might have brought kindness to the bereft and solitary. Could he not then have become an outstanding figure of his age?
Jia Yi, employed by the Han court as a young man from Luoyang, was of the same kind as Qu Ping. The attacks of Jiang and Guan obstructed him with accusations of disruptive innovation: how far removed were these from the slanders concerning the drafting of ordinances? Even Emperor Wen, for all his discernment, was misled in what he heard. Yet Jia Yi's proposals to change the calendrical arrangements, alter the colors of ceremonial dress, establish the official system, give early instruction concerning the heir's education, and implement all his policies for good government and peace carried on the legacy of the Offices of Zhou and embodied the aspirations of learned men. The world, however, saw only that his ambitions were broad and his employment limited, and judged him impractical. Alas! Among the generals, chief ministers, and meritorious officials of that time, who surpassed Jia Yi?
After Lianxi died, the Luo and Shu factions attacked one another, while the treacherous men of the Yuanfeng era secretly exploited their divisions. Matters reached the point of banishment to Fuling, and the prohibitions against factions grew daily more severe. Han Tuozhou gave free rein to his ambitions; during the Kaixi era he vigorously proscribed the so-called False Learning, and gentlemen consequently withdrew from public view…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
矣向使汝愚不竄同道為朋凡正心誠意
之學展盡底蘊豈無尊主庇民之功哉聖
遠言湮之餘而道不上行固非人力所能
為也嘗取二子而參較之懷瑾握瑜特無
鳳凰覽輝之見彈冠振衣猶表日月爭光
之誠蓋原得之為騷者也子虛大人諸作
更當奴僕命之矣光風霽月吟弄同於浴
沂玉色金聲和毅昭於傾府蓋茂叔得之
以為圖者也王通韓愈諸人奚啻伯仲見
===
之哉廼知東南之美不獨品金璣組之貢
而已然原之所志志事功也茂叔之志志
道德也無原之忠愛而徒襲其音響故浸
淫於漢魏愈變而愈下有圖之淵源而漸
窮其指歸故發揮乎孔孟益久而益明以
茂叔之賢雖安石猶知慕之願與天下效
之介潔如原雖自取芳譽終無益矣君子
予之而不盡予也學茂叔而未逮猶不失
為令名之士所謂循途而趨者也徒效原
punctuated: 矣。向使汝愚不竄，同道為朋，凡正心誠意之學展盡底蘊，豈無尊主庇民之功哉？聖遠言湮之餘，而道不上行，固非人力所能為也。嘗取二子而參較之：懷瑾握瑜，特無鳳凰覽輝之見；彈冠振衣，猶表日月爭光之誠，蓋原得之為騷者也。子虛、大人諸作，更當奴僕命之矣。光風霽月，吟弄同於浴沂；玉色金聲，和毅昭於傾府，蓋茂叔得之以為圖者也。王通、韓愈諸人，奚啻伯仲見之哉？廼知東南之美，不獨品金璣組之貢而已。然原之所志，志事功也；茂叔之志，志道德也。無原之忠愛而徒襲其音響，故浸淫於漢魏，愈變而愈下；有圖之淵源而漸窮其指歸，故發揮乎孔孟，益久而益明。以茂叔之賢，雖安石猶知慕之，願與天下效之。介潔如原，雖自取芳譽，終無益矣。君子予之而不盡予也。學茂叔而未逮，猶不失為令名之士，所謂循途而趨者也。徒效原
translation_en:
…thus it was. Had Zhao Ruyu not been banished, and had those sharing the same Way formed a fellowship and fully unfolded the learning of rectifying the mind and making intentions sincere, could they not have accomplished something in honoring the ruler and protecting the people? Yet when the sages were long gone and their words obscured, the failure of the Way to prevail among those above was indeed beyond human power to remedy.

I have compared these two men. Cherishing and holding fine jade, yet lacking the phoenix’s sight of glorious radiance; dusting off his cap and shaking out his robes, still displaying a sincerity that vied in brilliance with the sun and moon: this was what Qu Yuan grasped and expressed in Encountering Sorrow. Works such as Rhapsody on Sir Vacuous and Rhapsody on the Great Man should accordingly be assigned the standing of his servants. Like a clear breeze and the moon after rain, his singing and enjoyment resembled that of bathing in the Yi River; with a jade-like countenance and a voice resonant as metal, his gentleness and firmness shone forth as he opened his heart. This was what Zhou Maoshu grasped and embodied in his Diagram. How could men such as Wang Tong and Han Yu be regarded simply as his peers? Thus we know that the excellence of the southeast consists of more than its tribute of fine metals, pearls, and silk cords.

Yet Qu Yuan’s aspiration was directed toward practical achievement, while Maoshu’s was directed toward the Way and virtue. Those who lacked Qu Yuan’s loyal devotion but merely imitated the sounds of his poetry consequently became immersed in the styles of Han and Wei, declining with each successive transformation. Those who possessed the intellectual lineage of the Diagram and gradually fathomed its purport consequently elucidated the teachings of Confucius and Mencius, making them ever clearer with time. Such was Maoshu’s worth that even Wang Anshi knew to admire him and wished to emulate him together with all the world. To be as upright and pure as Qu Yuan might win one a fine reputation, but ultimately brought no benefit. The gentleman approves of him, but not without reservation. Even those who study Maoshu without reaching his level can still be men of good reputation: these are what are called people who advance along the proper path. Merely to imitate Qu Yuan…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之詞賦而靡麗詭異之習羣然相高所謂
雕蟲之技失故轍矣執事之所問者皆楚
賢也非愚所敢議也偶以所聞見從爲之
辭將就有道而正焉執事以爲何如
第五問
陳謨
同考試官敎諭朱批楚人論楚事亹亹可
聽有司決策行之亦楚之便宜也錄之以俟能者
考試官敎授蔣批議論剴切區畫詳明
===
用世之才可以槩見
考試官敎授桂批事核而謀臧非彌文
也佳士佳士
執事憑軾入楚目攝楚事將畫策而紀綱
之纚纚乎慘怛忠利之言敢不操牘以對
愚惟王者之分土建官以任民治豈徒取
充位而已哉必也爲之興利爲之捍患爲
之長顧卻慮以圖可久爲之先事豫防以
銷未萌如是則官不失職民不失和而境
punctuated:
之詞賦，而靡麗詭異之習羣然相高，所謂雕蟲之技，失故轍矣。執事之所問者，皆楚賢也，非愚所敢議也。偶以所聞見，從爲之辭，將就有道而正焉。執事以爲何如？
第五問
陳謨
同考試官敎諭朱批：楚人論楚事，亹亹可聽。有司決策行之，亦楚之便宜也。錄之以俟能者。
考試官敎授蔣批：議論剴切，區畫詳明，用世之才可以槩見。
考試官敎授桂批：事核而謀臧，非彌文也。佳士！佳士！
執事憑軾入楚，目攝楚事，將畫策而紀綱之。纚纚乎慘怛忠利之言，敢不操牘以對？愚惟王者之分土建官，以任民治，豈徒取充位而已哉？必也爲之興利，爲之捍患，爲之長顧卻慮以圖可久，爲之先事豫防以銷未萌。如是，則官不失職，民不失和，而境
translation_en:
…his lyric compositions and rhapsodies, vying with one another in ornate extravagance and outlandish conceits: these are what are called the petty arts of carving insects; they have strayed from the original track. Those about whom you ask are all worthies of Chu, whom I would not presume to judge. Drawing incidentally upon what I have heard and seen, I have accordingly composed these remarks, intending to submit them to one who possesses the Way for correction. What do you think of them?
Fifth Question
Chen Mo
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: A man of Chu discussing the affairs of Chu—his sustained exposition is well worth hearing. If the responsible officials resolve upon these policies and implement them, they will serve Chu’s practical needs. I record this essay to await someone capable of carrying them out.
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: The discussion is incisive and pertinent, and the planning detailed and clear. One can discern here his ability to serve the world.
Comment by Examiner Gui, Professor: His account of affairs is grounded in fact, and his proposals are sound; this is no mere accumulation of literary ornament. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!
You entered Chu leaning upon your carriage rail and surveyed its affairs with your own eyes, intending to devise policies and bring them into order. Faced with your flowing words of heartfelt concern, loyalty, and solicitude for the people’s welfare, how could I dare not take up my writing tablet and reply? I humbly consider that when a true king divides the territory and establishes offices, entrusting them with governing the people, surely he does not merely seek men to fill positions. They must promote benefits for the people and ward off calamities; they must look far ahead and consider possible reverses so as to plan for what can endure; and they must take precautions before events occur, eliminating troubles before they sprout. In this way, officials will not neglect their duties, the people will not lose their harmony, and the territory…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
内治矣然而興利務滋除害務本執拘攣
之議者不足以觀昭曠之原用因循之務
者不足以求明作之效故必有非常之事
而後有非常之功得人焉爾楚地數千里
距秦蜀控九江其間疏而爲三江瀦而爲
七澤蓋水國也昔在禹貢雲土夢作乂雲
夢於是而始穰依古以來溝洫非不力也
乃今田野多萑苻而編氓失其恒產則地
利薄矣昔在春秋齊桓盟江黃江黃於是
===
而始勁依古以來備禦非不周也乃今草
澤多淵藪而細民輕於爲邪則方慝興矣
周制稻人以瀦蓄水以防止水以澮瀉水
稼下地者賴之足民之道也今則圩有長
縣有簿郡有倅監司從而程督之制視周
備矣漢法郡國以車騎備平原以材官備
山阻以樓船備水泉戒不虞者賴之弭盜
之術也今則疆有候吏郡有偵夫衞有艘
卒監司從而分蒞之法視漢良矣然而利
punctuated:
内治矣。然而興利務滋，除害務本。執拘攣之議者，不足以觀昭曠之原；用因循之務者，不足以求明作之效。故必有非常之事，而後有非常之功，得人焉爾。楚地數千里，距秦蜀，控九江，其間疏而爲三江，瀦而爲七澤，蓋水國也。昔在《禹貢》，雲土夢作乂，雲夢於是而始穰。依古以來，溝洫非不力也。乃今田野多萑苻，而編氓失其恒產，則地利薄矣。昔在《春秋》，齊桓盟江黃，江黃於是而始勁。依古以來，備禦非不周也。乃今草澤多淵藪，而細民輕於爲邪，則方慝興矣。
周制，稻人以瀦蓄水，以防止水，以澮瀉水，稼下地者賴之，足民之道也。今則圩有長，縣有簿，郡有倅，監司從而程督之，制視周備矣。漢法，郡國以車騎備平原，以材官備山阻，以樓船備水泉，戒不虞者賴之，弭盜之術也。今則疆有候吏，郡有偵夫，衞有艘卒，監司從而分蒞之，法視漢良矣。然而利
translation_en:
…the territory would be well governed. Yet promoting benefits requires making them abundant, and removing harms requires addressing their roots. Those who cling to cramped proposals cannot perceive broad and illuminating principles; those who merely follow established routines cannot achieve the results of enlightened action. Thus extraordinary undertakings must precede extraordinary achievements: it is simply a matter of finding the right people. The land of Chu extends several thousand li, abutting Qin and Shu and commanding the Nine Rivers. Its waters flow through channels as the Three Rivers and collect in basins as the Seven Marshes: it is indeed a land of waters. Long ago, the Tribute of Yu recorded that the soil of Yun and Meng was brought under cultivation; only then did Yunmeng begin to yield abundantly. Since antiquity [?], efforts to maintain irrigation channels have certainly not been lacking. Yet now fields are thick with reeds and rushes, and registered commoners have lost their permanent means of livelihood: the land’s benefits have thus diminished. Long ago, in the Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Huan of Qi entered into a covenant with Jiang and Huang; only then did Jiang and Huang begin to grow strong. Since antiquity [?], defensive preparations have certainly not lacked thoroughness. Yet now the marshlands abound in lurking places, and ordinary people readily turn to wrongdoing: local evils have thus arisen.
Under Zhou institutions, the rice-field officers used reservoirs to store water, embankments to hold it back, and drainage channels to discharge it. Those who cultivated low-lying land depended on these measures: this was a means of ensuring the people’s sufficiency. Today, each polder has a headman, each county a Registrar, and each prefecture an Assistant Prefect, while the surveillance authorities oversee their work and enforce its standards. These institutions are more comprehensive than those of Zhou. Under Han regulations, the commanderies and kingdoms used chariots and cavalry to defend the plains, trained infantry to defend rugged mountain terrain, and towered warships to defend the waterways. Those charged with guarding against unforeseen dangers depended on these measures: this was a method of suppressing banditry. Today, the borderlands have lookout officers, the prefectures have scouts, and the guards have boat troops; the surveillance authorities exercise jurisdiction over their respective areas. These regulations are better than those of Han. And yet the benefits…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之未滋患之未弭誰任其咎哉古之善興
利者若孫叔敖在楚史起在魏鄭國在秦
李冰在蜀皆以治水聞焉芍陂之惠漳水
之勞鄭渠之饒陸海之沃民到于今稱之
矣要之古以導水爲利者也今以防水爲
利者也其利殊也古之善捍患者若龔遂
之於渤海賈琮之於交趾張敞之於冀州
李崇之於兗州皆以治盜顯焉佩犢之諭
賈父之歌入境之威名懸鼓之號令民到
===
===
于今稱之矣要之古以部内爲患者也今
以境外爲患者也其患異也以水利言之
湘水不爲菑勿治可也江水菑而不害猶
可治也松滋公安而下有司業已隄之假
令石首奏功可息肩矣漢水决沙洋其害
潛沔尤甚比年興工塞决口功成而水復
齧之則沙洋之績不可不爲之終慮也愚
嘗聞宋孟珙入荆郢憂江漢爲患開三海
八櫃分殺其流楚饗其利者數世
punctuated:
之未滋，患之未弭，誰任其咎哉？古之善興利者，若孫叔敖在楚、史起在魏、鄭國在秦、李冰在蜀，皆以治水聞焉。芍陂之惠、漳水之勞、鄭渠之饒、陸海之沃，民到于今稱之矣。要之，古以導水爲利者也，今以防水爲利者也，其利殊也。古之善捍患者，若龔遂之於渤海、賈琮之於交趾、張敞之於冀州、李崇之於兗州，皆以治盜顯焉。佩犢之諭、賈父之歌、入境之威名、懸鼓之號令，民到于今稱之矣。要之，古以部内爲患者也，今以境外爲患者也，其患異也。

以水利言之，湘水不爲菑，勿治可也；江水菑而不害，猶可治也。松滋、公安而下，有司業已隄之，假令石首奏功，可息肩矣。漢水决沙洋，其害潛沔尤甚，比年興工塞决口，功成而水復齧之，則沙洋之績不可不爲之終慮也。愚嘗聞宋孟珙入荆郢，憂江漢爲患，開三海八櫃，分殺其流，楚饗其利者數世。
translation_en:
…have not increased, and troubles have not been quelled: who bears the blame? Among those of antiquity skilled at promoting benefits, Sunshu Ao in Chu, Shi Qi in Wei, Zheng Guo in Qin, and Li Bing in Shu were all renowned for controlling water. The benefits of the Shaopi reservoir, the labors on the Zhang River, the abundance supplied by the Zheng Canal, and the fertility of the “inland sea”—the people praise these to this day. In essence, the ancients secured benefits by channeling water, whereas today we secure them by holding water back. The benefits sought are different. Among those of antiquity skilled at warding off troubles, Gong Sui in Bohai, Jia Cong in Jiaozhi, Zhang Chang in Jizhou, and Li Chong in Yanzhou were all distinguished for suppressing banditry. The exhortation to exchange swords for calves, the song praising “Father Jia,” the intimidating reputation upon entering the territory, and the orders to hang up warning drums—the people praise these to this day. In essence, the ancients faced troubles within their jurisdictions, whereas today we face troubles from beyond our borders. The troubles are different.

As for water management, the Xiang River causes no disasters, so it may be left alone; the Yangzi causes disasters but does no harm [?], and it can still be brought under control. From Songzi and Gong’an downstream, the responsible officials have already built dikes. If the works at Shishou succeed, they can lay down their burden. The Han River breached its banks at Shayang, causing particularly severe damage in Qianjiang and Mianyang. In recent years, works were undertaken to close the breach, but once completed, the water again ate away at them. Thus, the undertaking at Shayang requires consideration of how to bring it to lasting completion. I have heard that when Meng Gong of the Song entered Jingzhou and Yingzhou, he feared the danger posed by the Yangzi and Han rivers and opened the Three Lakes and Eight Reservoirs, dividing and reducing their flow. Chu enjoyed the benefits for several generations.

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
國初遺跡具在監稅者治之其後水道湮滅
而利擅專門矣昔賈讓陳治河三策後世
以爲口實竊謂今之治水者其策有二脩
孟珙遺政濬支河開穴口塞沙洋此數世
之計也是謂上策頃之築沙洋者監司檄
縣吏縣吏檄圩長圩長發人徒因朽壤積
塗泥將以逭簿責耳卽千夫荷畚惡能底
績哉誠使監司爲植郡縣巡功不奪流言
不愛重費相土宜順水勢而夾漢爲隄濬
===
其下流以防壅塞此數十年之計也是謂
中策使或憚力役而儉不貲之費因人言
而持兩端之疑日玩歲愒將立待其涸焉
此不終日之計也是無策矣由前二策力
持其議行之則今之下地異日之上腴也
以此興利寧出古人下哉以江防言之瀕
江之大澤以什數而洞庭彭蠡爲鉅二澤
延袤千百里蓋風波之巨匯納汙藏慝之
區也羣小外連內結不可勝詰又比年徵
punctuated:
國初，遺跡具在，監稅者治之。其後水道湮滅，而利擅專門矣。昔賈讓陳治河三策，後世以爲口實。竊謂今之治水者，其策有二：脩孟珙遺政，濬支河，開穴口，塞沙洋，此數世之計也，是謂上策。頃之築沙洋者，監司檄縣吏，縣吏檄圩長，圩長發人徒，因朽壤，積塗泥，將以逭簿責耳。卽千夫荷畚，惡能底績哉？誠使監司爲植，郡縣巡功，不奪流言，不愛重費，相土宜，順水勢，而夾漢爲隄，濬其下流以防壅塞，此數十年之計也，是謂中策。使或憚力役而儉不貲之費，因人言而持兩端之疑，日玩歲愒，將立待其涸焉，此不終日之計也，是無策矣。由前二策，力持其議行之，則今之下地，異日之上腴也。以此興利，寧出古人下哉？
以江防言之，瀕江之大澤以什數，而洞庭、彭蠡爲鉅。二澤延袤千百里，蓋風波之巨匯，納汙藏慝之區也。羣小外連內結，不可勝詰。又比年徵
translation_en:
At the beginning of our dynasty, the surviving works were all still there, and those supervising tax collection maintained them. Subsequently, the waterways silted up and disappeared, and their benefits were monopolized by particular households. In the past, Jia Rang presented three proposals for controlling the Yellow River, which later generations made a stock theme of discussion. I venture to suggest that those managing waterways today have two courses available. Restore the measures left by Meng Gong, dredge the branch channels, open Xuekou, and close the breach at Shayang: this is a plan for several generations and may be called the best course.
Recently, when embankments were being built at Shayang, the surveillance authorities sent orders to the county officials, who sent orders to the polder headmen, who in turn mobilized laborers. They relied on crumbling earth and piled up mud, intending merely to escape censure in the official records. Even if a thousand men shouldered earth baskets, how could they accomplish anything? If the surveillance authorities truly provided firm support [?], and the prefectural and county officials inspected the work, refusing to be swayed by rumors or to begrudge heavy expenditure, examining the suitability of the ground and following the force of the water, they could build embankments on both sides of the Han River and dredge its lower reaches to prevent obstruction. This is a plan for several decades and may be called the middle course. But if they shrink from labor service and economize on the immense expenditure, waver between alternatives because of what others say, and idle away days and years, expecting simply to wait for the water to dry up, this is a plan that will not last even a day: it is no plan at all. If they choose one of the first two courses, uphold it resolutely, and carry it out, today’s low-lying land will become tomorrow’s finest fertile fields. In promoting benefits in this way, need they fall short of the ancients?
As for river defense, the great lakes along the Yangzi number in the tens, with Dongting and Pengli the largest. These two lakes extend for hundreds and thousands of li. They are vast gathering places of wind and waves, and regions that harbor filth and conceal wrongdoing. The bands of malefactors maintain external connections and internal alliances beyond all reckoning. Moreover, in recent years, the levying…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
調夷部方舟所過無不齮龁莫之誰何不
逞之徒冒然而濟其惡遂多事矣然則遏
盜之機不可不爲之蚤計也
國家置監司者二一扼上游以察洞庭一控
下流以備彭蠡頃復增置守備護軍巡行
慮至周也顧承平以來禁令疎闊雖取辦
文法捕盜有人而尺籍之士固無恒心市
井之徒何論長技其流之弊曷可勝言或
好實而惠奸或鬻權而罔利即遇大猾辟
===
易不遑以此爲防是以狼牧者也昔歐陽
脩陳禦盜四事後世以爲名言竊謂今之
治盜者其策有二選吏士簡卒徒分疆域
信期會明賞罰某地有盜不期而獲者賞
之期而後獲者次賞失期而不獲者抵罪
罪先吏士賞先卒徒務操切而不少貸瀕
江井邑凡駔會之鬻舟者爲之籍以紀其
姓名操舟而漁者立之長以譏其出入即
有發覺者連坐之此内治之策也頃因吳
punctuated:
調夷部，方舟所過，無不齮龁，莫之誰何。不逞之徒，冒然而濟其惡，遂多事矣。然則遏盜之機，不可不爲之蚤計也。
國家置監司者二，一扼上游以察洞庭，一控下流以備彭蠡。頃復增置守備，護軍巡行，慮至周也。顧承平以來，禁令疎闊，雖取辦文法，捕盜有人，而尺籍之士固無恒心，市井之徒何論長技？其流之弊，曷可勝言？或好實而惠奸，或鬻權而罔利，即遇大猾，辟易不遑。以此爲防，是以狼牧者也。昔歐陽脩陳禦盜四事，後世以爲名言。竊謂今之治盜者，其策有二：選吏士，簡卒徒，分疆域，信期會，明賞罰。某地有盜，不期而獲者賞之，期而後獲者次賞，失期而不獲者抵罪。罪先吏士，賞先卒徒，務操切而不少貸。瀕江井邑，凡駔會之鬻舟者，爲之籍以紀其姓名；操舟而漁者，立之長以譏其出入，即有發覺者，連坐之。此内治之策也。頃因吳
translation_en:
…tribal troops have been mobilized; wherever their flotillas pass, they prey upon the people, and no one challenges them. Lawless men brazenly carry out their wicked deeds, and disturbances consequently multiply. We must therefore plan early how to forestall banditry.
The state has established two surveillance commissioners: one commands the upper reaches to keep watch over Dongting, and the other controls the lower reaches to guard against trouble at Pengli. Recently, garrison commandants have also been added, with troops providing protection and conducting patrols. These precautions are most thorough. Yet during the long peace, prohibitions have become lax. Although matters are dealt with through documentary procedures and personnel are assigned to apprehend bandits, soldiers on the military rolls lack steadfast commitment; as for men drawn from the marketplaces, what special skills can one expect? Who could fully recount the abuses that follow? Some covet material gain and indulge wrongdoers [?]; others sell their authority for profit. When they encounter powerful villains, they cannot retreat fast enough. To rely on such men for defense is to employ wolves as shepherds. In former times, Ouyang Xiu set forth four measures for resisting bandits, which later generations regarded as authoritative counsel. In my humble view, there are two strategies for suppressing banditry today. Select officers and pick the rank and file; divide their jurisdictions, enforce deadlines, and make rewards and punishments clear. When bandits appear somewhere, reward those who capture them before the appointed time; give a lesser reward to those who capture them only after that time; and punish those who miss the deadline without capturing them. In punishment, begin with the officers; in rewards, begin with the rank and file. Insist on strict enforcement without the slightest indulgence. In settlements along the river, register the names of all brokers who sell boats. Appoint headmen over those who fish from boats, to scrutinize their movements. Whenever wrongdoing is discovered, impose collective liability. This is the strategy for maintaining order within the territory. Recently, owing to Wu…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
越操兵而境外多流賊見兔顧犬不亦晚
乎宣布精銳守要害慎其譏察諜其往來
先聲所加無不震懾此外治之策也誠舉
二策力持其議行之則姦宄不容而舟楫
無警矣以此捍患寧出古人下哉嗟乎地
有四瀆江漢居二焉楚以地重久矣蓋由
河入淮則齊扼其吭由江入海則楚折其
衝乃今舍耒耜不耕罷兵甲不講非所以
重楚也興水利固善矣然而土著多游民
===
羈旅多豪猾游則惰農豪則攘利卽楚地
廣莫而華實之毛歸之四方羈旅者食其
毛而土著者供其賦一何悖也必也稽其
户口覈其田賦爲分籍之法如先臣丘濬
之所載者行之則水利興而利歸於楚楚
其有瘳矣乎慎江防善矣然而羈旅亡命
流轉爲姦無賴相從爲之嚆矢及罪覺則
轉而之他不可逮捕而楚人受纍矣必也
因其丘乘比其什伍立其約長稽其生業
punctuated:
越操兵，而境外多流賊，見兔顧犬，不亦晚乎？宣布精銳，守要害，慎其譏察，諜其往來，先聲所加，無不震懾，此外治之策也。誠舉二策，力持其議行之，則姦宄不容，而舟楫無警矣。以此捍患，寧出古人下哉？
嗟乎！地有四瀆，江漢居二焉。楚以地重久矣。蓋由河入淮，則齊扼其吭；由江入海，則楚折其衝。乃今舍耒耜不耕，罷兵甲不講，非所以重楚也。興水利固善矣，然而土著多游民，羈旅多豪猾。游則惰農，豪則攘利。卽楚地廣莫，而華實之毛歸之四方，羈旅者食其毛，而土著者供其賦，一何悖也！必也稽其户口，覈其田賦，爲分籍之法，如先臣丘濬之所載者行之，則水利興而利歸於楚，楚其有瘳矣乎？
慎江防善矣，然而羈旅亡命，流轉爲姦，無賴相從，爲之嚆矢。及罪覺，則轉而之他，不可逮捕，而楚人受纍矣。必也因其丘乘，比其什伍，立其約長，稽其生業
translation_en:
…with military operations in the Wu–Yue region, many roving bandits have appeared beyond our borders. Is it not too late to look for the hound only after seeing the hare? Deploy picked troops, guard strategic points, conduct inspections carefully, and gather intelligence on their movements. Wherever the advance report of our strength reaches, all will be overawed. This is the strategy for dealing with the external threat. If these two strategies are indeed adopted and resolutely implemented, evildoers will find no refuge, and boats will travel without alarm. In warding off trouble thus, would we fall short of the ancients?
Alas! Of the realm’s four great watercourses, the Yangzi and Han account for two. Chu has long been important because of its geography. On the route from the Yellow River into the Huai, Qi grips the throat; on the route from the Yangzi into the sea, Chu checks the onrush. Yet now ploughs are abandoned and fields left untilled; arms and armour are laid aside and military training neglected. This is no way to uphold Chu’s importance. Developing water conservancy is certainly good. Yet among the established residents are many idlers, and among the sojourners many powerful rogues. The idle neglect farming; the powerful seize the profits. Though Chu’s lands are vast, the produce of its flowers and fruits goes off to the four quarters. Sojourners consume its yield, while established residents pay its taxes. How perverse this is! We must examine household registers, audit land taxes, and institute separate registration, implementing the method recorded by the former minister Qiu Jun. Then water conservancy will flourish and its benefits accrue to Chu. Might Chu then recover from its afflictions?
Careful attention to river defence is good. Yet fugitives among the sojourners drift about committing crimes, and scoundrels join them, taking the lead in wrongdoing. When their crimes are discovered, they move elsewhere and cannot be arrested, while the people of Chu suffer implication in their offences. We must therefore work through the local territorial and levy units, organize the people into groups of ten and five, appoint community compact headmen, and examine their livelihoods…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
重其連坐爲保甲之法如先臣王守仁之
所已試者行之則防患密而無能嫁禍于
楚楚其無患矣乎夫築舍道傍者不可以
慮始眾議奪之也簡髮而櫛者不可以解
紛拘論束之也見彈而求炙者不可與樂
成近利急之也去三者之惑治人得而治
法舉矣其於利病何有哉楚人守一隅之
知固饑者之語餱糧瘍者之語痌瘝也惟
執事留聽焉
punctuated: 重其連坐，爲保甲之法，如先臣王守仁之所已試者行之，則防患密，而無能嫁禍于楚，楚其無患矣乎？夫築舍道傍者，不可以慮始，眾議奪之也；簡髮而櫛者，不可以解紛，拘論束之也；見彈而求炙者，不可與樂成，近利急之也。去三者之惑，治人得而治法舉矣，其於利病何有哉？楚人守一隅之知，固饑者之語餱糧，瘍者之語痌瘝也。惟執事留聽焉。
translation_en:
…make their collective liability more stringent, and implement a system of mutual household registration and surveillance (baojia), such as that already tried by the late minister Wang Shouren. Then precautions against trouble will be thorough, and no one will be able to shift calamity onto Chu. Would Chu not then be free from trouble?

One who builds a house beside the road cannot be consulted about an undertaking at its outset: the multitude of opinions diverts him. One who selects individual hairs before combing cannot untangle confusion: rigid arguments constrain him. One who sees a pellet and immediately asks for roast game cannot share in the enjoyment of success: eagerness for immediate gain makes him impatient. Remove these three delusions, and the right men to govern will be found and sound methods of government put into practice. What difficulty would there then be in securing benefits and remedying ills?

As a man of Chu, I cling to the knowledge of my own small corner. My words are indeed like those of a hungry man speaking of provisions, or a man afflicted with sores speaking of pain. I ask only that you, honored officials, give them your attention.

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄後序
嘉靖戊午秋湖廣鄉試錄成
三近以職事當敘諸末簡三
近惟我
國家設科取士垂二百年自
高皇帝以來內外宣力佐
治平之業者多賢科之士是賴
===
我
皇上敬
天立極
懋德育民
大訓敷言昭揭宇內多士應期
而興凡十有三舉于茲矣由
茲烝烝而進籲俊尊
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄後序

嘉靖戊午秋，湖廣鄉試錄成，三近以職事當敘諸末簡。三近惟我國家設科取士垂二百年，自高皇帝以來，內外宣力、佐治平之業者，多賢科之士是賴。我皇上敬天立極，懋德育民，大訓敷言，昭揭宇內，多士應期而興，凡十有三舉于茲矣。由茲烝烝而進，籲俊尊
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the wuwu year of Jiajing (1558), the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination was completed. By virtue of my official duties, I, Sanjin 三近, am charged with writing a postface on its concluding leaves. I reflect that our dynasty has established examinations to recruit scholars for nearly two hundred years. Since Emperor Gao, in exerting effort in service both at court and in the provinces and assisting the work of orderly and peaceful government, it has relied largely upon men from the examinations for the worthy.

Our present emperor reveres Heaven and establishes the supreme standard, cultivates virtue and nurtures the people. His great instructions are promulgated in words and clearly displayed throughout the realm. Scholars have risen in response to the age; by now, examinations have been held thirteen times. From this point they advance in ever-growing numbers, calling forth outstanding men and honoring …

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
帝億萬斯年未有紀極三近嘗伏
歎自古帝王久道化成未有
盛于
皇上者也及如楚徧觀一時譽髦
之盛則又竊歎江漢之澤豐
鎬之仁地稱首善非偶然爾
爾多士進矣宣力内外上贊
===
聖天子中興之治者多士事也君
臣之大義亦嘗聞之矣乎夫
君天也臣地也乾知大始坤
承天而效成能者地道也臣
道也在易家有嚴君故君稱
父臣稱子承事而用譽者臣
與子之道皆當爾也古之君
punctuated:
帝，億萬斯年，未有紀極。三近嘗伏歎：自古帝王久道化成，未有盛于皇上者也。及如楚，徧觀一時譽髦之盛，則又竊歎：江漢之澤，豐鎬之仁，地稱首善，非偶然爾。
爾多士進矣！宣力内外，上贊聖天子中興之治者，多士事也。君臣之大義，亦嘗聞之矣乎？夫君，天也；臣，地也。乾知大始，坤承天而效成能者，地道也，臣道也。在《易》，家有嚴君，故君稱父，臣稱子。承事而用譽者，臣與子之道皆當爾也。古之君
translation_en:
…the sovereign, for hundreds of millions of years, without any limit. I, Sanjin [?], have reverently marveled that, among the emperors and kings of antiquity, none has surpassed His Majesty in bringing about transformation through enduring adherence to the Way. Upon coming to Chu and surveying the abundance of renowned and outstanding scholars of this age, I privately marveled once more: with the beneficence of the Jiang and Han rivers and the benevolence of Feng and Hao, this land’s reputation as foremost in goodness is no mere accident.
Advance, you many scholars! To exert your strength in service within and beyond the capital, assisting the sage Son of Heaven in his governance of dynastic resurgence, is your task. Have you also heard of the great moral obligation between ruler and minister? The ruler is Heaven; the minister is Earth. Qian presides over the great beginning; Kun follows Heaven and brings its capacities to fruition. This is the Way of Earth and the Way of the minister. In the Book of Changes, the household has a stern ruler; thus the ruler is called the father and the minister the son. To serve obediently and thereby gain praise is what the Way of both minister and son requires. The gentlemen of antiquity…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
子竭其股肱之力以媚一人
鞠躬盡瘁而不以為勞者豈
不欲自處乎其逸哉分使然
爾書曰天惟純佑命則商實
百姓王人罔不秉德明恤烝
民之詩曰天監有周昭格于
下保茲天子生仲山甫蓋言
===
賢才之生上天所以佑保人
君也及攷六臣之烈內一巳
德外陳巳功上保王躬下乂
王室一何勞也仲山甫于周
內養君德外總諸侯入典政
本出營四方又何勞也彼數
臣者皆能敬共其君如事天
punctuated: 子竭其股肱之力，以媚一人，鞠躬盡瘁而不以為勞者，豈不欲自處乎其逸哉？分使然爾。《書》曰：「天惟純佑命，則商實百姓王人，罔不秉德明恤。」《烝民》之詩曰：「天監有周，昭格于下，保茲天子，生仲山甫。」蓋言賢才之生，上天所以佑保人君也。及攷六臣之烈，內一巳德，外陳巳功，上保王躬，下乂王室，一何勞也！仲山甫于周，內養君德，外總諸侯，入典政本，出營四方，又何勞也！彼數臣者，皆能敬共其君，如事天
translation_en: …gentlemen exerted all their strength as the ruler’s limbs to please the One Man, bending themselves to their duties and exhausting their energies without considering it toil. Could they not have wished to enjoy ease themselves? Their allotted duty made them act thus. The Book of Documents says: “Heaven wholly favored and sustained the mandate; thus among Shang’s hundred clans and royal servants, none failed to uphold virtue and exercise discerning care.” The poem “The Multitude of the People” says: “Heaven watched over Zhou; its radiant influence reached below. To protect this Son of Heaven, it brought forth Zhongshan Fu.” This means that Heaven brings worthy and talented men into the world in order to sustain and protect rulers. When we examine the achievements of the six ministers, they inwardly unified their own virtue and outwardly displayed their accomplishments; above, they protected the king’s person, and below, they governed the royal house. How great their toil! In Zhou, Zhongshan Fu inwardly nurtured the ruler’s virtue and outwardly oversaw the regional lords. At court he directed the foundations of government; abroad he attended to the affairs of the four quarters. How great his toil, too! Those ministers could all reverently serve their ruler as they served Heaven…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
事父然故名實純粹天下後
世侈言之爾多士生于
王國式逢明盛固
天篤厚我
皇用昭壽考作人之化者自今宣
力內外亦將格天致治如伊
尹以下六臣者之為乎亦將
===
夙夜匪懈如仲山甫之舉職
乎果如其人庶可以翊文明
之運迂
平壽之休無忝譽髦允徵于首
善矣顧不偉歟語曰愼厥終
惟其始故于多士之始進也
敬申君臣之大義告之
punctuated: 事父然，故名實純粹，天下後世侈言之。爾多士生于王國，式逢明盛，固天篤厚我皇，用昭壽考作人之化者。自今宣力內外，亦將格天致治，如伊尹以下六臣者之為乎？亦將夙夜匪懈，如仲山甫之舉職乎？果如其人，庶可以翊文明之運，迂平壽之休，無忝譽髦，允徵于首善矣，顧不偉歟？語曰：「愼厥終，惟其始。」故于多士之始進也，敬申君臣之大義告之。
translation_en: …as they would serve their fathers. Thus their reputations and actual achievements were alike pure and unalloyed, and the world and later generations have lavishly praised them. You many scholars were born in the royal realm and have encountered an enlightened and flourishing age.
