Surely Heaven is showing profound generosity to our emperor, thereby manifesting his transforming influence in nurturing men of talent for enduring years. From now on, as you exert yourselves in service within and beyond the court, will you likewise move Heaven and bring about good government, as did the six ministers beginning with Yi Yin? Will you likewise remain untiring morning and night, as Zhong Shanfu did in fulfilling his duties? If you truly resemble those men, you may help sustain this age of cultured enlightenment and usher in the blessings of peace and longevity [?], proving worthy of your reputation as outstanding scholars and truly bearing witness to excellence in education. Would this not be magnificent? As the saying goes, “To be careful of the end, attend to the beginning.” Therefore, as you many scholars first advance into public life, I respectfully reiterate the great principles governing ruler and minister and commend them to you.

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
江西南昌府儒學教授蔣三
近謹序
punctuated: 江西南昌府儒學教授蔣三近謹序。
translation_en: Preface respectfully composed by Jiang Sanjin, Instructor in the Confucian School of Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄序
嘉靖戊午秋湖廣復當鄉試
巡按監察御史臣萬恭舉行
如
制秉公肅度務脩成法而加勵焉
先是巡按御史黃季瑞招致
四方文學至是咸集乃以學
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄序

嘉靖戊午秋，湖廣復當鄉試。巡按監察御史臣萬恭舉行如制，秉公肅度，務脩成法而加勵焉。

先是，巡按御史黃季瑞招致四方文學，至是咸集，乃以學
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the wuwu year of Jiajing [1558], Huguang was again due to hold the Provincial Examination. Your servant Wan Gong, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector, conducted it according to the prescribed regulations, maintaining impartiality and strict standards, striving to uphold established procedures and exercising still greater diligence.

Previously, Huang Jirui, the Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector, had invited learned men from all quarters. By this time they had all assembled; thereupon, on the basis of learning …

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
合提學副使張天復與先劉
起宗所簡士三千三百人三
試之得九十人錄其名氏幷
文之式者以
獻學詩從諸執事後縱觀楚髦瑰
特振振濟濟有不可盡紀者
竊惟江漢之麗于王服也任
===
物作貢如元龜包茅之微猶
足以待邦之大事自古志之
矧斯人文涵濡
道化其所遘會尤不偶然者乎
昔
睿宗獻皇帝肇基于郢
知天守道
punctuated:
合提學副使張天復與先劉起宗所簡士三千三百人，三試之，得九十人，錄其名氏幷文之式者以獻。學詩從諸執事後，縱觀楚髦，瑰特振振，濟濟有不可盡紀者。
竊惟江漢之麗于王服也，任物作貢，如元龜、包茅之微，猶足以待邦之大事，自古志之。矧斯人文，涵濡道化，其所遘會尤不偶然者乎！
昔睿宗獻皇帝肇基于郢，知天守道
translation_en:
…bringing together the 3,300 scholars selected by Zhang Tianfu, the Education Intendant holding the rank of Vice Commissioner, and his predecessor Liu Qizong [?], they examined them in three sessions and selected ninety. They recorded their names, together with examination compositions suitable to serve as models, for presentation to the throne. I, Xueshi, followed behind the officials conducting the examination and surveyed the outstanding scholars of Chu: extraordinary in talent, flourishing and numerous, they possessed qualities that could not all be recorded.
I humbly reflect that, when the lands of the Jiang and Han rivers came under royal rule, tribute was levied according to their products. Even such humble offerings as great tortoise shells and bundles of thatching grass were sufficient to provide for the state's great ceremonies; this has been recorded since antiquity. How much more must this be true of these cultivated men, steeped in the transforming influence of the Way! Surely the occasion they have encountered is especially far from accidental!
Formerly, Emperor Ruizong Xian established his foundation in Ying, comprehending Heaven and keeping to the Way…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
含靈篤慶誕毓
皇上
神聖繼天於昭
大統夫五百年而王者興其間有
命世者多士之生應
皇上之會此其效也棫樸之雅曰
倬彼雲漢爲章于天周王壽
===
考遐不作人思齊曰古之人
無斁譽髦斯士夫多士所以
寧文王也詩人不云士之賢
乃云文王壽考無斁之所致
然則楚材之盛不有所由致
哉我
皇上道乆化成之效章章較著已
punctuated: 含靈篤慶，誕毓皇上，神聖繼天，於昭大統。夫五百年而王者興，其間有命世者。多士之生，應皇上之會，此其效也。《棫樸》之雅曰：「倬彼雲漢，爲章于天。周王壽考，遐不作人？」《思齊》曰：「古之人無斁，譽髦斯士。」夫多士所以寧文王也。詩人不云士之賢，乃云文王壽考無斁之所致。然則楚材之盛，不有所由致哉？我皇上道乆化成之效，章章較著已。
translation_en:
…embracing numinous potency and accumulating abundant blessings, he begot and nurtured His Majesty, whose divine sagacity carries on Heaven’s mandate and gloriously illuminates the great imperial succession. A true king arises every five hundred years, and in the interval there are men renowned in their age. That these many scholars have been born to coincide with His Majesty’s reign is evidence of this.

The court hymn The Oak Clusters (Yupu) says: “Resplendent is that River of Clouds, forming a pattern in Heaven. Long-lived is the king of Zhou: does he not nurture men of talent?” Siqi says: “The man of old never wearied; he honored and cultivated these scholars.” These many scholars were the means by which King Wen was brought repose. Yet the poet speaks not of the scholars’ worthiness, but attributes it to King Wen’s longevity and unflagging effort. Does not the flourishing of talent in Chu likewise have a source? The effects of His Majesty’s long practice of the Way and the fulfillment of his transforming influence are already abundantly manifest.

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
雖然士之自致與其所由致
於上其道未始不相須也士
以是應之而異其初之所成
上以是道之而違其終之所
望是鄉試之錄士辟之虛車
輪轅徒飾無所用之周之制
也三年賓興其鄉之賢者能
===
者而獻其書于王王拜受之
登之天府內史貳之此謂使
民興賢出使長也使民興能
入使治也賢與能皆書矣而
其用之德成而上藝成而下
其等異也當是時士之所以
致於上爭懋其德而不獨以
punctuated: 雖然，士之自致與其所由致於上，其道未始不相須也。士以是應之，而異其初之所成；上以是道之，而違其終之所望，是鄉試之錄士，辟之虛車，輪轅徒飾，無所用之。周之制也，三年賓興其鄉之賢者能者，而獻其書于王。王拜受之，登之天府，內史貳之。此謂使民興賢，出使長也；使民興能，入使治也。賢與能皆書矣，而其用之，德成而上，藝成而下，其等異也。當是時，士之所以致於上，爭懋其德，而不獨以
translation_en:
Nevertheless, the means by which scholars advance themselves and those by which they are brought forward by their superiors have always depended upon one another. If scholars respond to this examination in ways that depart from their original formation, and their superiors guide them through it in ways that frustrate their ultimate aspirations, then selecting scholars through the Provincial Examination is like an empty carriage: its wheels and shafts are mere ornament, serving no purpose.
Under the Zhou system, every three years the worthy and capable men of each district were honored as guests and recommended, and the written record of them was presented to the king. The king bowed as he received it and deposited it in the Celestial Treasury; the Interior Scribe kept a duplicate. This is what was meant by having the people recommend the worthy, who were sent out to serve as leaders, and having the people recommend the capable, who were brought in to administer affairs. Both the worthy and the capable were recorded, but in employing them, those accomplished in virtue were placed above, and those accomplished in practical arts below: their ranks differed. At that time, scholars seeking advancement before their superiors competed in cultivating their virtue, rather than relying solely upon …

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
藝自能故罝兎在野之人至
可爲公侯腹心功棐迪篤罔
不在時於稽內史之治信可
明徵後世抽天府之藏猶可
以指述勵翼篤棐之士而無
愧矣今鄉試之典其禮與成
周並隆者也書多士之文辭
===
卒澤於道德仁義粹如也其
所以應上之求得猶未免於
藝乎如以成而下者自獻得
無與所望者背乎書曰皇極
之敷言是彝是訓惟帝其訓
皇之敬德錫厥庶民猶彝訓也矧
多士首沐
punctuated: 藝自能，故罝兎在野之人，至可爲公侯腹心，功棐迪篤，罔不在時。於稽內史之治，信可明徵。後世抽天府之藏，猶可以指述勵翼篤棐之士而無愧矣。今鄉試之典，其禮與成周並隆者也。書多士之文辭，卒澤於道德仁義，粹如也。其所以應上之求，得猶未免於藝乎？如以成而下者自獻，得無與所望者背乎？《書》曰：「皇極之敷言，是彝是訓，惟帝其訓。」皇之敬德，錫厥庶民，猶彝訓也。矧多士首沐
translation_en:
…regard themselves as capable on the strength of their accomplishments alone. Thus even men setting rabbit nets in the countryside could become the trusted confidants of dukes and lords: those who rendered service and assistance, guided others, and acted with sincerity were all to be found among them. Examining the administration of the Interior Scribe provides clear confirmation of this [?]. When later generations draw upon the holdings of the Celestial Treasury, they can still identify and recount the deeds of men who diligently assisted their rulers and served them faithfully, without cause for shame.

Today the rites of the Provincial Examination are as exalted as those of the Zhou at its height. We record the compositions of the many scholars, ultimately imbued with the Way, virtue, benevolence, and righteousness, and wholly pure [?]. Yet can the means by which they answer their sovereign’s call still remain confined to accomplishments? If they present themselves on the basis of attainments that rank lower, would this not run counter to what is expected of them? The Book of Documents says: “The words promulgated by the August Ultimate are constant principles and instructions; they are the sovereign’s instruction.” The sovereign’s reverence for virtue, bestowed upon his common people, likewise constitutes enduring instruction. How much more, then, these many scholars, who have been foremost in receiving…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
聖化久且益深自玆以往共能克
對大章而有指述於後世以
無失其終之望則文王以寧
之盛尚亦有稽於斯錄也夫
學詩不佞敬敘諸首簡維時
總督湖廣川貴軍務兵部侍
郎王崇先巡撫今總督湖廣
===
川貴採木都御史李憲卿巡
撫湖廣都御史趙炳然撫治
鄖陽都御史劉學易保釐輯
寧文武爲憲江漢若流膠序
咸賴巡按直隸御史林騰蛟
考賦所至視學談經多士風
焉若雅志右文則總兵安遠
punctuated:
聖化，久且益深。自玆以往，共能克對大章，而有指述於後世，以無失其終之望，則文王以寧之盛，尚亦有稽於斯錄也夫！學詩不佞，敬敘諸首簡。
維時，總督湖廣川貴軍務兵部侍郎王崇，先巡撫、今總督湖廣川貴採木都御史李憲卿，巡撫湖廣都御史趙炳然，撫治鄖陽都御史劉學易，保釐輯寧，文武爲憲，江漢若流，膠序咸賴。巡按直隸御史林騰蛟，考賦所至，視學談經，多士風焉。若雅志右文，則總兵安遠
translation_en:
…the sage sovereign’s transforming influence, which, with time, has grown ever deeper. If, from this point onward, all can duly answer to this great example and leave something for later generations to cite and recount, thus fulfilling the hope that they will remain steadfast to the end, then the flourishing peace that King Wen attained may also find testimony in this record! I, Xueshi, lacking in ability, respectfully place this preface at the beginning of the volume.
At this time, Wang Chong, Vice Minister of War and Supreme Commander of Military Affairs in Huguang, Sichuan, and Guizhou; Li Xianqing, Censor-in-chief, formerly Grand Coordinator and now Superintendent of Timber Procurement in Huguang, Sichuan, and Guizhou; Zhao Bingran, Censor-in-chief and Grand Coordinator of Huguang; and Liu Xueyi, Censor-in-chief and Pacification Commissioner of Yunyang, safeguarded and governed the region, bringing harmony and peace. They provided models in civil and military affairs; the Jiang and Han regions followed their course like flowing water, and the schools all benefited from their support. Lin Tengjiao, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Zhili, examined the levies [?] wherever he went, inspected the schools, and discussed the Classics; the many scholars were influenced by his example. As for those whose enduring aspiration was to honor literary learning, there was the Regional Commander, [the Marquis of] Anyuan …

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
侯栁震守備太監張方而工
部郎中張國珍員外郎朱裳
主事方良曙先後有事兹土
胥勸得人者也左叅政雷賀
右叅政徐霈游震得張希舉
右叅議成子學李燧宋廷表
郝成性副使龔秉德黃宗器
===
程秀民張正和周鎬王光祖
熊勉學僉事于錦周美栁宗
葵崔都朱天球署都指揮僉
事常勳與入
賀副使馮覲叅議李萬實皆與
有勞焉至是計上而賢能適
與計偕斯亦全楚之修以待
punctuated: 侯栁震、守備太監張方，而工部郎中張國珍、員外郎朱裳、主事方良曙，先後有事兹土，胥勸得人者也。左叅政雷賀，右叅政徐霈、游震得、張希舉，右叅議成子學、李燧、宋廷表、郝成性，副使龔秉德、黃宗器、程秀民、張正和、周鎬、王光祖、熊勉學，僉事于錦、周美、栁宗葵、崔都、朱天球，署都指揮僉事常勳，與入賀副使馮覲、叅議李萬實，皆與有勞焉。至是計上，而賢能適與計偕，斯亦全楚之修以待
translation_en: …Marquis Liu Zhen and the eunuch Defender Zhang Fang; also Zhang Guozhen, Director in the Ministry of Works, Zhu Shang, Vice Director, and Fang Liangshu, Secretary, who successively undertook duties in this territory—all encouraged the selection of worthy men. Lei He, Left Administration Vice Commissioner; Xu Pei, You Zhende, and Zhang Xiju, Right Administration Vice Commissioners; Cheng Zixue, Li Sui, Song Tingbiao, and Hao Chengxing, Right Administration Assistant Commissioners; Gong Bingde, Huang Zongqi, Cheng Xiumin, Zhang Zhenghe, Zhou Hao, Wang Guangzu, and Xiong Mianxue, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Yu Jin, Zhou Mei, Liu Zongkui, Cui Du, and Zhu Tianqiu, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; Chang Xun, acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner; together with Feng Jin, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and Li Wanshi, Administration Assistant Commissioner, who had gone to court to offer congratulations—all contributed their efforts. Now the accounts have been submitted, and the worthy and capable men are duly traveling to the capital along with those accounts. This, too, represents the cultivation undertaken throughout Chu in preparation for…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
邦之大用者也於戲備矣
廣東廣州府儒學教授桂學
詩謹序
punctuated:
邦之大用者也。於戲！備矣！
廣東廣州府儒學教授桂學詩謹序。
translation_en:
…for great service to the state. Ah! All is now prepared!
This preface is respectfully composed by Gui Xueshi, Instructor at the Confucian School of Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong.

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試
監臨官
巡按湖廣監察御史吳百朋〔惟錫浙江義烏縣人丁未進士〕
提調官
湖廣等處承宣布政使司左布政使傅鎮〔國鼎福建中左千戶所籍福清縣人壬辰進士〕
湖廣等處承宣布政使司右布政使谷嶠〔惟升直隸興州前屯衛官籍河南息縣人戊戌進士〕
監試官
湖廣等處提刑按察司按察使俞憲〔汝成直隸無錫縣人戊戌進士〕
湖廣等處提刑按察司副使章士元〔伯允直隸吳縣人甲辰進士〕
===
考試官
廣東廣州府儒學教授桂學詩〔用言江西上饒縣人癸卯貢士〕
江西南昌府儒學教授蔣三近〔秉修四川涪州人丙午貢士〕

translation_en:
Huguang Provincial Examination, the thirty-seventh year of Jiajing (1558)

Supervising Official
Wu Baipeng, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Huguang. His courtesy name was Weixi; he was from Yiwu County, Zhejiang, and was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the dingwei year.

Proctors
Fu Zhen, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Huguang. His courtesy name was Guoding; he was registered with the Zhongzuo Battalion in Fujian and was a native of Fuqing County. He was a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year.
Gu Jiao, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Huguang. His courtesy name was Weisheng; he held official-household registration with the Xingzhou Front Garrison Guard in Zhili and was a native of Xi County, Henan. He was a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.

Examination Overseers
Yu Xian, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Huguang. His courtesy name was Rucheng; he was from Wuxi County, Zhili, and was a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.
Zhang Shiyuan, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Huguang. His courtesy name was Boyun; he was from Wu County, Zhili, and was a metropolitan graduate of the jiachen year.

Examiners
Gui Xueshi, Professor of the Confucian School of Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. His courtesy name was Yongyan; he was from Shangrao County, Jiangxi, and was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the guimao year.
Jiang Sanjin, Professor of the Confucian School of Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Bingxiu; he was from Fuzhou, Sichuan, and was a tribute scholar of the bingwu year.

Associate Examiners
Yu Zhaoyang, Instructor of the Confucian School of Jinzhou, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Shaoming; he held official-household registration with the Guilin Central Guard in Guangxi and was a native of Dingyuan County, Zhili. He was a tribute scholar of the yimao year.
Huang Hua, Instructor of the Confucian School of Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Deyuan; he was from Liuhe County, Yingtian Prefecture, and was a tribute scholar of the renzi year.
Gu Shi, Instructor of the Confucian School of Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture, Henan. His courtesy name was Shike; he was from Xinghua County, Zhili, and was a tribute scholar of the yimao year.
Wu Zhu, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yushan County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Yifan; he was from Changle County, Fujian, and was a tribute scholar of the jiyou year.
Zhu Tu, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yongjia County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. His courtesy name was Xiyu; he was from Leping County, Jiangxi, and was a tribute scholar of the bingwu year.

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:

translation_en:

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:

punctuated:

巡綽官：

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
舜有臣五人而天下治
及其至也察乎天地
心之所同然者何也謂理也義也聖人先
得我心之所同然耳故理義之悅我心
猶芻豢之悅我口
易
元吉在上大有慶也
===
說之大民勸矣哉
制而用之謂之法利用出入民咸用之謂
之神
昔者聖人之作易也將以順性命之理是
以立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔
與剛立人之道曰仁與義兼三才而兩
之故易六畫而成卦分陰分陽迭用柔
剛故易六位而成章
書
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

舜有臣五人，而天下治。

及其至也，察乎天地。

心之所同然者何也？謂理也，義也。聖人先得我心之所同然耳。故理義之悅我心，猶芻豢之悅我口。

易

元吉在上，大有慶也。

說之大，民勸矣哉！

制而用之謂之法，利用出入，民咸用之謂之神。

昔者聖人之作易也，將以順性命之理，是以立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。兼三才而兩之，故易六畫而成卦；分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，故易六位而成章。

書
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Shun had five ministers, and all under Heaven was well governed.

When it reaches its utmost extent, it is manifest throughout Heaven and Earth.

What is it that our hearts alike affirm? It is principle and righteousness. The sages merely apprehended before us what our hearts alike affirm. Thus principle and righteousness delight my heart just as the meat of grass-fed and grain-fed animals delights my palate.

Book of Changes (Yi)

Supreme good fortune in the highest position: there is great cause for celebration.

Great indeed is the power of joy: the people are inspired to exert themselves!

Fashioning it and putting it to use is called a method. Making its use beneficial in going forth and coming in, so that all the people employ it, is called the numinous.

When the sages of old made the Changes, they intended thereby to accord with the principles of human nature and destiny. Thus they established the Way of Heaven as yin and yang, the Way of Earth as yielding and firm, and the Way of humankind as benevolence and righteousness. They encompassed the Three Powers and doubled each; hence, in the Changes, six lines form a hexagram. Distinguishing yin and yang and employing the yielding and firm alternately, the six positions of the Changes thus form an ordered pattern.

Book of Documents (Shu)

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
惟動丕應徯志以昭受上帝天其申命用
休
江漢朝宗于海九江孔殷沱潛旣道雲土
夢作乂
一曰食二曰貨三曰祀四曰司空五曰司
徒六曰司寇七曰賓八曰師
公其惟時成周建無窮之基亦有無窮之
聞
詩
===
采采芣苢薄言袺之采采芣苢薄言襭之
如跂斯翼如矢斯棘如鳥斯革如翬斯飛
君子攸躋
虎拜稽首天子萬年
豐年多黍多稂亦有高廩萬億及秭爲酒
爲醴烝畀祖妣以洽百禮降福孔皆
春秋
秋九月齊侯宋公江人黃人盟于貫〔僖公〕
〔二年〕
punctuated:
惟動丕應，徯志，以昭受上帝，天其申命用休。

江漢朝宗于海，九江孔殷，沱潛旣道，雲土夢作乂。

一曰食，二曰貨，三曰祀，四曰司空，五曰司徒，六曰司寇，七曰賓，八曰師。

公其惟時成周，建無窮之基，亦有無窮之聞。

詩

采采芣苢，薄言袺之；采采芣苢，薄言襭之。

如跂斯翼，如矢斯棘，如鳥斯革，如翬斯飛，君子攸躋。

虎拜稽首，天子萬年！

豐年多黍多稂，亦有高廩，萬億及秭。爲酒爲醴，烝畀祖妣，以洽百禮，降福孔皆。

春秋

秋九月，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人盟于貫〔僖公〕〔二年〕。
translation_en:
…Whenever you act, there is a mighty response; they await your intentions. Thus you may illustriously receive the favor of the Lord on High, and Heaven will renew its mandate with blessings.

The Jiang and Han rivers flow toward the sea as lords attend court before their sovereign. The nine rivers are thoroughly regulated; the Tuo and Qian have been channeled, and the lands of Yun and Meng brought under cultivation.

The first is food; the second, goods; the third, sacrifices; the fourth, the Minister of Works; the fifth, the Minister of Education; the sixth, the Minister of Justice; the seventh, guests; and the eighth, the army.

May you, Duke, thereby bring Zhou to completion, establishing an everlasting foundation and likewise an everlasting reputation.

Book of Odes

Gather, gather the plantain; gather it in the skirts held in your hands. Gather, gather the plantain; gather it in the skirts tucked into your belts.

Like a figure standing on tiptoe in stately poise, like an arrow in its straightness, like a bird spreading its wings, like a pheasant in flight: such is the hall the noble lord ascends.

Hu bowed and knocked his head to the ground: “May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years!”

In a plentiful year there is much millet and much darnel [?], and there are lofty granaries, holding quantities counted in myriads, hundreds of millions, and trillions. Make wine and sweet liquor to present to the ancestral grandfathers and grandmothers, fulfilling the hundred rites. The blessings they send down are all-embracing.

Spring and Autumn Annals

In autumn, in the ninth month, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and representatives of Jiang and Huang made a covenant at Guan. 〔Duke Xi〕〔Second year〕

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
歸父還自晉至笙遂奔齊宣公十有八年
夏蔡朝吳出奔鄭昭公十有五年秋
晉士鞅宋樂祁犁衞北宮喜曹人邾人
滕人會于扈昭公二十有七年三月
公會劉子晉侯宋公蔡侯衞侯陳子鄭
伯許男曹伯莒子邾子頓子胡子滕子
薛伯杞伯小邾子齊國夏于召陵侵楚
定公四年
吳入州來成公七年
===
冬楚子蔡侯陳侯許男頓子沈子徐人越
人伐吳昭公五年夏曹公孫會自鄸
出奔宋昭公二十年〔鄧景文字體道〕
禮記
凡在天下九州之民者無不咸獻其力以
共皇天上帝社稷寢廟山林名川之祀
樂者心之動也聲者樂之象也文采節奏
聲之飾也君子動其本樂其象然後治
其飾
punctuated:
歸父還自晉，至笙，遂奔齊。宣公十有八年。夏，蔡朝吳出奔鄭。昭公十有五年。秋，晉士鞅、宋樂祁犁、衞北宮喜、曹人、邾人、滕人會于扈。昭公二十有七年。三月，公會劉子、晉侯、宋公、蔡侯、衞侯、陳子、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、莒子、邾子、頓子、胡子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊國夏于召陵，侵楚。定公四年。吳入州來。成公七年。
冬，楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、許男、頓子、沈子、徐人、越人伐吳。昭公五年。夏，曹公孫會自鄸出奔宋。昭公二十年。〔鄧景文字體道〕
禮記
凡在天下九州之民者，無不咸獻其力，以共皇天上帝、社稷、寢廟、山林、名川之祀。
樂者，心之動也；聲者，樂之象也；文采節奏，聲之飾也。君子動其本，樂其象，然後治其飾。
translation_en:
Guifu, returning from Jin, reached Sheng and then fled to Qi. (Eighteenth year of Duke Xuan.) In summer, Chao Wu of Cai fled to Zheng. (Fifteenth year of Duke Zhao.) In autumn, Shi Yang of Jin, Yue Qili of Song, Beigong Xi of Wei, and representatives of Cao, Zhu, and Teng met at Hu. (Twenty-seventh year of Duke Zhao.) In the third month, the duke met with Viscount Liu, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Wei, the Viscount of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Lesser Zhu, and Guo Xia of Qi at Shaoling, and they invaded Chu. (Fourth year of Duke Ding.) Wu entered Zhoulai. (Seventh year of Duke Cheng.)
In winter, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Chen, the Baron of Xu, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Shen, and forces from Xu and Yue attacked Wu. (Fifth year of Duke Zhao.) In summer, Gongsun Hui of Cao fled from Meng to Song. (Twentieth year of Duke Zhao.) 〔Deng Jingwen, courtesy name Tidao.〕
Book of Rites
Among all the people of the Nine Provinces under Heaven, none fails to contribute their labor to provide for sacrifices to August Heaven and the Lord on High, to the gods of soil and grain, to the ancestral chambers and temples, and to the mountains, forests, and renowned rivers.
Music is the stirring of the heart; sound is the manifestation of music; patterned embellishments and rhythm are the adornment of sound. The gentleman stirs its source, takes pleasure in its manifestation, and only then regulates its adornment.

之謂備

第貳塲

大哉堯之為君

擬漢令郡國求遺賢詔〔高帝十一年〕

第叁塲
translation_en:
Blessing means completeness; completeness is the name for being in accord in every respect. To be in accord in all respects is what is meant by completeness.
Benevolence is on the right; the Way is on the left.
Second Session
Discourse
“Great indeed was Yao as a ruler!”

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第五道
問養士莫重於明倫化民莫先於善俗斯
二者人治之大者也聖帝明王其教思
無窮矣而施由近始恒於湯沐惓惓焉
書紀平章詩頌譽髦皆是道也兩漢繼
周而興稍爲近古詔郡國以孝廉舉士
詔有司以孝弟教民流風善政猶有存
者然而歌風餘烈徒詫乎帝鄉臨雍上
儀無裨於主德方諸古昔遠矣其得失
===
可詳言之歟由漢而下亦有足稱者歟
我
太祖高皇帝繼天立極用夏變夷治教畢張人
士永賴過淮
諭父老示之以化俗之大端
卽位諭中書示之以興學之上務篤近舉遠
德教沛然洋洋
聖謨萬世爲楷亦可得而誦說之歟至我
皇上建
punctuated:
第五道

問：養士莫重於明倫，化民莫先於善俗。斯二者，人治之大者也。聖帝明王，其教思無窮矣，而施由近始，恒於湯沐惓惓焉。書紀平章，詩頌譽髦，皆是道也。兩漢繼周而興，稍爲近古，詔郡國以孝廉舉士，詔有司以孝弟教民，流風善政猶有存者。然而歌風餘烈徒詫乎帝鄉，臨雍上儀無裨於主德，方諸古昔遠矣。其得失可詳言之歟？由漢而下，亦有足稱者歟？我太祖高皇帝繼天立極，用夏變夷，治教畢張，人士永賴。過淮，諭父老，示之以化俗之大端；卽位，諭中書，示之以興學之上務。篤近舉遠，德教沛然洋洋，聖謨萬世爲楷，亦可得而誦說之歟？至我皇上建
translation_en:
Fifth Question

Question: In nurturing scholars, nothing matters more than clarifying human relationships; in transforming the people, nothing takes precedence over improving customs. These two are great concerns of human governance. The sage emperors and enlightened kings gave boundless thought to instruction, yet began its implementation close at hand, showing constant solicitude for their home domains. The Documents records the harmonizing of the people, and the Odes praises distinguished men: both express this Way. The Former and Later Han arose after the Zhou and came somewhat close to ancient practice. They commanded the commanderies and kingdoms to recommend men for filial devotion and integrity, and ordered the responsible officials to teach the people filial devotion and respect for elder brothers. Some inherited influence and good government thus survived. Yet the lingering achievements celebrated in the Song of the Wind served merely as a boast for the emperor’s hometown, while the grand ceremony of visiting the imperial school did nothing to advance the ruler’s virtue. Compared with antiquity, these fell far short. Can you explain their successes and failures in detail? From the Han onward, were there also examples worthy of praise?

Our Emperor Taizu Gao succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard, transforming the peoples beyond Chinese civilization through its ways. Government and instruction were fully instituted, to the lasting benefit of scholars and people. When passing through Huai, he instructed the elders, showing them the essential principles for transforming customs; upon ascending the throne, he instructed the Secretariat, showing it that promoting schools was a foremost responsibility. He devoted care to those nearby and extended it to those far away; his moral instruction flowed abundantly and spread widely. His sagely plans are a model for all generations. Can you also recite and explain them? Now our reigning emperor has established …

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
君師之極操政教之本
聲教所訖莫不彬彬而
首善之建始于南國其
幸舊邦也頒
詔闕里立烝民之彝訓其顯
先德也勒文郡學覲
皇考之耿光所以丕承
祖禰廣勵士民亦必有典要乎視我
皇祖之舊章帝王之遐軌同一揆乎否邪夫識
===
其大者雅賢者能之其對揚
天子之
顯命
問大倫有五而君親為重臣之事君子之
事親惟忠與孝爾此至德要道萬世不
可易也昔之論大孝純忠至虞舜周公
止矣載攷傳記有分忠孝為二者有合
忠孝為一者有專問孝而不及於忠者
豈其道固當兼盡而亦未始相悖歟孝
banxin: 鄉試錄 十一 本
punctuated:
君師之極，操政教之本，聲教所訖，莫不彬彬。而首善之建，始于南國。其幸舊邦也，頒詔闕里，立烝民之彝訓；其顯先德也，勒文郡學，覲皇考之耿光。所以丕承祖禰，廣勵士民，亦必有典要乎？視我皇祖之舊章、帝王之遐軌，同一揆乎否邪？夫識其大者，雅賢者能之，其對揚天子之顯命。
問：大倫有五，而君親為重。臣之事君，子之事親，惟忠與孝爾。此至德要道，萬世不可易也。昔之論大孝純忠，至虞舜、周公止矣。載攷傳記，有分忠孝為二者，有合忠孝為一者，有專問孝而不及於忠者。豈其道固當兼盡，而亦未始相悖歟？孝
translation_en:
…the highest standard for ruler and teacher, and grasps the foundations of government and instruction. Wherever his civilizing influence reaches, all display cultivated refinement. The establishment of a foremost center of moral instruction began in the southern lands. When he visited his former homeland, he issued an edict to Queli, establishing enduring teachings for the people; in making manifest his forebears’ virtue, he had a text engraved at the prefectural school, displaying [?] the brilliant glory of his deceased imperial father. Surely there are authoritative principles governing these means of carrying forward the legacy of his ancestors and father and broadly encouraging scholars and commoners? Compared with the established institutions of our imperial ancestor and the distant precedents of ancient emperors and kings, do these follow the same standard or not? Those of cultivated worth [?] can recognize what is essential in these matters. Respond, then, by extolling the Son of Heaven’s illustrious command.
Question: There are five cardinal human relationships, of which those with one’s ruler and parents are especially weighty. A minister’s service to his ruler and a son’s service to his parents consist simply in loyalty and filial piety. These constitute the highest virtue and the essential Way, unalterable for all generations. In past discussions of supreme filial piety and pure loyalty, none have surpassed Shun of Yu and the Duke of Zhou. Yet examination of transmitted writings and records reveals that some distinguish loyalty and filial piety as two things, some unite them as one, and some inquire exclusively into filial piety without addressing loyalty. Is it that this Way requires both to be fulfilled completely, and that they have never been mutually opposed? Filial piety…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
經一書成於曾子門人之手其言自天
子至於庶人孝無終始後世乃有擬作
忠經而其中所列則以聖君冢臣百工
守宰兆人為序然則忠之為道又不專
為人臣者訓其可與孝經相為表裏否
歟抑别有可議者歟我
國家以綱常為治嘗莊誦
孝順事實
歷代臣鑒與夫
===
五倫書所載所以教天下之為人臣子者至
矣其宏綱要旨可數而敬陳之歟諸士
子行且服官移孝為忠矣試以平日所
講明者著于篇以觀敦本重倫之學毋
徒曰藝焉已哉
問天道運而陰陽相巡故百物化聖德運
而文武並用故百志成三代之英非獨
文事能也而亦有用武之績若大禹伊
尹周公是已聖帝明王咸用之而致盛
punctuated:
經一書，成於曾子門人之手，其言自天子至於庶人，孝無終始。後世乃有擬作忠經，而其中所列，則以聖君、冢臣、百工、守宰、兆人為序。然則忠之為道，又不專為人臣者訓，其可與《孝經》相為表裏否歟？抑别有可議者歟？我國家以綱常為治，嘗莊誦《孝順事實》、《歷代臣鑒》與夫《五倫書》所載，所以教天下之為人臣子者至矣。其宏綱要旨，可數而敬陳之歟？諸士子行且服官，移孝為忠矣。試以平日所講明者著于篇，以觀敦本重倫之學，毋徒曰藝焉已哉！

問：天道運而陰陽相巡，故百物化；聖德運而文武並用，故百志成。三代之英，非獨文事能也，而亦有用武之績，若大禹、伊尹、周公是已。聖帝明王咸用之而致盛
translation_en:
…the Classic of Filial Piety was composed by disciples of Zengzi. It speaks of everyone from the Son of Heaven down to the common people, stating that filial piety has neither end nor beginning. Later generations composed a Classic of Loyalty in imitation of it, arranging its categories in the following order: sage rulers, chief ministers, the various officials, prefects and magistrates, and the multitude of the people. Thus, the way of loyalty likewise provides instruction beyond those who serve as subjects. Can this work and the Classic of Filial Piety complement one another as outward expression and inner substance? Or are there other points open to question? Our dynasty governs through the cardinal bonds and constant virtues. We have reverently read the Accounts of Filial Obedience, the Mirror for Ministers of Successive Dynasties, and the Book of the Five Human Relationships: their instruction for all under Heaven who serve as subjects and children is most complete. Can you enumerate and respectfully set forth their broad principles and essential purport? You candidates will soon enter official service and turn your filial devotion into loyalty. Set down in writing what you have studied and clarified in your daily learning, so that we may see your understanding of strengthening the foundations and honoring human relationships. Do not treat this merely as an exercise in literary skill!

Question: The Way of Heaven moves, and yin and yang follow one another in turn; thus the myriad things undergo transformation. Sagely virtue operates, and civil and military means are employed together; thus the many aspirations are fulfilled. The outstanding men of the Three Dynasties were skilled not only in civil affairs but also achieved military successes. Such were Yu the Great, Yi Yin, and the Duke of Zhou. Sage emperors and enlightened kings employed both and thereby brought about flourishing…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
治其經緯之章戡定之烈果相須乎否
邪後世若左袒之師澶淵之役武功競
矣或木彊少文或不學無術終不以其
故貶功獨何歟他若才儗管葛而前部
生心言事慷慨而車戰失利之二子非
不文也何爲乎勝負無益邪我
皇上文武聖神法天爲治思得全才而任使之
今搢紳之士莫不知兵封疆之臣莫不
講業文武之材具矣南平日本北走匈
===
奴率用此也然而當事諸臣猶或不能
稱
上意何哉頃者
詔求備邊之材羣臣得舉所知矣其間才各有
長短而華實亦異誇大者或慕請纓之
名雍容者或襲緩帶之譽執秩者將何
以紏察之夫文武爲憲其人楚產也諸
士尚友古人必有足述者願聞其槩當
爲籍
punctuated: 治。其經緯之章、戡定之烈，果相須乎？否邪？後世若左袒之師、澶淵之役，武功競矣，或木彊少文，或不學無術，終不以其故貶功，獨何歟？他若才儗管葛而前部生心、言事慷慨而車戰失利之二子，非不文也，何爲乎勝負無益邪？我皇上文武聖神，法天爲治，思得全才而任使之。今搢紳之士莫不知兵，封疆之臣莫不講業，文武之材具矣。南平日本，北走匈奴，率用此也。然而當事諸臣猶或不能稱上意，何哉？頃者，詔求備邊之材，羣臣得舉所知矣。其間才各有長短，而華實亦異。誇大者或慕請纓之名，雍容者或襲緩帶之譽，執秩者將何以紏察之？夫「文武爲憲」，其人楚產也。諸士尚友古人，必有足述者，願聞其槩，當爲籍
translation_en:
…good government. Were their achievements in ordering the realm and their glorious deeds in pacifying it indeed mutually dependent, or were they not? In later ages, military prowess flourished in such instances as the army that bared its left arms and the campaign at Chanyuan. Some commanders were blunt and unpolished; others lacked learning and practical ability. Yet their achievements were never belittled on that account. Why was this so? Consider, too, those two men: one whose talents were compared with those of Guan Zhong and Zhuge Liang, yet whose vanguard harbored disloyal intentions; the other who spoke passionately on affairs of state, yet suffered defeat in chariot warfare. Neither lacked civil accomplishments. Why, then, did these contribute nothing to securing victory rather than defeat?

Our Emperor, accomplished in civil and military affairs, sagely and divinely perceptive, models his rule on Heaven and seeks men of comprehensive ability to employ. Today, among the gentlemen who wear the official sash, none is ignorant of military affairs; among the ministers entrusted with the frontiers, none neglects the study of his duties. Talent in both civil and military affairs is thus available. Pacifying the Japanese in the south and putting the Xiongnu to flight in the north have generally depended upon such men. Yet some ministers charged with these affairs still fail to fulfill His Majesty’s wishes. Why is this?

Recently, an edict sought men capable of preparing the frontier defenses, allowing the assembled ministers to recommend those they knew. Among these men, each has strengths and weaknesses, and outward brilliance differs from substantial ability. Boastful men may covet the fame of volunteering to bind the enemy; men of leisurely bearing may lay claim to the reputation of commanders who wore their sashes loose. How are those holding office to scrutinize them? The man described as ‘a model in civil and military affairs’ was a native of Chu. You gentlemen take the ancients as your friends and must have something worth recounting. I wish to hear its essentials and shall enter them in a register…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
奏之
問六籍而下楚士以論著鳴者吾得二人
焉昔稱或爲詞賦之祖或得孔孟之傳
固皆不朽之言矣槩諸六經何所祖述
乎世謂易微而易在楚詩亡而詩在楚
信斯議也宜莫如二家之言乃今挾策
而讀之則無當二者詩與易安在哉宋
玉景差爲騷羽翼其後移官長沙者賦
而悼之則皆受繩墨於騷矣可與三閭
===
絜廣狹乎二程伯仲受圖歸洛其後講
業嶽麓者猶多發明則皆受符節於圖
矣可與舂陵相後先乎夫引三后之純
粹揭聖人之立極其言弘廓深遠矣使
得志當世果能有所建述庶幾疇昔者
乎藉令絳灌之言不入黨錮之禁輟罷
二三君子所就業孰多邪諸士居其國
誦讀其詩書宜論其世矣豈曰方人爲
賢
punctuated:
奏之。

問：六籍而下，楚士以論著鳴者，吾得二人焉。昔稱或爲詞賦之祖，或得孔孟之傳，固皆不朽之言矣。槩諸六經，何所祖述乎？世謂易微而易在楚，詩亡而詩在楚。信斯議也，宜莫如二家之言。乃今挾策而讀之，則無當二者，詩與易安在哉？宋玉、景差爲騷羽翼，其後移官長沙者，賦而悼之，則皆受繩墨於騷矣，可與三閭絜廣狹乎？二程伯仲受圖歸洛，其後講業嶽麓者，猶多發明，則皆受符節於圖矣，可與舂陵相後先乎？夫引三后之純粹，揭聖人之立極，其言弘廓深遠矣。使得志當世，果能有所建述，庶幾疇昔者乎？藉令絳灌之言不入，黨錮之禁輟罷，二三君子所就業孰多邪？諸士居其國，誦讀其詩書，宜論其世矣。豈曰方人爲賢？
translation_en:
…submit it to the throne.

Question: Since the Six Classics, I find two men of Chu renowned for their writings. One has been called the progenitor of lyric poetry and rhapsodies, the other the recipient of the transmitted teachings of Confucius and Mencius. Their writings are certainly imperishable. Yet, measured against the Six Classics, what did they take as their models and carry forward? It is commonly said that when the Changes became obscure, the Changes survived in Chu, and when the Odes were lost, the Odes survived in Chu. If this judgment is sound, surely nothing should equal the writings of these two men. Yet when we now take up their texts and read them, they do not accord with either classic. Where, then, are the Odes and the Changes?

Song Yu and Jing Cha lent wings to the Encountering Sorrow (Li sao). Later, the man transferred to office in Changsha [Jia Yi] composed a rhapsody mourning its author. All thus took their standards from the Encountering Sorrow. Can their breadth and scope be measured against those of the Minister of the Three Clans [Qu Yuan]? The two Cheng brothers received the Diagram [of the Supreme Ultimate] and returned to Luo. Later, those who taught at Yuelu made many further elucidations. All thus derived their warrant from the Diagram. Can they vie for precedence with the master of Chongling [Zhou Dunyi]?

One invoked the unsullied virtue of the three sovereigns; the other expounded the sage’s establishment of the ultimate standard. Their words were expansive, profound, and far-reaching. Had they been able to realize their aspirations in their own age, could they truly have established institutions and transmitted teachings approaching those of antiquity? Suppose that the words of Jiang and Guan had not been heeded, and that the prohibitions against the proscribed faction had been lifted: which of these gentlemen would have accomplished more? You scholars live in their country and recite their poetry and writings; you should therefore consider the ages in which they lived. Surely this is not to say that judging other men makes one worthy?

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
問楚地踔遠三江七澤在焉大都利病水
利與江防是已夫稻人之職周以足民
樓舩之官漢以弭盜其籍固在可舉而
行之與後若芍陂開利漳水興謠引涇
而名鄭渠灌蜀而號陸海此皆興民利
者也渤海易俗交趾作歌到部而冀州
遂安懸鼓而兗州無警此皆捍民患者
也所至輒效其果遵何術哉
國家之制以營水利則郡縣分職監司董之
===
矣然潛沔之隄防猶或潰溢公安之利
患互爲乘除沙洋之績不終穴口之議
復沮是興利而利未滋也以飭江防則
吏士分部監司督之矣然沿江而下不
廢干掫舟楫所過猶多警備或乘徵調
而牟利或爲嚮導而召姦是捍患而患
未弭也察斯二者果無治人乎抑亦無
治法乎玆欲導地利以布民詰方慝以
屏惡將何施而可願爲有司決策焉
punctuated:
問：楚地踔遠，三江七澤在焉，大都利病，水利與江防是已。夫稻人之職，周以足民；樓舩之官，漢以弭盜。其籍固在，可舉而行之與？後若芍陂開利，漳水興謠，引涇而名鄭渠，灌蜀而號陸海，此皆興民利者也。渤海易俗，交趾作歌，到部而冀州遂安，懸鼓而兗州無警，此皆捍民患者也。所至輒效，其果遵何術哉？
國家之制，以營水利，則郡縣分職，監司董之矣。然潛沔之隄防猶或潰溢，公安之利患互爲乘除，沙洋之績不終，穴口之議復沮，是興利而利未滋也。以飭江防，則吏士分部，監司督之矣。然沿江而下，不廢干掫；舟楫所過，猶多警備。或乘徵調而牟利，或爲嚮導而召姦，是捍患而患未弭也。察斯二者，果無治人乎？抑亦無治法乎？玆欲導地利以布民，詰方慝以屏惡，將何施而可？願爲有司決策焉。
translation_en:
Question: The territory of Chu is vast and remote; within it lie the Three Rivers and Seven Marshes. Its benefits and troubles chiefly concern water management and river defense. Through the duties of officials responsible for rice fields, the Zhou ensured the people's sufficiency; through officers commanding tower ships, the Han suppressed banditry. Records of these institutions certainly survive: can they be taken up and put into practice? In later times, the Shaopi reservoir brought benefits, and works on the Zhang River inspired songs of praise. Diverting the Jing River produced what was called the Zheng Canal, while irrigating Shu earned it the name “a sea on land.” These all promoted the people's welfare. Customs were transformed in Bohai, and songs were composed in Jiaozhi; an official's arrival at his post brought peace to Jizhou, and the hanging of a drum left Yanzhou free of alarms. These all protected the people against calamities. Wherever these officials went, their measures proved effective. What methods did they actually follow?
Under our dynasty's institutions, responsibility for water management is divided among prefectures and counties, with the circuit intendants overseeing them. Yet the embankments of Qian and Mian still sometimes burst or overflow; at Gong'an, benefits and harms alternately offset one another; the achievements at Shayang were not carried through; and the proposal concerning Xuekou was again obstructed. Thus benefits are pursued, yet have not increased. To strengthen river defense, civil officials and soldiers are assigned separate sectors, with the circuit intendants supervising them. Yet patrols cannot be discontinued along the river downstream, and wherever boats pass, extensive precautions are still needed. Some exploit requisitions and mobilizations for profit; others act as guides and bring in malefactors. Thus calamities are resisted, yet have not been quelled. Considering these two matters, are there truly no capable administrators? Or are there no effective methods of administration? We now wish to develop the land's resources so as to settle the people, and to investigate local wrongdoing so as to eliminate evil. What measures would achieve this? Please determine a course of action for the responsible authorities.

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
舜有臣五人而天下治
陳述齡
同考試官教諭陳批揄揚而有典則即有
能言斯亦擅場矣
同考試官教諭吳批形容虞廷明良相遇
之盛讀之令人躍然
考試官教授蔣批爾雅深厚一字不苟
===
考試官教授桂批精緻
聖君得人之盛而天下化成焉蓋君得臣而萬
化行也大舜得人之盛如此其治化之隆也有
以哉記者之意若謂天之生才不偶而君臣之
相遇為難惟夫舜也以重華之德陟元后之位
紹堯致治太和丕著於人文應運而興羣賢咸
服於有位禹為司空棄為后稷凡其所翕受以
煕帝之載者皆名世之良弼焉契作司徒臯陶
作士而伯益作虞凡其所時舉以亮天之工者
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「舜有臣五人，而天下治。」
陳述齡

同考試官教諭陳批：「揄揚而有典則，即有能言，斯亦擅場矣。」
同考試官教諭吳批：「形容虞廷明良相遇之盛，讀之令人躍然。」
考試官教授蔣批：「爾雅深厚，一字不苟。」
考試官教授桂批：「精緻。」

聖君得人之盛，而天下化成焉。蓋君得臣而萬化行也。大舜得人之盛如此，其治化之隆也有以哉！記者之意若謂：天之生才不偶，而君臣之相遇為難。惟夫舜也，以重華之德，陟元后之位，紹堯致治，太和丕著於人文；應運而興，羣賢咸服於有位。禹為司空，棄為后稷，凡其所翕受以煕帝之載者，皆名世之良弼焉。契作司徒，臯陶作士，而伯益作虞，凡其所時舉以亮天之工者，
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“Shun had five ministers, and all under Heaven was well governed.”
Chen Shuling

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Its praise accords with established standards. Even among those skilled in expression, this would command the field.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “It portrays the flourishing court of Shun, where an enlightened sovereign and worthy ministers met. Reading it makes one leap with delight.”
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: “Refined and substantial; not a single word is carelessly chosen.”
Comment by Examiner Gui, Professor: “Exquisitely wrought.”

Through the abundance of worthy men secured by the sage ruler, all under Heaven was transformed and brought to perfection. For when a ruler obtains worthy ministers, every transforming influence takes effect. Such was the abundance of worthy men secured by the great Shun: surely there was good reason for the eminence of his governance and transforming influence!

The recorder’s meaning seems to be this: Heaven does not produce talented men by chance, yet it is difficult for ruler and ministers to encounter one another. Shun, possessing the virtue of Chonghua—“Renewed Splendor”—ascended to the position of supreme sovereign. Succeeding Yao, he brought about good government, and supreme harmony became grandly manifest in human culture. Rising in response to the destined time, the assembled worthies all served in official positions. Yu became Minister of Works, and Qi became Lord of Millet. All those whom Shun received together to advance the sovereign’s undertakings were excellent supporting ministers renowned in their age. Xie became Minister of Education, Gao Yao became Judge, and Bo Yi became Forester. All those whom he appointed at the proper time to assist in Heaven’s work …

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
皆盛時之黎獻焉以舜爲君使五人者爲臣是
不惟有君也而又有臣也不惟有臣也而又衆
多也天下欲無治焉得乎蓋舜統治於上則聖
人作而萬物覩五人者分治於下則賢才輔而
庶績凝股肱耳目各能其職而水土以平也民
人以育也野無遺賢玆萬邦之所以咸寧乎左
右贊襄各宣其力而百姓以親也五刑以明也
鳥獸草木以若也俊乂在官玆四方之所以風
動乎天爲舜而生才舜爲天下而得人知人以
===
安民此惟大舜之能事而有虞人才之盛可想
見矣抑聞之天不言而萬物亨歲功成者五行
之運宣其化矣舜猶天也五人者猶五行之順
布於四時也承君之德而宣之民者也舜與天
合德則其從欲以治者豈惟得人焉爾乎嗚呼
雖甚盛德蔑以加矣
及其至也察乎天地
張楚翹
同考試官教諭顧 批〔察天地處括盡章旨〕
punctuated:
皆盛時之黎獻焉。以舜爲君，使五人者爲臣，是不惟有君也，而又有臣也；不惟有臣也，而又衆多也。天下欲無治，焉得乎？蓋舜統治於上，則聖人作而萬物覩；五人者分治於下，則賢才輔而庶績凝。股肱耳目各能其職，而水土以平也，民人以育也。野無遺賢，玆萬邦之所以咸寧乎！左右贊襄各宣其力，而百姓以親也，五刑以明也，鳥獸草木以若也。俊乂在官，玆四方之所以風動乎！天爲舜而生才，舜爲天下而得人，知人以安民，此惟大舜之能事，而有虞人才之盛可想見矣。抑聞之，天不言而萬物亨、歲功成者，五行之運宣其化矣。舜猶天也，五人者猶五行之順布於四時也，承君之德而宣之民者也。舜與天合德，則其從欲以治者，豈惟得人焉爾乎？嗚呼！雖甚盛德，蔑以加矣！

及其至也，察乎天地。
張楚翹
同考試官教諭顧 批〔察天地處括盡章旨〕
translation_en:
…all were worthy men of that flourishing age. With Shun as ruler and these five men as ministers, there was not only a ruler but ministers as well; and there were not merely ministers, but many of them. How could the realm fail to be well governed? When Shun presided over government above, the sage arose and all things beheld him. When the five men shared the work of government below, worthy talents assisted him and every undertaking was firmly established. As his limbs, ears, and eyes, each fulfilled his office: the waters and lands were brought into order, and the people were nurtured. No worthy man remained overlooked in the countryside: was this not why the myriad states all enjoyed peace? His assistants on either side each devoted their strength to aiding him: the people were brought into harmony, the five punishments were clearly administered, and birds, beasts, plants, and trees were properly tended. Outstanding men held office: was this not why the four quarters responded as if stirred by the wind? Heaven produced talented men for Shun, and Shun obtained them for the sake of the realm. To recognize men’s abilities and thereby bring peace to the people—this was the particular achievement of the great Shun. We can thus envision the abundance of talent under the lord of Yu.

I have also heard that Heaven does not speak, yet all things flourish and the year’s work is accomplished because the movements of the Five Phases disseminate its transforming power. Shun was like Heaven, and these five men were like the Five Phases, which unfold harmoniously through the four seasons: they received their ruler’s virtue and spread it among the people. Since Shun’s virtue accorded with Heaven, could his ability to govern as he wished have depended solely on obtaining the right men? Ah! Even the most abundant virtue could not surpass this!

“When it reaches its utmost, it is manifest in Heaven and Earth.”
Zhang Chuqiao
Associate Examiner Gu, Instructor, comments: 〔The passage on being manifest in Heaven and Earth encompasses the meaning of the entire chapter.〕…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
類以浮詞失之此作良是
同考試官學正余批體認旣明詞復純正
可以爲文矣
考試官敎授蔣批馴雅可誦
考試官敎授桂批有理致
中庸舉斯道之全體而通極於天地焉夫法象
莫大於天地也而斯道之全體有以通極之不
其費矣乎中庸論費隱而結之以此若曰道之
在天下也始於近不禦於遠君子之於道也析
===
其精必合其全故語道而始於夫婦者特就其
造端言之耳而非其全體也若推類以究其極
則徵之聖人而聖人無全能質之天地而天地
有遺憾小大莫不無該而上下相爲昭格是不
亦察於天地乎故仰觀於天凡高明所覆而在
天成象者皆斯道之峻極也俯察於地凡博厚
所載而在地成形者皆斯道之蟠委也以兩而
化則乾以大生坤以廣生其竝行而不悖者孰
非太極之各足邪以一而神則天道下濟地道
punctuated:
類以浮詞失之，此作良是。

同考試官學正余批：體認旣明，詞復純正，可以爲文矣。

考試官敎授蔣批：馴雅可誦。

考試官敎授桂批：有理致。

中庸舉斯道之全體而通極於天地焉。夫法象莫大於天地也，而斯道之全體有以通極之，不其費矣乎？中庸論費隱而結之以此，若曰：道之在天下也，始於近，不禦於遠；君子之於道也，析其精，必合其全。故語道而始於夫婦者，特就其造端言之耳，而非其全體也。若推類以究其極，則徵之聖人，而聖人無全能；質之天地，而天地有遺憾。小大莫不無該，而上下相爲昭格，是不亦察於天地乎？故仰觀於天，凡高明所覆而在天成象者，皆斯道之峻極也；俯察於地，凡博厚所載而在地成形者，皆斯道之蟠委也。以兩而化，則乾以大生，坤以廣生，其竝行而不悖者，孰非太極之各足邪？以一而神，則天道下濟，地道
translation_en:
…Such writings commonly go astray through empty phrasing; this composition is indeed sound.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, School Instructor: “The apprehension is clear, and the language is also pure and correct. This qualifies as accomplished writing.”

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Prefectural School Professor: “Refined and elegant, well worth reciting.”

Comment by Examiner Gui, Prefectural School Professor: “It has depth of principle.”

The Doctrine of the Mean presents this Way in its entirety, extending to the utmost reaches of Heaven and Earth. Now, among models and images, none is greater than Heaven and Earth; yet the entirety of this Way extends throughout them to their utmost limits. Is its scope not vast? The Doctrine of the Mean discusses the Way’s vastness and hiddenness and concludes with this statement. It is as though it said: the Way in the world begins with what is near, yet is not confined when it reaches what is distant. In approaching the Way, the gentleman analyzes its subtleties but must also comprehend its entirety. Thus, when speaking of the Way, to begin with husband and wife is merely to speak of its starting point, not its entirety. If one extends the analogies to investigate its utmost reach, then, tested against the sages, there are things even the sages cannot fully accomplish; measured against Heaven and Earth, there remain deficiencies even in Heaven and Earth. Nothing small or great lies outside its compass [?], and above and below mutually manifest its presence. Is this not its being manifest throughout Heaven and Earth?

Thus, when we look upward to Heaven, all that its lofty brightness covers and all that takes on celestial configuration are this Way reaching its sublime height. When we look downward to Earth, all that its breadth and thickness bear and all that takes shape upon Earth are this Way spreading and winding through things. Through duality it brings about transformation: Qian, the Creative, generates through greatness, and Kun, the Receptive, generates through breadth. As they proceed together without conflict, how could either fail to possess the Supreme Ultimate in its fullness? Through unity it works wondrously: the Way of Heaven descends to aid, and the Way of Earth…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
上行其相得而有合者孰非帝則之必察邪是
知道始於夫婦而不止於夫婦也察於天地而
不盡於天地也其用甚廣而其體則微大哉道
乎斯其至矣君子察於此於是乎有體道之功
焉蓋道也者通於天地而實本於吾心者也夫
婦吾心之彝倫也鳶魚吾心之物理也天地聖
人吾心之統會也知道具於一心而動靜交相
爲力則中和致而天地以位萬物以育裁成輔
相舉得之矣是故君子不求諸天地而求諸吾
===
心
心之所同然者何也謂理也義也聖人先
得我心之所同然耳故理義之悅我心
猶芻豢之悅我口
李鳴
同考試官教諭譚 批詞不繁而意已盡深得性善之
言者
同考試官教諭鍾 批構思精密且無一贅詞宜錄以
式
punctuated:
上行，其相得而有合者，孰非帝則之必察邪？是知道始於夫婦而不止於夫婦也，察於天地而不盡於天地也。其用甚廣，而其體則微。大哉道乎！斯其至矣。君子察於此，於是乎有體道之功焉。蓋道也者，通於天地而實本於吾心者也。夫婦，吾心之彝倫也；鳶魚，吾心之物理也；天地聖人，吾心之統會也。知道具於一心，而動靜交相爲力，則中和致，而天地以位，萬物以育，裁成輔相舉得之矣。是故君子不求諸天地，而求諸吾心。
「心之所同然者何也？謂理也，義也。聖人先得我心之所同然耳。故理義之悅我心，猶芻豢之悅我口。」
李鳴
同考試官教諭譚 批：詞不繁而意已盡，深得性善之言者。
同考試官教諭鍾 批：構思精密，且無一贅詞，宜錄以式。
translation_en:
…ascends. In their mutual accord and union, how could the Sovereign’s norm fail to be manifest? Thus we know that the Way begins with husband and wife but does not stop with husband and wife; it is manifest in Heaven and Earth but is not exhausted by Heaven and Earth. Its operation is exceedingly broad, while its substance is subtle. Great indeed is the Way! Here it reaches its utmost. The gentleman discerns this and thereby undertakes the work of embodying the Way. For the Way pervades Heaven and Earth, yet is truly rooted in my own heart. Husband and wife represent the enduring human relationships within my heart; the kite and the fish represent the principles of things within my heart; Heaven, Earth, and the sages are comprehensively united within my heart. Knowing that the Way is fully present in the single heart, and making activity and stillness mutually sustaining, one brings equilibrium and harmony to their fullest realization: Heaven and Earth take their proper places, and the myriad things are nurtured. The work of regulating and completing their transformations, and assisting their workings, is thereby fully accomplished. Thus the gentleman seeks it not in Heaven and Earth, but in his own heart.
“What is it that hearts alike approve? It is principle and righteousness. The sages have simply apprehended before us what our hearts alike approve. Thus principle and righteousness delight my heart just as the meat of grass-fed and grain-fed animals delights my palate.”
Li Ming
Associate Examiner Tan, Instructor, comments: “The wording is concise, yet the meaning is fully expressed. This is someone who has deeply grasped the teaching that human nature is good.”
Associate Examiner Zhong, Instructor, comments: “The conception is meticulous, and there is not a single superfluous phrase. It should be recorded as a model.”

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授蔣批切當
考試官教授桂批簡而文
大賢深著人心好德之同以見性之善也盖理
義之心人皆有之也卽其好德之同情而可以
識心矣且夫道原於性性統於心心也者妙衆
體而爲言者也惟口耳目尚有同者何獨至於
心而疑之心之所同然者何也理義之謂也夫
理寓於物者也而吾心之體具焉所以立天下
之有也夫義裁夫事者也而吾心之用行焉所
===
以效天下之動也斯二者皆降衷之恒性雖聖
人與人同也其知覺超乎庶類若非夫人之可
幾及而理義出於一原亦不過先得我心之所
同然者耳聖人何以異於人哉唯其取諸心而
至足故自悅諸心而無間心不與理義期而理
義自不能不契於吾心盖有天機存焉不知理
義之美者無良心者也猶之口不與芻豢期而
芻豢自不能不嗜於吾口盖有至味存焉不知
芻豢之美者不知味者也人同則心同心同則
punctuated:
考試官教授蔣批：切當。
考試官教授桂批：簡而文。
大賢深著人心好德之同，以見性之善也。盖理義之心，人皆有之也。卽其好德之同情，而可以識心矣。且夫道原於性，性統於心。心也者，妙衆體而爲言者也。惟口耳目尚有同者，何獨至於心而疑之？心之所同然者何也？理義之謂也。夫理，寓於物者也，而吾心之體具焉，所以立天下之有也。夫義，裁夫事者也，而吾心之用行焉，所以效天下之動也。斯二者，皆降衷之恒性，雖聖人，與人同也。其知覺超乎庶類，若非夫人之可幾及，而理義出於一原，亦不過先得我心之所同然者耳。聖人何以異於人哉？唯其取諸心而至足，故自悅諸心而無間。心不與理義期，而理義自不能不契於吾心，盖有天機存焉。不知理義之美者，無良心者也。猶之口不與芻豢期，而芻豢自不能不嗜於吾口，盖有至味存焉。不知芻豢之美者，不知味者也。人同則心同，心同則
translation_en:
Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “Apt and sound.”
Examiner Gui, Instructor, comments: “Concise and polished.”
The great worthy clearly reveals that human hearts share a love of virtue, thereby demonstrating the goodness of human nature. For everyone possesses a heart endowed with moral principle and righteousness. Through this shared disposition to love virtue, we can understand the heart. The Way originates in human nature, and human nature is governed by the heart. The term “heart” refers to that which wondrously integrates the body's various faculties. Even the mouth, ears, and eyes have something in common across all people; why should we doubt this only when it comes to the heart? What is it that all hearts alike approve? Moral principle and righteousness. Principle inheres in things, and the heart's essential constitution possesses it in full; through it, all that exists under Heaven is established. Righteousness determines what is fitting in affairs, and the heart's activity operates through it; through it, all movement under Heaven finds expression. These two constitute the constant nature bestowed by Heaven: even the sage shares them with everyone else. His understanding surpasses that of ordinary people, seemingly beyond their reach; yet principle and righteousness arise from a single source. He has merely apprehended first what our hearts alike approve. How, then, does the sage differ from other people? Only because he draws upon his heart and finds complete sufficiency does he take uninterrupted delight within it. The heart makes no prior arrangement with principle and righteousness, yet they cannot but accord with our hearts, for an innate operation of Heaven resides within. Those who do not recognize the beauty of principle and righteousness lack their original good heart. Likewise, the mouth makes no prior arrangement with the meat of grass-fed and grain-fed animals, yet our mouths cannot but relish it, for it possesses the finest flavor. Those who do not recognize the excellence of such meat do not understand flavor. Since people are alike, their hearts are alike; since their hearts are alike, then…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
悅同觀其所悅而心之所同然者明矣不然則
是心也何以能達之天下哉吁彼有陷溺其心
而顧於降才之殊是尤焉亦弗思耳矣雖然芻
豢者物也外也理義者管於心者也内也非外
也人有芻豢則知求之有理義而不知求此陷
溺之所由來也反而求之則窮理盡性精義入
神所以作聖者胥此矣人莫不飲食也鮮能知
味也知性者當自得之
易
===
元吉在上大有慶也
李畿嗣
同考試官教諭顧 批履至上九乃履道之成
天人感應之妙也是作闡揚其義無餘蘊矣錄之
同考試官學正余 批不襲陳言而詞理俱
足自中矩矱佳士佳士
考試官教授蔣 批講大有慶處得旨
考試官教授桂 批明暢
象傳舉履爻大善之極而深著其得天之佑也
punctuated:
悅同。觀其所悅，而心之所同然者明矣。不然，則是心也，何以能達之天下哉？吁！彼有陷溺其心，而顧於降才之殊是尤焉，亦弗思耳矣。雖然，芻豢者，物也，外也；理義者，管於心者也，内也，非外也。人有芻豢則知求之，有理義而不知求，此陷溺之所由來也。反而求之，則窮理盡性，精義入神，所以作聖者胥此矣。人莫不飲食也，鮮能知味也。知性者當自得之。

易

元吉在上，大有慶也。

李畿嗣

同考試官教諭顧批：履至上九，乃履道之成、天人感應之妙也。是作闡揚其義，無餘蘊矣。錄之。

同考試官學正余批：不襲陳言，而詞理俱足，自中矩矱。佳士！佳士！

考試官教授蔣批：講大有慶處得旨。

考試官教授桂批：明暢。

象傳舉履爻大善之極，而深著其得天之佑也。
translation_en:
…their delights are the same. Observe what delights them, and what their hearts alike approve becomes clear. Otherwise, how could this heart be shared throughout the world? Alas! There are those who let their hearts sink into degradation, yet instead blame differences in their Heaven-bestowed capacities [?]. They simply fail to reflect. Nevertheless, meat from grass-fed and grain-fed animals is a material thing, something external; moral principle and rightness belong within the heart: they are internal, not external. People know to seek such meat, yet do not know to seek the moral principle and rightness they possess. This is how their degradation comes about. If they turn back and seek within themselves, they can investigate principle fully, fulfill their nature, refine their understanding of rightness, and enter the realm of the spiritual. All that makes one a sage lies here. Everyone eats and drinks, but few can discern flavor. Those who understand human nature should grasp this for themselves.

Book of Changes

“Supreme good fortune in the topmost position: there is great cause for rejoicing.”

Li Jisi

Comment by Associate Examiner Gu, Instructor: “When the hexagram Treading (Lü) reaches its topmost nine, the way of treading attains completion: here is the subtle working of the mutual response between Heaven and humanity. This composition expounds that meaning, leaving nothing unexplored. Include it.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor: “Without borrowing conventional expressions, it is fully accomplished in both language and reasoning, and naturally meets the standards. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!”

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: “The discussion of ‘great cause for rejoicing’ captures the purport.”

Comment by Examiner Gui, Professor: “Clear and fluent.”

The Commentary on the Images points to the utmost perfection of goodness in the line of Treading and makes profoundly clear its receipt of Heaven’s aid.

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
蓋履道之成天人感應之機係之也上九旣會
大善之極矣則天之佑也豈其微哉象傳之意
蓋謂履之爲道也本諸已以大善爲極功徵諸
天以大順爲極致此視履之所期以自遂而不
可必得者玆惟爻至上九履已成矣履至其旋
善已極矣合衆善以成其行而德崇業廣之下
自足以上格乎天心聚百順以成其身而體信
達順之餘自可以永綏乎天命故始而曰吉可
以顯惠迪之應矣而尤益之元吉以申其命繼
===
而曰元吉可以彰大善之徵矣而尤要之在上
以昭其極則其慶之大爲何如哉蓋惟天顯道
而吾考道以爲無失則天命之寵綏者自獲乎
多福之懷惟天眷德而吾聚德以爲不回則上
帝之賚予者將出於望外之益保佑命之可以
言慶矣而又自天申之則嘉樂之休所以凝其
命於無疆者何其久而大也福履綏之可以言
慶矣而又勿替引之則申錫之祚所以貽其福
於無窮者何其遠而大也履而至是則吾之昭
punctuated: 蓋履道之成，天人感應之機係之也。上九旣會大善之極矣，則天之佑也，豈其微哉？象傳之意，蓋謂履之爲道也，本諸已，以大善爲極功；徵諸天，以大順爲極致。此視履之所期以自遂，而不可必得者。玆惟爻至上九，履已成矣；履至其旋，善已極矣。合衆善以成其行，而德崇業廣之下，自足以上格乎天心；聚百順以成其身，而體信達順之餘，自可以永綏乎天命。故始而曰吉，可以顯惠迪之應矣，而尤益之元吉，以申其命；繼而曰元吉，可以彰大善之徵矣，而尤要之在上，以昭其極。則其慶之大爲何如哉？蓋惟天顯道，而吾考道以爲無失，則天命之寵綏者，自獲乎多福之懷；惟天眷德，而吾聚德以爲不回，則上帝之賚予者，將出於望外之益。保佑命之，可以言慶矣，而又自天申之，則嘉樂之休，所以凝其命於無疆者，何其久而大也！福履綏之，可以言慶矣，而又勿替引之，則申錫之祚，所以貽其福於無窮者，何其遠而大也！履而至是，則吾之昭
translation_en:
…For upon the completion of the Way of Treading hinges the responsive interaction between Heaven and humanity. Since the topmost nine has already brought together goodness in its highest perfection, how could Heaven’s aid be slight? The meaning of the Commentary on the Images is that the Way of Treading, grounded in oneself, takes consummate goodness as its highest achievement; verified in Heaven, it takes consummate accord as its ultimate attainment. These are what examining one’s treading looks toward for its fulfillment, yet they cannot be secured with certainty. Now, however, when the line reaches the topmost nine, treading is complete; when treading comes full circle, goodness has reached its utmost. By combining all forms of goodness to perfect one’s conduct, one’s exalted virtue and extensive accomplishments naturally suffice to reach Heaven’s heart above. By gathering every form of accord to perfect oneself, through embodying trustworthiness and attaining accord one may naturally enjoy the enduring favor of Heaven’s Mandate. Thus, when it first says “auspicious,” this reveals the response to following the right way; yet it further adds “supremely auspicious” to reaffirm its pronouncement. Next, when it says “supremely auspicious,” this manifests the evidence of consummate goodness; yet it particularly locates this “at the top” to make clear its culmination. How great, then, must its blessings be!

Heaven makes the Way manifest, and if I examine the Way so as to be without error, then, favored and sustained by Heaven’s Mandate, I naturally receive abundant blessings. Heaven cherishes virtue, and if I accumulate virtue without deviation, then the gifts of the Lord on High will bring benefits beyond my expectations. To be “protected, aided, and charged with the Mandate” may already be called a blessing; when this is further “reaffirmed from Heaven,” how enduring and great is the favor celebrated in “Admirable Joy” (Jia le), which secures that Mandate without limit! To be “settled in blessed fortune” may already be called a blessing; when this is further “continued without lapse,” how far-reaching and great is the good fortune repeatedly bestowed, which transmits blessings without end! When treading has reached this point, then my manifest…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授桂批精確
大傳原易有以闡乎性命因詳言以明之也夫
性命之理三才備矣卦爻卽三才之道也謂易
非性命之奧乎夫子翼易之意蓋以易雖陳乎
法象之粗而義實該夫至理之奧昔者聖人之
作易非曰意爲之也亦惟融性命於擬議之精
而發幽微於形器之顯立象盡意本順乎斯理
焉而已何者自天道之所以成象曰陰與陽而
靜專動直焉地道之所以成質曰柔與剛而靜
===
翕動闢焉人道之所以成德曰仁與義而慈愛
斷制焉斯固性命之分見於三才者也而何以
順之蓋聖人以三才皆以兩而成體而三畫不
足以備其體也於是兼三才而兩之貞悔全而
大小合故易六畫而成卦矣吾見五上以兩而
陰陽分也三四以兩而仁義明也初二以兩而
剛柔配也不亦統之而得性命之全乎又以三
才每相錯以爲用而定畫不足以盡其用也於
是分陰分陽迭用柔剛爻有等而物相雜故易
punctuated:
考試官教授桂批：「精確。」

大傳原易有以闡乎性命，因詳言以明之也。夫性命之理，三才備矣；卦爻卽三才之道也，謂易非性命之奧乎？夫子翼易之意，蓋以易雖陳乎法象之粗，而義實該夫至理之奧。昔者聖人之作易，非曰意爲之也，亦惟融性命於擬議之精，而發幽微於形器之顯，立象盡意，本順乎斯理焉而已。何者？自天道之所以成象，曰陰與陽，而靜專動直焉；地道之所以成質，曰柔與剛，而靜翕動闢焉；人道之所以成德，曰仁與義，而慈愛斷制焉。斯固性命之分見於三才者也，而何以順之？蓋聖人以三才皆以兩而成體，而三畫不足以備其體也，於是兼三才而兩之，貞悔全而大小合，故易六畫而成卦矣。吾見五上以兩而陰陽分也，三四以兩而仁義明也，初二以兩而剛柔配也，不亦統之而得性命之全乎？又以三才每相錯以爲用，而定畫不足以盡其用也，於是分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，爻有等而物相雜，故易
translation_en:
Examiner Gui, an instructor, comments: “Precise and accurate.”

The Great Commentary investigates the origins of the Book of Changes as a means of elucidating human nature and destiny, and therefore explains them in detail to make them clear. The principles of nature and destiny are fully embodied in the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity. The hexagrams and their lines are precisely the Way of these Three Powers. Could one say that the Changes does not contain the profound mysteries of nature and destiny? The Master's intention in furnishing the Changes with its Wings was surely this: although the Changes sets forth the outward forms of patterns and images, its meaning actually encompasses the profundities of ultimate principle. When the sages of old composed the Changes, they did not simply devise it at will. Rather, they integrated nature and destiny into the subtleties of comparison and deliberation, and revealed what is hidden and subtle through manifest forms and concrete things. In establishing images to express their meaning fully, they did no more than follow this underlying principle.

How is this so? That by which the Way of Heaven produces images is called yin and yang: in stillness it is concentrated, and in movement it is direct. That by which the Way of Earth produces material substance is called the yielding and the firm: in stillness it closes, and in movement it opens. That by which the human Way produces virtue is called benevolence and righteousness: it expresses itself in compassionate love and decisive judgment. These are indeed the separate manifestations of nature and destiny in the Three Powers. But how does one accord with them?

The sages considered that each of the Three Powers takes form through a pair, and that three lines were insufficient to embody their forms completely. Accordingly, they combined the Three Powers and doubled them. The lower and upper trigrams were complete, and the small and the great united; thus, in the Changes, six lines form a hexagram. I observe that the fifth and top lines constitute a pair through which yin and yang are distinguished; the third and fourth constitute a pair through which benevolence and righteousness are made clear; and the first and second constitute a pair through which the firm and the yielding are matched. Does this not bring them together and thereby encompass nature and destiny in their entirety?

They further considered that the Three Powers operate through their continual intermingling, and that fixed lines were insufficient to exhaust their operations. Accordingly, they distinguished yin and yang and employed the yielding and the firm alternately. The lines have their ranks, and things intermingle; thus, in the Changes …

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
六位而成章矣吾見五陽上陰而動靜交也三
仁四義而慈斷行也初剛二柔而翕闢時也不
亦拆之而盡性命之變乎是則非性命無以立
三才非易書無以順性命易其至矣乎夫是義
也得之河圖焉五位之合卽三才之兩也而其
相得卽剛柔之迭用也一而已矣然圖從中起
而三才之所以各一太極太極之所以流行於
三才不外是焉噫性命之原淵乎微矣
書
===
惟動丕應徯志以昭受上帝天其申命用
休
李鳴
同考試官敎諭譚 批講得天得民處詞莊
意切真得古人告君之體
同考試官敎諭鍾 批詞意渾融子蓋善發
天人之蘊者
考試官敎授蔣 批思致精密
考試官敎授桂 批雋永可玩
punctuated:
六位而成章矣。吾見五陽上陰而動靜交也，三仁四義而慈斷行也，初剛二柔而翕闢時也。不亦拆之而盡性命之變乎？是則非性命無以立三才，非易書無以順性命，易其至矣乎！夫是義也，得之河圖焉。五位之合，卽三才之兩也；而其相得，卽剛柔之迭用也。一而已矣。然圖從中起，而三才之所以各一太極，太極之所以流行於三才，不外是焉。噫！性命之原，淵乎微矣！

書

惟動丕應，徯志以昭受上帝，天其申命用休。

李鳴

同考試官敎諭譚 批：講得天得民處，詞莊意切，真得古人告君之體。

同考試官敎諭鍾 批：詞意渾融，子蓋善發天人之蘊者。

考試官敎授蔣 批：思致精密。

考試官敎授桂 批：雋永可玩。
translation_en:
…the six positions thus form an ordered pattern. I see yang in the fifth position and yin in the topmost, so that activity and stillness interact; benevolence in the third and righteousness in the fourth, so that compassion and decisiveness are exercised; firmness in the first and yielding in the second, so that closing and opening occur at the proper times. Is this not to distinguish them and thereby encompass all the transformations of nature and destiny? Thus, without nature and destiny there would be no means of establishing the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—and without the Book of Changes there would be no means of following nature and destiny. How consummate the Changes is! This principle can be apprehended in the River Chart. The conjunction of the five positions is precisely the pairing within each of the Three Powers; their mutual accord is precisely the alternating operation of firmness and yielding. These are one and the same. Yet the chart begins at its center: the reason each of the Three Powers embodies a Supreme Ultimate, and the reason the Supreme Ultimate circulates through the Three Powers, lie nowhere beyond this. Ah! How profound and subtle is the source of nature and destiny!

Book of Documents

“Whenever you act, they respond fully, awaiting your intentions; thereby you manifestly receive the favor of the Lord on High. Heaven will renew its mandate to you with blessings.”

Li Ming

Associate Examiner Tan, Instructor, comments: “In discussing how to win Heaven’s favor and the people’s allegiance, the language is dignified and the meaning earnest. This truly captures the manner in which the ancients addressed their rulers.”

Associate Examiner Zhong, Instructor, comments: “Language and meaning blend into a seamless whole. You are indeed skilled at bringing out the profound implications of Heaven and humanity.”

Examiner Jiang, Professor, comments: “The thought and conception are subtle and precise.”

Examiner Gui, Professor, comments: “Rich in lasting significance and worthy of contemplation.”

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
大臣告聖君欲其得民而得天也蓋君德與天
人相為感通者也夫旣愼厥位矣而得民得天
豈非理之所必至哉大禹陳謨于舜而推言至
此意蓋曰人君成位于中上承天命而下係民
情者也夫苟內外交脩之至則其所感召者為
何如邪彼民罔常懷而丕從厥志者其情也今
惟出其愼脩者而著于動作之間則導之者為
盡善應之者為盡神動之而言也民莫不承聽
焉先意以迎之有不令而從者矣動之而行也
===
民莫不承順焉傾心以嚮之有不戒而孚者矣
是何也人之所助者信也君能信以發志而民
之順以從君也有不出于必然者乎天無常親
而惟德是與者其道也今惟本其愼脩者以凝
乎至顯之命則受之者非妄圖佑之者非私與
荷天之寵固陟此元后矣而保定之休自是垂
之於勿替焉享天之祜固奄有四海矣而純嘏
之錫自是申之於無疆焉是何也天之所助者
順也君能順以承天而天之眷命用懋也有不
punctuated: 大臣告聖君，欲其得民而得天也。蓋君德與天人相為感通者也。夫旣愼厥位矣，而得民得天，豈非理之所必至哉？大禹陳謨于舜，而推言至此，意蓋曰：人君成位于中，上承天命而下係民情者也。夫苟內外交脩之至，則其所感召者為何如邪？彼民罔常懷，而丕從厥志者，其情也。今惟出其愼脩者而著于動作之間，則導之者為盡善，應之者為盡神。動之而言也，民莫不承聽焉，先意以迎之，有不令而從者矣；動之而行也，民莫不承順焉，傾心以嚮之，有不戒而孚者矣。是何也？人之所助者信也。君能信以發志，而民之順以從君也，有不出于必然者乎？天無常親，而惟德是與者，其道也。今惟本其愼脩者以凝乎至顯之命，則受之者非妄圖，佑之者非私與。荷天之寵，固陟此元后矣，而保定之休，自是垂之於勿替焉；享天之祜，固奄有四海矣，而純嘏之錫，自是申之於無疆焉。是何也？天之所助者順也。君能順以承天，而天之眷命用懋也，有不
translation_en:
A great minister admonishes a sage ruler, wishing him to win the people and thereby win Heaven. For the ruler’s virtue, Heaven, and the people move and respond to one another. Once he has exercised care in his position, is winning the people and Heaven not the inevitable outcome of principle? When the Great Yu presented his counsels to Shun and extended his argument to this point, his meaning was surely this: the ruler occupies the central position, receiving Heaven’s mandate above and engaging the people’s sentiments below. If he perfects his cultivation both inwardly and outwardly, what responses will he call forth?

The people cherish no one constantly, yet greatly follow the ruler’s aspirations: such is their disposition. If he now brings forth the fruits of his careful cultivation and manifests them in his activities, his guidance will be wholly good, and their response wondrously complete. When he acts through speech, none among the people fails to listen attentively; anticipating his intentions, they meet them, obeying without being commanded. When he acts through deeds, none among the people fails to comply; turning wholeheartedly toward him, they trust him without being admonished. Why is this? Those whom people assist are the trustworthy. If the ruler expresses his aspirations with sincerity, can the people’s willing obedience to him be anything but inevitable?

Heaven has no constant favorite, but supports virtue alone: such is its Way. If he now takes his careful cultivation as the foundation for securing Heaven’s most manifest mandate, then the recipient does not seek it presumptuously, nor does the power that protects him bestow its favor out of partiality. Bearing Heaven’s favor, he has indeed ascended to the position of supreme sovereign; henceforth the blessing of protection and stability will descend upon him without cease. Enjoying Heaven’s blessing, he has indeed come to possess all within the Four Seas; henceforth the bestowal of great good fortune will be renewed without limit. Why is this? Those whom Heaven assists are the compliant. If the ruler complies in serving Heaven, and Heaven’s gracious mandate thereby grows more abundant, can this fail to …

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
出于必然者乎吁下而得民則君位以民心之
歸而益安上而得天則君位以天命之隆而益
固向非交修之力其何以致是哉抑聞之位在
德元則慎位者君之道當然耳乃禹猶推及于
天與人歸之盛豈亦取必于未然者乎蓋觀天
者觀之民觀民者觀我生者也天也人也己也
一理也感應一機也舜以玄德升聞而天下謳
歌朝覲訟獄者無不歸焉其得天民蓋固有之
也而禹實要其至焉耳豈徒托諸空言已邪以
===
是知天人相與之際古聖人所為兢業而弗懈
者蓋深有見于是理矣
一曰食二曰貨三曰祀四曰司空五曰司
徒六曰司寇七曰賓八曰師
陳文燭
同考試官教諭譚批敘次有法詞氣渾成
非徒經生組繪之談而已錄之
同考試官教諭鍾批因天厚民之意發揮
殆盡誠非苟作者
punctuated:
出于必然者乎？吁！下而得民，則君位以民心之歸而益安；上而得天，則君位以天命之隆而益固。向非交修之力，其何以致是哉？抑聞之，位在德元，則慎位者，君之道當然耳。乃禹猶推及于天與人歸之盛，豈亦取必于未然者乎？蓋觀天者觀之民，觀民者觀我生者也。天也，人也，己也，一理也；感應，一機也。舜以玄德升聞，而天下謳歌、朝覲、訟獄者無不歸焉。其得天民，蓋固有之也，而禹實要其至焉耳。豈徒托諸空言已邪？以是知天人相與之際，古聖人所為兢業而弗懈者，蓋深有見于是理矣。
一曰食，二曰貨，三曰祀，四曰司空，五曰司徒，六曰司寇，七曰賓，八曰師。
陳文燭
同考試官教諭譚批：敘次有法，詞氣渾成，非徒經生組繪之談而已，錄之。
同考試官教諭鍾批：因天厚民之意，發揮殆盡，誠非苟作者。
translation_en:
…could this fail to follow inevitably? Ah! By gaining the people below, the ruler’s position becomes more secure through the allegiance of their hearts; by gaining Heaven above, his position becomes firmer through the grandeur of Heaven’s mandate. Without the work of cultivating both, how could this have been achieved? Yet I have heard that the throne belongs to the foremost in virtue: taking care over his position is therefore simply what the ruler’s Way requires. Nevertheless, Yu went on to speak of the fullness of Heaven’s support and the people’s allegiance. Was he, too, asserting certainty about what had yet to happen? Those who observe Heaven look to the people; those who observe the people examine their own conduct. Heaven, the people, and oneself share a single principle; stimulus and response operate through a single mechanism. Shun’s profound virtue became known on high, and all throughout the realm who sang praises, attended court, or pursued lawsuits turned to him. He already possessed the favor of Heaven and the people; Yu was truly calling for its fullest realization. How could these have been merely empty words? From this we know that, in the interaction between Heaven and humankind, the ancient sages remained vigilant and never slackened because they had profound insight into this principle.
“First, food; second, goods; third, sacrifices; fourth, the Minister of Works; fifth, the Minister of Education; sixth, the Minister of Justice; seventh, guests; eighth, the army.”
Chen Wenzhu
Comment by Associate Examiner Tan, Instructor: “The sequence is methodical, and the language and tenor form a seamless whole. This is more than the ornamental discourse of a mere student of the Classics. Selected for inclusion.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhong, Instructor: “The meaning of following Heaven to enrich the people’s livelihood is expounded almost exhaustively. This is certainly no carelessly composed work.”

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授蔣批詞理俱優
考試官敎授桂批語有興要
君子列八政之目以緩急而爲敘焉夫八政皆
所以厚民而其敘有緩急也知所先後斯可以
言治乎箕子陳洪範之疇而衍及于此意謂邦
本係乎民民生貴于厚所謂農用八政者其目
維何食所以養生饑斯困矣則播時百穀以遂
其樂利之天者無不足也貨所以利用壅斯匱
矣則阜通五材以裕其貿遷之化者罔弗周也
===
===
是故食居一而貨即次焉祀典不備何以敎敬
于是乎制三禮而禋五祀焉示天下萃渙之義
也司空不建何以奠居于是乎居四民而時地
利焉貽天下幹止之寧也是故祀居三而司空
又次焉由是而性有未復則利用敎乃立司徒
以掌敎焉敷典和則式訓于旣富之餘矣由是
而敎有或違則利用刑乃立司寇以掌刑焉明
罰勅法允防其姦暴之過矣玆二政者不居于
五與六乎禮不可廢而有交焉則立之賓晉接
punctuated:
考試官敎授蔣批：詞理俱優。
考試官敎授桂批：語有興要。
君子列八政之目，以緩急而爲敘焉。夫八政皆所以厚民，而其敘有緩急也。知所先後，斯可以言治乎！箕子陳洪範之疇，而衍及于此，意謂邦本係乎民，民生貴于厚。所謂農用八政者，其目維何？食所以養生，饑斯困矣，則播時百穀，以遂其樂利之天者，無不足也。貨所以利用，壅斯匱矣，則阜通五材，以裕其貿遷之化者，罔弗周也。是故食居一，而貨即次焉。祀典不備，何以敎敬？于是乎制三禮而禋五祀焉，示天下萃渙之義也。司空不建，何以奠居？于是乎居四民而時地利焉，貽天下幹止之寧也。是故祀居三，而司空又次焉。由是而性有未復，則利用敎，乃立司徒以掌敎焉，敷典和則，式訓于旣富之餘矣。由是而敎有或違，則利用刑，乃立司寇以掌刑焉，明罰勅法，允防其姦暴之過矣。玆二政者，不居于五與六乎？禮不可廢，而有交焉，則立之賓，晉接
translation_en:
Examiner Jiang, an instructor, comments: “Both expression and reasoning are excellent.”
Examiner Gui, an instructor, comments: “The wording has evocative force and concision [?].”
The gentleman lists the eight branches of government in order of their relative urgency. All eight serve to enrich the people's livelihood, yet their sequence distinguishes the more urgent from the less urgent. Only when one understands what comes first and what follows can one speak of governing! When Jizi set forth the categories of the Great Plan and elaborated upon this subject, his meaning was that the foundation of the state rests upon the people, and that what matters in their livelihood is abundance. What, then, are the items in what is called “diligently employing the eight branches of government”? Food sustains life: hunger brings distress. Thus, sowing the various grains so as to fulfill people's Heaven-given capacity for happiness and well-being leaves nothing lacking. Goods provide things for use: obstructed circulation brings scarcity. Thus, increasing and circulating the five materials so as to enrich the workings of trade and exchange leaves nothing unprovided for. For this reason, food occupies first place, and goods come next.
If the sacrificial institutions are incomplete, how can reverence be taught? Accordingly, the three rites are established and pure offerings made at the five sacrifices, showing all under Heaven the meaning of gathering together and dispersing. If the office of Minister of Works is not established, how can settled habitation be secured? Accordingly, the four classes of people are settled and the benefits of the land utilized in their proper seasons, bequeathing to all under Heaven the peace of stable dwelling [?]. For this reason, sacrifices occupy third place, and the Minister of Works comes next.
Thereafter, if people's original nature has not yet been restored, instruction is beneficial; hence the Minister of Education is appointed to oversee instruction. By spreading the constant norms and harmonizing the standards, he teaches the people once they have become prosperous. Thereafter, if some contravene that instruction, punishments are beneficial; hence the Minister of Justice is appointed to oversee punishments. By making penalties clear and enforcing the laws, he effectively guards against their transgressions of wickedness and violence. Do these two branches of government not occupy fifth and sixth places? Ritual propriety cannot be neglected, and there are relations to maintain; hence provision is made for guests, receiving them in audience…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
底法之訓而成端拱之休者咸與維新矣以統
萬民而萬民於是乎具瞻焉南面而治所以修
肯構之道而致垂衣之化者此為之所矣是其
堂之美也而豈徒哉吁君子是以知宣王之能
率祖攸行也昔者洛邑之成也而召公之告成
王必曰我受天命丕若有夏歷年式勿替有殷
歷年欲王以小民受天永命夫有周作大邑者
非棘其欲也固將以圖治而受命也然則宣王
之肯堂由繼先言之則子道盡矣由勤民言之
===
則君道盡矣其王業中興而祈天永命也宜哉
噫王可謂丕承先烈者矣
虎拜稽首天子萬年
胡鶴來
同考試官教諭陳批語和而莊召公報稱
之意溢於言外是深於詩者
同考試官教諭吳批詞意懇至體制謹嚴
足稱善頌矣
考試官教授蔣批忠愛之意藹然
punctuated:
底法之訓，而成端拱之休者，咸與維新矣。以統萬民，而萬民於是乎具瞻焉。南面而治，所以修肯構之道，而致垂衣之化者，此為之所矣。是其堂之美也，而豈徒哉！吁！君子是以知宣王之能率祖攸行也。昔者洛邑之成也，而召公之告成王，必曰：「我受天命，丕若有夏歷年，式勿替有殷歷年。」欲王以小民受天永命。夫有周作大邑者，非棘其欲也，固將以圖治而受命也。然則宣王之肯堂，由繼先言之，則子道盡矣；由勤民言之，則君道盡矣。其王業中興而祈天永命也，宜哉！噫！王可謂丕承先烈者矣。
虎拜稽首，天子萬年。
胡鶴來
同考試官教諭陳批：語和而莊，召公報稱之意溢於言外，是深於詩者。
同考試官教諭吳批：詞意懇至，體制謹嚴，足稱善頌矣。
考試官教授蔣批：忠愛之意藹然。
translation_en:
…all who follow the instruction to take this as their model [?] and bring about the blessings of governing with folded hands have joined in the renewal. Here he unites the myriad people, and here all the people look up to him. Facing south, he governs: this is the place where he pursues the way of completing his forebears’ construction and brings about the transforming influence of rule with robes hanging loosely. Such is the excellence of his hall—could it be merely ornamental? Ah! From this the gentleman knows that King Xuan could follow the course of his ancestors. When Luoyi was completed, the Duke of Shao, in admonishing King Cheng, made a point of saying: “Having received Heaven’s Mandate, may we fully equal the years of Xia and not fall short of the years of Yin.” He wished the king, through care for the common people, to receive Heaven’s enduring Mandate. When the Zhou built their great capital, it was not to pursue their desires urgently, but assuredly to seek good government and receive the Mandate. Thus King Xuan’s willingness to build the hall, considered as continuing his forebears’ work, fulfilled the way of a son; considered as diligent care for the people, it fulfilled the way of a ruler. How fitting that he should revive the royal enterprise and pray for Heaven’s enduring Mandate! Ah! The king may indeed be said to have magnificently carried forward his forebears’ achievements.

“Hu bowed and knocked his head to the ground: may the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years.”
Hu Helai

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “The language is harmonious yet dignified. The Duke of Shao’s intention to requite imperial favor overflows beyond the words. This is someone with a profound understanding of the Book of Odes.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “The wording and sentiments are deeply earnest, and the form is careful and rigorous. It well deserves to be called an accomplished eulogy.”

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: “The sentiment of loyalty and affection is warmly manifest.”

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授桂批〔疏鬯舂容〕
大臣拜命而欲壽其君以所感者深也夫壽君
之心固不待於有感大臣承寵命而祝之以萬
年也充其情之不能自已者乎昔者召虎經營
平僭亂於江漢天王錫祉隆寵命於岐周夫是
舉也圭瓚秬鬯之釐祀可崇其先祖而山川土
田之錫傳遂及之後人虎也覩王命之在前將
侈之爲不世之遇榮無以尙矣而敢不拜嘉乎
儼天顏於咫尺蓋持之以如臨之心禮不敢越
===
也於是而稽首焉人臣受恩無可以報謝者但
曰天子萬年而已矣蓋王者端拱於上惟以高
朗令終爲福而人臣願獻於君亦以永錫難老
爲忠其必天佑民而王躬是保所以出禮樂征
伐於天下者萬年歷有道之長而後帝嘏始純
也舍是若諸福之物則君之餘爾而又何加焉
天篤周而歷數爾常所以修田獵會同於諸侯
者四國仰無疆之慶而後臣心始愜也外此如
可致之祥皆足以供之而又何尙邪君念勳而
punctuated:
考試官敎授桂批〔疏鬯舂容〕

大臣拜命而欲壽其君，以所感者深也。夫壽君之心，固不待於有感；大臣承寵命而祝之以萬年也，充其情之不能自已者乎！昔者召虎經營，平僭亂於江漢；天王錫祉，隆寵命於岐周。夫是舉也，圭瓚秬鬯之釐祀，可崇其先祖；而山川土田之錫，傳遂及之後人。虎也覩王命之在前，將侈之爲不世之遇，榮無以尙矣，而敢不拜嘉乎？儼天顏於咫尺，蓋持之以如臨之心，禮不敢越也。於是而稽首焉。人臣受恩，無可以報謝者，但曰「天子萬年」而已矣。蓋王者端拱於上，惟以高朗令終爲福；而人臣願獻於君，亦以永錫難老爲忠。其必天佑民而王躬是保，所以出禮樂征伐於天下者，萬年歷有道之長，而後帝嘏始純也。舍是，若諸福之物，則君之餘爾，而又何加焉？天篤周而歷數爾常，所以修田獵會同於諸侯者，四國仰無疆之慶，而後臣心始愜也。外此，如可致之祥，皆足以供之，而又何尙邪？君念勳而
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Gui, Professor of Confucian Studies: 〔Lucid and fluent, measured and ample.〕

When a great minister bows in acceptance of a royal command and wishes his ruler long life, it is because he has been deeply moved. The wish that his ruler live long surely does not depend upon some occasion stirring his feelings. Yet when a great minister receives a gracious command and blesses his ruler with ten thousand years of life, is this not the fullest expression of feelings he cannot restrain?

Formerly, Shao Hu campaigned and quelled usurpation and disorder in the Jiang and Han region; the heavenly king bestowed blessings and conferred lavish honors at Qizhou. On this occasion, the sacrificial blessings associated with the jade-handled libation ladle and black-millet aromatic wine could bring honor to his ancestors, while the grants of mountains, rivers, and landed estates would pass down to his descendants. Seeing the royal command before him, Hu would exalt it as a distinction rarely encountered in any age, an honor beyond which there could be none. How could he dare not bow in gratitude for this favor? Reverently envisioning the royal countenance close at hand, he maintained the attitude of one standing in the king’s presence and dared not overstep ritual propriety. Thereupon he bowed his head to the ground. Having received such grace, a minister has nothing with which to repay it or express his thanks; he can only say, “May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years!”

The king sits above with hands reverently folded, regarding only a lofty, illustrious life and a good end as true blessings. Likewise, a minister wishing to offer something to his ruler takes loyalty to mean wishing him the lasting gift of freedom from old age. Heaven must aid the people and protect the king’s person, so that he who issues commands concerning rites, music, punitive expeditions, and warfare throughout the realm may enjoy ten thousand years of enduring rule in accordance with the Way. Only then will the blessing of the Lord on High be complete. Apart from this, the things counted as blessings are merely incidental to the ruler: what more could they add?

Heaven must deal generously with Zhou, and the allotted succession of your reigns must endure, so that, as the king conducts hunts and assemblies among the regional lords, the lands of the four quarters may look up to blessings without limit. Only then will the minister’s heart be satisfied. Beyond this, whatever auspicious things can be procured can all be supplied to him; what further value could they have? The ruler remembers meritorious service and…

title: 嘉靖三十七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
寵其臣臣受賜而祝其君上下交相愛也如此
周之治所以不可及歟抑因是而知穆公忠愛
之心無有已也夫萬年之壽惟一人之德可以
當之而萬年之治亦惟一人之德可以成之也
公之勸君也欲其令聞不已而洽四國以文德
焉其明保治之基乎夫其身本以武功獲懋賞
而保治永圖乃欲於文德取之豈謀身不及謀
國哉君子於是知古人愛君之心之無已也
春秋
===
秋九月齊侯宋公江人黃人盟于貫〔僖公二年〕
陳謨
同考試官教諭朱批經意專在服楚與國
見桓公伯業慮周義著不分對是
考試官教授蔣批得春秋予齊桓意
考試官教授桂批雅健
伯主服遠以孤外勢春秋特詞以予之也此貫
澤之盟齊桓服江黃以制楚也其慮周而義著
punctuated:
寵其臣，臣受賜而祝其君，上下交相愛也如此，周之治所以不可及歟！抑因是而知穆公忠愛之心無有已也。夫萬年之壽，惟一人之德可以當之；而萬年之治，亦惟一人之德可以成之也。公之勸君也，欲其令聞不已，而洽四國以文德焉，其明保治之基乎！夫其身本以武功獲懋賞，而保治永圖乃欲於文德取之，豈謀身不及謀國哉？君子於是知古人愛君之心之無已也。

春秋

秋九月，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人盟于貫。〔僖公二年〕

陳謨

同考試官教諭朱批：經意專在服楚與國，見桓公伯業慮周義著，不分對是。
考試官教授蔣批：得春秋予齊桓意。
考試官教授桂批：雅健。

伯主服遠以孤外勢，春秋特詞以予之也。此貫澤之盟，齊桓服江黃以制楚也，其慮周而義著
translation_en:
…bestows favor upon his ministers, and the ministers, receiving his gifts, pray for their ruler. Such was the mutual affection between those above and those below: was this not why Zhou’s governance was beyond compare? From this, moreover, we know that Duke Mu’s loyal affection knew no end. Only the virtue of the One Man can merit a lifespan of ten thousand years; likewise, only the virtue of the One Man can bring about ten thousand years of good government. In exhorting his ruler, the duke wished his good reputation to endure without cease and his civil virtue to pervade the states in all four quarters. Did he not clearly understand the foundation for preserving good government? He himself had originally won lavish rewards through military achievements, yet for the enduring preservation of good government he sought recourse to civil virtue.
